articleTitle: Research on the emergence mechanism of group leaders
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The phenomenon of leader emergence is typically defined as a cognitive process of leadership that occurs within a general biological group. This process is indicative of the interactions between groups and individuals within those groups. Therefore, it is important to study the mechanisms of the leader emergence for the formation of leadership, the understanding of group behavior and the research of groups complex systems. Based on the charge force model, the leader emergence is described, in this paper, in terms of a time-varying hybrid potential energy function with uncertain parameters. Based on this potential energy function, the formation process of leaders is analyzed and modeled. This process involves individuals within the group perceiving and recognizing the emergence of leaders through interaction. Computer simulations are performed to illustrate and verify the mechanism and validity of the models. This model not only solves the problem of target generation and target selection of swarm robots, but also simulates the behavior process of self-organization.

articleTitle: Endoscopic Path Planning in Robot-Assisted Ear Surgery Based on Improved A-Star Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Preoperative planning is crucial in transcanal endoscopic ear surgery (TEES), especially with the increasing advancement of robot-assisted surgical systems. However, current preoperative path planning largely relies on the surgeon's experience. To address this, a preoperative path planning method based on an improved A* algorithm is proposed in this paper. First, an optimized search space method is introduced by accounting for the endoscope’s size and dimensions. Second, turning constraints are incorporated into the cost function to ensure that the planned path meets surgical requirements. Finally, a cubic B-spline is employed to smooth the curve, generating a safe surgical path from the ear entry point to the target surgical area. Simulation results demonstrate that the improved A* algorithm can efficiently find a feasible path in a short time, effectively keeping the planned path away from obstacles while reducing path length and the number of turns, thereby enhancing the safety and stability of robot operation in TEES.

articleTitle: MixDACM and WMF-DAWHampel-Based FMCW Radar for Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the field of life sign detection, the use of 77GHz Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) millimeterwave radar is being explored for non-contact monitoring of vital signs. This technology is challenged by interference from respiratory harmonics and clutter, which can result in abnormal phase values. An advanced algorithm for FMCW radar life sign signal detection is introduced in this study, combining first-order and second-order Difference of Arbitrary-Constant Multiplication (MixDACM) for phase unwrapping with a Windowed Median Filter-based Adaptive Weighted Hampel (WMFDAWHampel) method for managing outliers. The methodology involves utilizing the intermediate frequency signal from the FMCW radar to locate the target accurately. Subsequently, the MixDACM technique is applied for phase unwrapping, followed by the WMF-DAWHampel filter to address any residual abnormal phase values. Band-pass filters are then used to isolate the respiratory and heartbeat signals, facilitating the estimation of breathing and heart rates. Experimental results indicate that the integration of MixDACM and WMF-DAWHampel methods significantly improves phase unwrapping quality and outlier management. The integration of advanced signal processing techniques results in precise respiratory and heartbeat signal extraction, achieving estimation errors of 8.810% and 3.325%, respectively. Results from the study affirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in boosting the precision of life sign detection through FMCW radar technology.

articleTitle: Research on the Recognition of ECG Signals based on Integrated LSTM-GRU Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence technology to achieve automatic diagnosis of ECG signals is an inevitable trend in future technological development. This design targets the nonstationarity and individual variability of ECG signals, proposing an integrated model of Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) for heart rate signal recognition. Wavelet scattering transform is employed to extract the time-frequency features of ECG signals, thereby improving the model's convergence speed and recognition accuracy. The experiment uses the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, which includes five categories of ECG signal data: N, A, V, L and R. Test results show that the integrated LSTM-GRU network outperforms traditional LSTM networks in both training speed and recognition accuracy, with an accuracy rate as high as 98.7%, which is of great significance for the future development of automatic ECG signal diagnosis technology.

articleTitle: 3D Information Perception of Earthworks Based on Machine Vision and LiDAR Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The environment at earthwork construction sites is complex, which severely restricts the development of autonomous operation of intelligent construction machinery. To address this issue, a perception method based on the fusion of machine vision and LiDAR is proposed for sensing earthwork information at construction sites. By leveraging the rich semantic information in camera images and the accurate three-dimensional information in LiDAR point clouds, earthwork targets in the images are extracted using the Mask R-CNN instance segmentation network model. Then, the three-dimensional point clouds from the LiDAR are projected onto the two-dimensional image to extract earthwork color point clouds, achieving the fusion perception of earthwork information. Experimental results indicate that this method enables efficient fusion of earthwork image data and point cloud data, achieving extraction of earthwork operation targets and three-dimensional information perception.

articleTitle: A Spectral Clustering Algorithm for Similar Matrix Reconstruction based on Adaptive Neighborhood Standard Deviation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In view of the shortcomings of the classical spectral clustering algorithm in the artificial setting of scale parameters and the accuracy of the similar matrix construction, which leads to the low accuracy of the clustering results, a similar matrix reconstruction spectral clustering algorithm based on adaptive neighborhood standard deviation is proposed. The algorithm uses the inverse of the sample neighborhood standard deviation as a parameter to measure the local density of the sample. It constructs an adaptive scale parameter by incorporating a multi-region density adjustment strategy. Additionally, a nonlinear Sigmoid function is introduced to design the scale difference adjustment term, and the similarity matrix is reconstructed by integrating global density. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves good clustering performance on both synthetic datasets and real UCI datasets, with more stable clustering results.

articleTitle: Four-Degree Digital Twin Robotic Arm in Webots Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper offers a process for creating a low-cost digital twin, the 4 Degrees of Freedom (DOF) robotic arm specially made for the Webots environment. Conventional methods of controlling robotic arms frequently depend on pricey hardware and exclusive software, which restricts their adaptability and accessibility. We suggest a method that uses the Robot Operating System (ROS) for communication to combine the Webots simulation platform with MATLAB to solve this. Evaluating the suggested system's performance involved running eight, square, and circular trajectories. The Circle-Shaped trajectory, using a Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller, performed better than the Eight-Shaped and Square-Shaped trajectories of 6.46e-5, 2.46e-3 and 1.34e-2, respectively. These findings imply that the suggested digital twin configuration offers a practical, affordable substitute for robotics applications.

articleTitle: Collaborative search and tracking based on dynamic map and information fusion for UAV swarm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To improve the accuracy and stability of multi-target tracking tasks for UAV swarm, a UAV scheduling method based on multi-agent reinforcement learning is proposed. In the proposed method, a multi-agent actor-critic with attention (MAAC) algorithm is proposed, which is used to optimize scheduling strategies effectively. By incorporating dynamic mapping and information fusion mechanisms, the UAV swarm can continuously update target histories, environmental search statuses, and UAV positions, to better perceive and adapt to the environment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods in tracking accuracy, response delay, and collision rate, especially in dynamic and communication-limited environments.

articleTitle: Discriminant Neighborhood Preserving Embedding with Autoencoder for fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the development of modern industry, fault diagnosis has become a hot research area. The Discriminant Neighborhood Preserving Embedding (DNPE) algorithm has demonstrated excellent performance in handling complex industrial data. However, DNPE only preserves the local structure and discriminative information after dimensionality reduction, without the ability to recover the low-dimensional embedded data back to its original form. This lack of recovery capability may lead to the loss of important information in the data. Inspired by the reconstruction mechanism of autoencoders, a new NPE algorithm, DNPE-AE (Discriminant Neighborhood Preserving Embedding with Autoencoder), is proposed. Experiments on the bearing fault dataset provided by Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), show that DNPE-AE outperforms other methods in fault recognition and classification.

articleTitle: Research on Collision Detection Method Based on Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Research the collision detection problem during equipment operation. Collect data on collisions occurring at different positions during normal operation and operation of the equipment, process the signals using wavelet transform, extract feature indicators such as kurtosis for analysis, and finally use Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification method to distinguish collisions and their specific locations. The research results show that using the One-Versus-Rest (OVR) classification method with a lifting table as the experimental object, the accuracy of the data reaches 96.11%, the classification time is 0.021, and it has high detection and discrimination rates. Moreover, this method can effectively detect collisions during equipment operation based on the collected data and determine the specific location of the collision.

articleTitle: Ground Station Software Design Based on Human Machine Hybrid Intelligence: A Command and Control Application of Human in the Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Ground station software plays a crucial role in the intelligent development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) across various countries. This work analyzes the current shortcomings of ground station software in supporting UAV missions. In response, a command-and-control system for ground station software, based on human-machine hybrid intelligence, is proposed. The system design includes multiple aspects such as human-machine modeling, human-machine interface design, and human-machine data sharing. These aspects cover task deployment, task monitoring, and task analysis. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed ground station software, a simulation testing environment integrated with Docker containers is constructed to package and isolate UAV control software. This setup is used to test the collaborative operation of hundreds of UAVs and the control by commanders. Experimental results demonstrate that the application achieves effective coordination, high command capabilities, and stable operation, making it a significant advancement in enhancing the intelligence and efficiency of UAV swarm tasks.

articleTitle: Path planning of warehouse UAV automatic inventory under multi-objective constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the increasing application of UAVs in intelligent warehouses, how to solve the problem of path planning in complex environments, especially multi-objective path planning and obstacle avoidance, has become a key challenge. In this paper, A 3D path planning method based on A* algorithm and B spline curve is proposed to optimize the automatic inventory path of UAVs. Firstly, the traditional path planning algorithm is optimized by introducing Angle cost to reduce unnecessary turns and improve flight stability and energy efficiency. Secondly, a multi-objective path optimization strategy is proposed to ensure the shortest path and reduce inventory time and energy consumption by automatically adjusting the order of target points. At the same time, B-spline curve is used to smooth the path, eliminate sharp turns, and improve flight smoothness. The experimental results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method in complex three-dimensional environment, which can avoid obstacles, optimize paths, and achieve higher inventory efficiency in multi-objective point planning, and has strong practical application value.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Random Scenario Prediction Based on Time Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Due to the randomness and time correlation of photovoltaic (PV) power output, the PV data obtained by conventional short-term point or interval prediction methods cannot support the robust scheduling and reliable operation of the power system under the condition of high proportion of PV integration. A photovoltaic random scenario prediction model based on Time - generative adversarial network (TimeGAN) is proposed. Firstly, the photovoltaic samples are decomposed into static and time-series data, and the network structures of embedding, reconstruction, generation and discrimination are constructed. Secondly, taking the static and time-series data as samples, the embedding and reconstruction networks are jointly trained. Finally, taking the output of the embedding network as samples, the generation and discrimination networks are trained adversarially, and the output of the generation network is fed back to the embedding-reconstruction training to test the fitting effect of the time series. Aiming to minimize the reconstruction, supervised and unsupervised losses, the model conducts in-depth learning of the photovoltaic time characteristics and predicts random scenarios. The validity of the proposed model is verified by the example calculation.

articleTitle: Video Tracking and Auxiliary Obstacle Avoidance of Power Plant Inspection Robot based on Deep Learning and 3D Digital Twin System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The highly intricate landscape of power plant equipment and personnel demands sophisticated solutions, rendering robot-based automation control and the digitalization of production information indispensable for the realization of plant intelligence and smart operational paradigms. Traditional inspection robots, despite their proficiency in gathering information and executing predefined tasks, confront substantial hurdles in terms of adaptability and robustness within the confines of complex environments. The limitations of onboard sensors, such as the narrow fields of view offered by chassis-mounted devices and head-mounted cameras, result in the creation of numerous blind spots that make the robots vulnerable to collisions. Additionally, these robots are frequently perceived as standalone entities, rather than as integral components of the intricate power plant ecosystem. In response to these challenges, this article introduces an innovative control method that leverages the refined Unicorn video tracking algorithm. This algorithm provides real-time tracking, obstacle warnings, and collision pre-alerts for inspection robots in edge cases and unforeseen situations, thereby significantly enhancing their adaptability and preprocessing capabilities in complex environments. Furthermore, the process of collecting and annotating virtual datasets has been greatly simplified through the utilization of a 3D digital twin system, which facilitates the preparation of training datasets with minimal effort.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Vehicle Steering Column Pattern Image Based on K-Net Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As an important assembly part of the automobile, the steering column module is mainly used to control the turn signal and the wiper switch. Therefore, it is necessary to check the integrity of its printed beacon pattern. However, the image quality of the traditional image processing vision system is easily affected by the field environment, and due to the existence of a large number of reflection areas in the image, the image segmentation is low precision, low adaptability and high error rate. Therefore, this paper uses K-Net deep learning network semantic segmentation model to automatically remove image reflection. By using Swin-T backbone network and introducing self-attention mechanism, the segmentation performance of beacon is further improved, and the anti-reflective binary segmentation of beacon is realized. Finally, the superiority of the above model is verified in the production line data set of enterprise steering column products. The experimental results show that: (1) K-Net network has a good segmentation effect, and its mIoU reaches 95.77%; (2) After using the Swin-T backbone network, the mIoU of K-Net model increased by 1.1% compared with the traditional CNN backbone network.

articleTitle: Adapting LLMs for Ballistocardiographic Signals: A Multi-Task Learning Framework for BCG to ECG Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Ballistocardiography (BCG) offers a non-invasive method for continuous cardiac monitoring, yet its weak and noisy signals pose challenges for accurate heart rate (HR) estimation. We propose a novel multi-task learning framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to reconstruct electrocardiography (ECG) signals from BCG inputs, with auxiliary tasks of heart rate prediction and heart rate anomaly detection aimed at enhancing reconstruction accuracy. Utilizing a Transformer-based architecture, our model captures both local and global features of BCG signals, facilitating precise ECG waveform reconstruction. The multi-task approach enhances performance through shared representations across tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.927 for ECG reconstruction and a relative Root Mean Square Error (rRMSE) of 0.113 for heart rate prediction, outperforming single-task models. Our primary contribution lies in adapting pre-trained LLMs to BCG signals, achieving significant advancements in modality alignment and multimodal fusion. This work substantially improves the accuracy of ECG signal reconstruction from BCG inputs, providing a robust solution for continuous and non-invasive cardiovascular health monitoring.

articleTitle: TCN-BiGRU: A Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Enhanced Temperature Time Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that combines a temporal convolutional network (TCN) with a bidirectional gated recursive unit (BiGRU), aiming to improve the accuracy of temperature prediction. The model effectively addresses the challenges of complexity, non-stationarity, and high volatility in temperature time series prediction. TCN can capture long-term temporal dependencies through its scalable convolutional structure, thereby identifying complex patterns and periodic changes in data, BiGRU enhances adaptability to the dynamics and unpredictability of meteorological phenomena by fully considering historical and future influences. Through the synergistic effect of TCN and BiGRU, the proposed model exhibits stronger multi-scale feature extraction capability and complex temporal relationship modeling ability in temperature prediction and can better handle nonlinear dynamics and long time-dependence problems compared with the traditional methods. The experimental results show that the hybrid model can provide better prediction performance than the traditional methods in a wide range of geographic regions and climatic conditions, with strong noise immunity and adaptability to extreme weather events. This study provides an effective technical framework for deep learning applications in climate science, which is of great theoretical significance and application value in the fields of environmental monitoring, energy management and climate change response.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Vehicle Regulation Algorithm Based on Driving Intent Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this paper, a multimodal fusion driver intention prediction system is proposed based on the driver lane change intention reasoning framework. The system utilizes the improved Attention-BiLSTM neural network model for intention prediction by analyzing the driver's behavior, traffic environment and vehicle physical state. By preprocessing and analyzing the data from the Brain4cars database, the driver's head pose and driving scene features are extracted, thus providing rich input information for the model. The experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper achieves more than 92% accuracy in recognizing the driver's intention to change lanes, which is significantly better than the traditional support vector machine and LSTM models. This research provides the theoretical foundation and technical support for the realization of intelligent driver assistance systems, and has important application prospects.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Electromagnetic Absorbers Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network approach for the design and optimization of electromagnetic absorbers operating in the 20-30 GHz frequency range. This method offers significant advantages in terms of miniaturization and wide bandwidth. By training the MLP neural network, the absorber structure is automatically optimized within this frequency band. The predicted results are in strong agreement with full-wave simulation outcomes. The findings demonstrate that this approach effectively enhances absorber efficiency, providing a novel solution for electromagnetic compatibility and stealth technology applications.

articleTitle: Prediction model of influencing factors of quality of life in middle-aged and elderly patients with chronic diseases based on machine learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To predict the model of influencing factors of the quality of life of patients with chronic diseases in China, which is beneficial to improve the quality of life of patients with chronic diseases, and to formulate effective intervention measures for them. Methods: According to the data of China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) in 2020, 1187 subjects who met the research criteria were screened by lasso algorithm, and five machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, decision tree, naive Bayes) were evaluated. In order to select the best model to predict the influencing factors. Results: The lasso algorithm screened 24 possible related variables to determine 7 variables, compared the performance of five different machine learning models on the test set, and the results showed that the logical regression model performed better. Conclusion: Logistic regression in the prediction model based on machine learning can accurately obtain the influencing factors of the quality of life of patients with chronic diseases, and provide the basis for the follow-up research.

articleTitle: Terminal sliding mode control of acupuncture robot based on RBF neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To solve the problem of trajectory tracking control when the acupuncture robot performs treatments, a terminal sliding mode controller which is based on RBF neural network was designed. Firstly, the acupuncture robot treatment system was established. Then, the dynamic model of the acupuncture robot was developed based on Lagrange equations. Next, the control strategy which is used in the trajectory tracking of the acupuncture robot was proposed. In this control scheme, with the introduction of non-singular fast terminal sliding mode function, the issue of singular value was avoided, and the unmodeled characteristics and external disturbances of the acupuncture robot by using RBF neural network. Additionally, according to the Lyapunov theory, it is proved that the designed controller is stable. Finally, by means of visual simulation and the comparative analysis, it shows that the designed controller has faster convergence speed, higher control accuracy and better anti-jamming performance.

articleTitle: Radar Phrase Extraction Based on Deep Convolutional Conditional Random Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Extracting radar phrases from multifunctional radar pulse sequences and identifying the internal operation law and working mechanism among the working modes is the foundation for subsequent working mode prediction. However, most existing studies at the syntactic level fail to address the full range of issues, focusing only on radar word extraction and working pattern recognition. In this paper, we propose an improved CNN-BiLSTM-CRF model for radar phrase extraction. It is based on the BiLSTM network model, which is able to extract richer local features using convolutional neural networks. The model is simulated on generated radar pulse word sequences, and the results show that the CNN-BiLSTM-CRF model improves the F-value of radar phrase extraction by 2.688% on the test set compared with the BiLSTM-CRF model. The simulation results prove that the improved method is effective.

articleTitle: Small Sample Wireless Technology Identification Enhanced by Cyclic Shift and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Small sample wireless technology identification has significant application value in complex electromagnetic environments. However, the generalization ability and recognition accuracy of models are often limited due to insufficient data. This paper proposes a small sample wireless technology identification method enhanced by cyclic shift and attention mechanism. The method is applied to a six-class classification task involving CV2X, Five_G, ITSG5, LTE, Noise, and WiFi signal categories. By incorporating cyclic shift data augmentation during the training phase, the model's robustness to time-series data is improved. Meanwhile, the SE attention mechanism is employed to optimize the feature space and strengthen the representation of key features. Experiments were conducted with different sample sizes (100, 200, 300, 400, 500), comparing the testing accuracy, confusion matrices, and feature distributions of the models before and after optimization. Results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances the classification performance of the model under small sample conditions. Compared to the initial model, the optimized model achieves higher testing accuracy across all sample sizes, with more concentrated feature distributions and markedly improved category separability. Furthermore, confusion matrices reveal that the optimized model shows a particularly notable improvement in classifying small sample categories, with a significant reduction in misclassification rates. This method provides an efficient solution to the challenges of small sample wireless technology identification.

articleTitle: Embodied Intelligence Applications in Assistive Technologies for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Embodied Intelligence (EI) in assistive technologies for the visually impaired (BLV) population. The study examines the challenges faced by BLV individuals, including mobility, information access, and social interaction, while identifying the limitations of existing assistive devices. A theoretical framework is proposed, integrating EI's core components—perception, decision-making, and action execution—to deliver adaptive and personalized solutions. To validate the framework, an experimental study was conducted using an EI prototype. Participants, including those with complete and partial blindness, were observed over 60 days, with data collected both before and after using the prototype. Results, analyzed through the Visual Functioning Subscale (VFS), demonstrated significant improvements in navigation, safety, and social engagement. This research highlights the transformative potential of EI in enhancing the independence and quality of life of BLV individuals while addressing critical ethical and societal considerations for its implementation.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of CIoU and CNN Joint Compression in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid development and application of autonomous driving technology, vehicle computing devices are facing increasingly daunting challenges. These systems need to process a large amount of sensory data in real-time, plan routes, and make decisions, which requires more computational resources. Therefore, effective model compression methods have become crucial. Our study aims to reduce the size and computational complexity of models through weight pruning and convolutional split compression methods, thereby reducing the consumption of computational resources while maintaining model performance and accuracy. We also utilize the CIoU loss function to improve the accuracy and efficiency of obstacle detection in autonomous driving systems. In simulated experiments, we tested and evaluated the improved model using a dataset of simulated road scenarios. The results of the experiments validate the effectiveness of model compression and demonstrate the advantages of the improved model in increasing obstacle detection rates and reducing computational costs. These improvements can help autonomous driving systems operate efficiently with limited computational resources, thereby enhancing system reliability and practicality. Our research provides valuable theoretical and practical support for advancing autonomous driving technology.

articleTitle: Dynamic scheduling method of computing resources in Internet of Vehicles based on an improved NSGAII algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) represents a critical component of modern mobile edge computing systems. IoV computing resources encompass backend cloud resources, roadside edge nodes, and vehicle-mounted units. Traditional static scheduling methods struggle to meet the real-time performance and resource utilization demands imposed by the IoV's dynamic and heterogeneous environment. This study introduces a dynamic scheduling approach for IoV computing resources leveraging an enhanced Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to address multi-objective optimization challenges in resource allocation. First, the study develops a multi-objective optimization model that integrates key performance metrics, including task delay, energy consumption, and resource utilization. Subsequently, an improved NSGA-II framework incorporating adaptive encoding, selection, crossover, and mutation strategies is formulated to enhance the algorithm's global optimization capabilities in dynamic IoV scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches in multi-objective optimization efficacy, convergence rate, and algorithmic stability, offering an efficient solution for managing IoV computing resources.

articleTitle: Intelligent Pursuit and Evasion Decision-Making in Active Defense Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the complex environment of modern aerial warfare, an attacking missile attempts to successfully penetrate defenses and strike a target aircraft, while a defensive missile intercepts the attacking missile to protect the target. Meanwhile, the target aircraft itself possesses intelligent evasion capabilities, employing smart maneuvering strategies to evade the attacking missile's pursuit. In this triadic confrontation within an active defense scenario, intelligent strategy decisions of all participating agents are critical to the outcome of the engagement. In the dynamically evolving battlefield, improving the penetration capability of the attacking missile, enhancing the coordination of multi-agent decision-making, and strengthening the evasion capability of the target aircraft are key challenges. To address these challenges, the objective of this study is to enhance the attacking missile's penetration ability in an active defense scenario, particularly in the presence of interference from a defensive missile, while also improving the coordination and collaborative effectiveness of multiple agents. Therefore, this work proposes an improved Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm that incorporates a Transformer Encoder. By introducing the Transformer Encoder, the algorithm's representation capacity and decision-making precision are significantly enhanced, addressing the limitations of traditional MAPPO in processing complex environmental information, penetrating defensive missiles, and generating intelligent evasion strategies for the target aircraft.

articleTitle: Intelligent Recognition and Control System for Flexible Robotic Hands Based on Multi-channel Tactile Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the development of intelligent manufacturing and robotic technology, flexible robotic hands have demonstrated substantial application potential in fields such as industrial automation and medical devices due to their flexibility and adaptability. However, traditional visual recognition methods have limitations in acquiring mechanical properties of objects, such as hardness and texture, which makes it difficult to achieve accurate recognition under complex environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-channel tactile sensing system based on the STM32F1 microcontroller, aiming to endow the flexible robotic hand with efficient object recognition and grasp control capabilities. The system integrates multiple thin-film pressure sensors, with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) employed to process the pressure data in multiple channels, extracting tactile features layer by layer and analyzing the dynamic mechanical information during the grasping process. Experimental results indicate that the designed system achieves an accuracy of 97.9% in the classification tasks involving objects with various hardness levels, verifying the robustness and accuracy of the system in identifying diverse objects.

articleTitle: Research on automatic identification and detection of plug seedlings based on machine vision
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the process of plug seedling, there will be the problem of missing sowing and bad seedlings. At this stage, the method of artificial removal is generally adopted. In the process of research on automatic seedling equipment, visual inspection is a key part of the whole process. This paper takes lettuce seedlings as the research object, establishes a data set, and analyzes its characteristics. The seedling visual recognition system based on YOLOv10 algorithm framework was used to establish an automatic recognition and detection model for plug seedlings. After testing, the model can accurately identify the position of reseeding seedlings, and finally summarized.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Generative Adversarial Network for 3D Point Cloud Upsampling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: We present an enhanced generative adversarial network for 3D point cloud upsampling (PU-EGAN). The Residual Dense Feature Extractor (RDFE) improves the network’s ability to capture subtle features and enhance feature representation. It achieves this by combining residual concatenation with dense feature propagation. To further improve the reconstruction of point cloud details and textures, we propose Point Attention Coordinate Reconstruction (PACR). PACR focuses on generating more detailed points by calculating point attention weights using the newly introduced Point Attention (PA) mechanism. Both objective and subjective evaluations demonstrate that PU-EGAN outperforms existing methods.

articleTitle: Design of an Arc-Wheel Robot Based on ROS System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces the design and development of the Arc-Wheel robot, a ROS-based platform tailored for exploration and operational tasks in multi-terrain environments. The robot incorporates a novel arc-wheel design, an adaptable suspension system, and a modular chassis structure <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, collectively enhancing terrain adaptability, obstacle-crossing capabilities, and hardware reconfigurability. The ESP32S3 microcontroller serves as the system's core processor, enabling seamless communication and real-time control within the ROS framework <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[2]</sup>. Experimental results, including evaluations on grass, steep slopes, and rocky surfaces <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>, highlight the robot's exceptional stability and locomotion performance under complex conditions. These findings demonstrate the system's potential for deployment in exploration and rescue missions, contributing a robust and scalable solution to the challenges of multi-terrain robotics.

articleTitle: Lightweight Automatic Modulation Classification Method Using Filter Pruning via Geometric Median
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is a technique employed to determine the modulation type of signals in non-cooperative communication systems. It is crucial in military and civilian communications, offering significant potential for various applications. Recently, AMC methods based on deep learning (DL) are known for their outstanding performance. However, the high computational cost and large model size of DL-based AMC methods limit their application in edge Internet of Things (IoT) systems. Hence, this paper proposes a lightweight AMC method based on filter pruning via geometric median (FPGM). Specifically, we start by determining the geometric median of the filters in each layer, which effectively represents the filter distribution within that layer. Then, filters near the geometric median are identified and filtered out through the characteristics of the geometric median. Finally, the performance degradation of the model caused by the removal of filters can be restored through fine-tuning. Our experimental findings suggest that the proposed FPGM-based AMC method reduces the model size by 99%. At the same time, the classification accuracy is degraded by approximately 1.61%, which significantly outperforms other lightweight AMC methods.

articleTitle: Development of an Underwater Anticorrosion Coating Maintenance Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The maintenance of anti-corrosion coatings on underwater steel structures is crucial for ensuring their structural integrity and extending service life. However, current manual maintenance methods are labor-intensive, costly, and risky, highlighting the necessity of developing underwater robots to achieve efficient and automated maintenance. To achieve automated underwater surface coating maintenance, this study designed an underwater coating robot. Based on analysis of underwater coating maintenance procedure and environmental factors, the overall robot components are designed, including adhering and moving chassis, surface preparation tool, coating applying tool and water clearing tool. On the basis of robot design, experiments and computer simulation were conducted to verify the grinding and coating capability of the coating maintenance robot. Experimental results indicate that the proposed robot is capable of underwater coating repair tasks.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Evaluation and Optimization Methods in Electric Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study presents a reinforcement learning-based framework for optimizing energy efficiency in electric vehicle (EV) and grid interactions. Managing grid load, especially during peak charging times, becomes critical as EV adoption increases. The framework leverages short-term load forecasting with data from the Electricity Load Forecasting dataset to dynamically balance energy distribution. Experimental results show a 131.5% reduction in Peak-to-Average Load Ratio (PALR) with a GRU model, a 97.53% improvement in Charging Efficiency Index (CEI) with a CNN-LSTM model, and a lower RMSE, demonstrating the framework’s effectiveness in enhancing grid integration and EV charging efficiency.

articleTitle: Scene Text Detection using Hyperbolic Tangent Binarization and CLIP
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Deep learning-based scene text detection has advanced significantly and has promising application prospects. The binarization of hyperbolic tangent network plus (HTBNet++) is designed to solve the problem of missing small text and dense text in scene images. By designing the backbone network based on CLIP, pretrained text and image features were introduced to achieve better feature extraction. At the same time, text and image prompts play a key role in feature fusion so that the features of text and image pairs can be better applied to text detection. In addition, an auxiliary segmentation loss was designed to guide the network to better perform reverse gradient propagation during the training process. Experimental results on Total-Text and TD500 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances text detection accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: A gene regulatory network method based on single-cell multi-omics data
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The interactions between chromatin, transcri-ption factors, and genes give rise to complex regulatory circuits that can be represented as gene regulatory networks (GRNs). To date, many methods have been proposed for constructing regulatory networks based on scRNA-seq data, which map GRNs using single-cell transcriptomics data. Here, we introduce single-cell epigenomic ATAC-seq data to construct more accurate GRNs from multi-omics perspective. We constructed the GRN in mouse hematopoietic cells, using mouse peripheral blood ATAC-seq data to establish benchmark GRNs to infer the GRN of specific clusters. Finally, we conducted network analysis on the constructed GRNs.

articleTitle: Modal Invariant Joint Representation Learning for Missing Multimodal Ship Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Multimodal image classification and recognition of ships can help to develop the field of intelligent traffic on ships.However, a portion of modalities is sometimes missing in specific ship identification, which can lead to the failure of traditional multimodal approaches. In order to address this problem, the current state-of-the-art approach for missing modality correlation is to directly map the available modality-specific features into a space with the aim of extracting shared potential representations that are robust to all modal combinations.In this paper, a Modality-Invariant Joint Representation Learning (MIJR) is proposed, where robust features are first extracted by Modality-Invariant Feature Learning (MIFL), and then the modal information available in the missing case is fully explored by the Transformer-related Feature Extraction Module and Modal Weight Fusion Module. This enables the performance to be maintained even when a portion of the modal data is missing. Our proposed method achieves an accuracy of 88.13% even when 30% of the public VAIS dataset is missing.

articleTitle: Multi class sea surface target dataset for autonomous navigation of ships
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This article proposes a sea surface target dataset for autonomous navigation of ships, which includes 2290 basic images and 4 classifications. Selecting the optimal model for training and using the mesoscale experimental ship Chuangzhi for validation, the model accuracy reached 89.12%, the recall rate reached 80.28%, and the comprehensive index F1 score was 84%. The actual ship test has shown that the self built dataset has an average confidence increase of about 17% compared to the traditional COCO dataset, and is significantly better than the COCO dataset when facing multiple targets, small targets, and long-distance scenarios. This dataset can effectively improve the detection comprehensiveness, accuracy, and robustness of the model in actual sea surface scenarios, providing important support for the development of autonomous navigation technology for ships.

articleTitle: Design and Application of a Multi-task Legal Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the challenges of automating complex tasks in the legal domain, this paper presents Law-Qwen, a multi-task legal large language model based on Qwen7B-Chat. By applying Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning, the model significantly reduces the volume of parameter updates, while combining self-construction and instruction augmentation strategies enables Law-Qwen to efficiently perform tasks such as legal consultation, case classification, and judgment prediction. In the LawBench benchmark test, Law-Qwen achieved a score of 0.492 in the legal QA task, surpassing the second-highest model, LexiLaw, by 22.4%. The total score across all tasks reached 7.517, the highest among the five models evaluated, fully demonstrating Law-Qwen’s multi-task processing advantage. This advancement provides strong technical support for enhancing the capabilities of legal large models in complex tasks, promoting the application prospects of intelligent legal solutions in judicial scenarios.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Harris Hawks Optimization Algorithm for GRU Hyperparameter Tuning: Application to Mooring System Tension Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The accuracy of tension prediction for mooring systems affects the safety and efficiency of production planning for offshore platforms as well as ship systems. With the development of deep learning, tension prediction based on neural networks has been widely used and has shown excellent performance. However, the performance of neural networks depends largely on the setting of hyper-parameters, and frequent manual adjustments of hyper-parameters are required in use to obtain the best neural network performance results, which is undoubtedly time-consuming and affects the performance of the task at the same time. To address this problem, this paper proposes a Harris-Hawkes optimization algorithm (ADLS-HHO) based on an adaptive two-layer search strategy and an improved Levy flight mechanism to automatically optimize the GRU hyperparameters. Specifically, ADLS-HHO employs an adaptive two-layer search framework to enhance the dynamic balance between exploitation and exploration, and Levy flights to enhance the global exploration capability while guiding the local search strategy through a dynamically maintained memory pool. Experimental results show that the prediction accuracy of the proposed ADLS-HHO-GRU model is better than that of the conventional model, and in addition, the number of convergence iterations required by ADLS-HHO-GRU is less than that of the existing classical algorithms. These results indicate that ADLS-HHO-GRU provides an effective method while maintaining computational efficiency.

articleTitle: The Brain-Inspired Cooperative Shared Control Framework for Brain-Machine Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In brain-machine interface (BMI) applications, a key challenge is the low information content and high noise level in neural signals, severely affecting stable robotic control. To address this challenge, we proposes a cooperative shared control framework based on brain-inspired intelligence, where control signals are decoded from neural activity, and the robot handles the fine control. This allows for a combination of flexible and adaptive interaction control between the robot and the brain, making intricate human-robot collaboration feasible. The proposed framework utilizes spiking neural networks (SNNs) for controlling robotic arm and wheel, including speed and steering. While full integration of the system remains a future goal, individual modules for robotic arm control, object tracking, and map generation have been successfully implemented. The framework is expected to significantly enhance the performance of BMI. In practical settings, the BMI with cooperative shared control, utilizing a brain-inspired algorithm, will greatly enhance the potential for clinical applications.

articleTitle: Tree Climbing Robot Utilizing FreeRTOS Real-Time Operating System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This thesis proposes an intelligent tree climbing robot designed to save tree trimming and human resources. The robot adopts a dual-loop PID algorithm to realize the closed-loop control of motors, which ensures precise movement and efficient tree climbing. In addition, based on FreeRTOS real-time sensor data processing and analysis, the robot is able to respond quickly to environmental changes, thus ensuring safe and stable operation in complex environments. Its bionic clamping mechanism combines spring and control system to realize stable clamping on the tree trunk and enhance the safety of operation. At the same time, the robot is equipped with a grasping hook device and a rope system, which can safely grasp and fix the leaves, further improving operational efficiency and personnel safety.

articleTitle: Intelligent Obstacle Avoidance and Path Planning for Unmanned Vessels Based on an Improved Bug2 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, the demand for intelligence in unmanned vessels is becoming increasingly prominent. One of the core problems in the process of automatic navigation of unmanned vessels is how to make effective collision avoidance decisions in time. In this paper, an improved Bug2 algorithm is proposed, which introduces angle determination and bypassing strategy in the traditional Bug2 algorithm, effectively solves the deficiencies of the conventional Bug2 algorithm in the fixed obstacle avoidance direction and timing of the movement, and significantly improves the dynamic obstacle avoidance performance of the algorithm. The dynamic obstacle simulation test verifies that the algorithm has high real-time and strong path planning ability. After that, the unmanned boat control system is designed, and in the physical test on the lake, the unmanned boat can rely on the improved Bug2 algorithm to plan the obstacle avoidance path in time when encountering obstacles, realizing the autonomous obstacle avoidance, which provides solid technical support for intelligent navigation in the complex sea area.

articleTitle: An Intrusion Detection Method Combining Coarse and Fine Classification for Industrial Internet
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the popularization of applications, the industrial internet is facing increasingly serious security threats. In the complex data scenario of the industrial internet, machine learning algorithms are difficult to adapt to the problems of massive imbalanced data and low detection time efficiency. An intrusion detection method combining coarse and fine classification is proposed in this paper. Firstly, all samples are roughly classified into benign data or attack data using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). Secondly, Variational Auto-Encoder is used to balance the training samples of attack data, and the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator is used to optimize the parameters of LightGBM. Finally, the optimized LightGBM is used to subdivide the attack data into specific attacks. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 99.92% on the CIC-IDS2017 dataset, which is 1.04% higher than that obtained by directly using LightGBM, and testing time is reduced by 69.12%.

articleTitle: Fiber Optic Vibration Signal Recognition Based on GOA-VMD and Weighted Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In distributed fiber optic vibration sensing systems, the fiber optic vibration signals are often affected by complex real-world environments, resulting in unstable signal recognition outcomes. To address the question, this paper proposes a recognition method combining the Goose Optimization Algorithm (GOA), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), and Support Vector Machines (SVM). First, GOA is used to optimize VMD, enabling the adaptive selection of VMD parameters to obtain more stable Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). Next, correlation coefficients are used to screen the IMFs, retaining the highly correlated IMFs, which are then weighted and combined to reconstruct the signal. Time-domain and frequency-domain features are then extracted from the reconstructed vibration signal. Finally, SVM is employed to recognize signals, and GOA is also used to optimize the parameters in SVM to enhance its performance. Experimental results show that the method based on GOA-VMD and weighted reconstruction achieves higher accuracy, verifying the superiority compared with other recognition methods.

articleTitle: Collision detection method for industrial robots based on multi-channel information fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Collision detection is an important part of ensuring its safety and reliability, and it is a low-cost and low-requirement collision detection method to detect and identify collision events based on the data of sensors or monitoring systems inside the robot. In view of the shortcomings of the existing deep learning methods in processing the robot motion state data, this paper constructs a CA-Transformer network with multi-channel information fusion, takes the real-time load as the judgment index, realizes the fast and effective prediction of the robot load, and integrates a variety of sensor data in turn to improve the analysis ability of the robot state. The research results can provide ideas for the safe operation detection of robots.

articleTitle: Research on Factors Affecting Weight Based on Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In view of the increasing prevalence of overweight and obesity in Chinese residents, in order to explore the factors affecting weight, three machine learning models based on logical regression algorithm, decision tree algorithm and random forest algorithm are constructed to explore the factors affecting weight. The model is continuously optimized by parameters and cross-validation, and the performance of the model is evaluated by using four indicators: accuracy, precision, recall and the harmonic average of the two. The results show that the accuracy of logistic regression algorithm, decision tree algorithm and random forest algorithm are 0.65, 0.75 and 0.8 respectively, which shows that the decision tree algorithm and random forest algorithm can better complete the classification and prediction of weight influencing factors, and the random forest algorithm has the best classification and prediction effect, which can be used for researchers and practitioners in the field of nutrition and health reference.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Photovoltaic Power Prediction Models Based on BP and XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation is influenced by fluctuating environmental factors and exhibits significant non-linearity, making accurate prediction challenging. This paper constructs photovoltaic power prediction models based on BP neural network and XGBoost algorithms, and experimentally validates their predictive performance. The models are evaluated using metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The experimental results indicate that the BP neural network demonstrates stable performance in handling complex nonlinear relationships, while XGBoost achieves higher prediction accuracy and better generalization ability when the dataset is relatively small. This study provides a reference for the selection of photovoltaic power prediction models and lays the foundation for improving prediction accuracy in renewable energy power systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Locally Optimized Path Planning For Unmanned Surface Vehicle Under High Sea Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence algorithms has promoted the intelligent transformation of the shipbuilding industry, and unmanned surface vehicle (USV) have become prominent representative products. However, in the case of offshore sailing, high sea state environmental impact may be encountered, and the wind, current and waves of the environment will change with time, so it is necessary to take into account the impact of wind, ocean currents and waves on the energy consumption and driving safety during the collision avoidance process of USV in real scenarios. Therefore, this paper introduces an Informed Affected DWA algorithm, called IA-DWA, that combines wind, current and wave assessment calculations, while improving the assessment methods of energy consumption and navigation safety. Simulation results show that, compared with Affected DWA algorithm, IA-DWA algorithm greatly improves time efficiency, energy consumption, and safety, and achieves collision avoidance.

articleTitle: Gait phase detection based on inception-self-attention
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Gait analysis is an important research direction in motion monitoring and lower limb exoskeleton. Based on real IMU data and ground reaction force data, this paper proposes a deep learning model that combines Inception and Self-Attention mechanisms for gait phase classification. The experiment uses multi-time step input to perform classification tasks under 4-phase, 5-phase, and 6-phase gait division conditions and comprehensively analyzes the impact of model parameters on performance. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy of the proposed method under different divisions reaches 97.85%, 96.77%, and 96.37% respectively, reflecting the model’s adaptability to different gait fine-grained classification tasks. This study provides effective support for the application of gait recognition technology in the development of smart wearable devices and motion monitoring and also lays a theoretical and practical foundation for in-depth research on gait phase classification.

articleTitle: Kinematics-Based Vibration Control of a Wheeled Quadruped Robot Traversing Speed Bumps
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The Wheeled Quadruped Robot (WQR) combines the advantages of wheeled and legged mobility, garnering attention for its superior agility and stability in challenging environments. However, smoothly navigating uneven and complex terrains remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a novel kinematics-based control strategy for crossing parallel and staggered speed bumps, leveraging data from an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) and in-wheel contact sensors to enhance stability and mitigate vibrations. Our approach incorporates an advanced vibration control method that precisely adjusts the angles of the WQR's hip and knee joints in real-time, based on feedback from the IMU's pitch angle and the contact states of the in-wheel contact sensors. By continuously monitoring and adjusting the WQR’s posture, we achieve a significant reduction in vibration amplitude during speed bumps traversal, thereby enhancing both driving comfort and overall stability. Extensive simulations have validated the effectiveness of our method, demonstrating a notable decrease in vibration amplitude. This advancement facilitates the deployment of WQRs in harsh terrains, ensuring more reliable, efficient, and comfortable operation. By tackling the challenges of navigating complex environments, our research propels the development of WQRs for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Photovoltaic Power Prediction Models Based on BP and SVR
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The power output of photovoltaic (PV) generation is influenced by various environmental factors, exhibiting non-linearity and uncertainty. This paper constructs photovoltaic power prediction models based on BP neural network and support vector regression (SVR) algorithms, and performs a comparative analysis of model performance using metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The results show that the BP neural network is suitable for handling complex nonlinear large-scale data, while SVR demonstrates higher accuracy and generalization ability under small sample conditions. This study provides a reference for the selection and optimization of photovoltaic power prediction models.

articleTitle: An Aaptive Sliding Mode Control Based on an Improved Reduced-Order Proportional-Integral Observer with an Improved Super-Twisting Oserver
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper describes an adaptive sliding mode control method, which constructs an improved over-twisted observer based on the improved reduced-order proportional integral observer (IROPIO) and Super-Twisting linear term over-twisting algorithm (STLT). Among them, the system introduces a first-order linear term, which accelerates the convergence rate of velocity estimation and greatly reduces the estimation error. At the same time, this method effectively reduces the fluctuation of the control signal and shortens the time required for the system trajectory to reach the slip mode surface. IROPIO can accurately predict unknown disturbances when the system is running, and provide feedforward compensation for adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC), effectively solving the overshoot condition of the speed response that may occur due to disturbance estimation errors during the speed jump process. Robustness and dynamic performance are thus improved. Experimental results show that this method can significantly optimize control performance in practical applications, providing an efficient and reliable solution to the control problems of high-speed and high-precision systems.

articleTitle: YOLOv5-CBAM: A Small Object Detection Model Based on YOLOv5 and CBAM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: At present, object detection is a crucial technology, which plays an indispensable role in the field of object recognition, such as garbage detection conducted by unmanned boats in cleaning rivers and ship detection in traveling. Nowadays, YOLO algorithm is widely used and object detection requires the system to process external environment information in real time. With a fast processing speed, YOLO can process video streams at a very high frame rate. Thanks to its high-speed detection capabilities, it has become an ideal candidate algorithm in autonomous driving. However, the current YOLO technology is lack of detection accuracy for small objects, which may lead to potential risks and uncertainties in scenarios that require high-precision detection. Thus, this paper proposes a YOLOv5-CBAM small object recognition model, which adds two layers of CBAM to the backbone network of the original YOLOv5 model. Channel attention mechanism and spatial attention mechanism are introduced to promote the detection accuracy of small objects. In this paper, through experiments on WSODD dataset and compared with YOLOv5, it is confirmed that the YOLOv5-CBAM model proposed in this paper achieves better results in small object detection, play an indispensable part in the obstacle detection.

articleTitle: Design of arc welding robot workstation with dual station detection based on vision
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: At present, commonly used arc welding robot workstations mainly include three working surfaces: loading, welding, and unloading during welding operations. The process flow is as follows: the handling robot clamps the weldment for loading, the fixture fixes the weldment, the arc welding robot welds the weldment, and the handling robot clamps the weldment for unloading. The quality of weld seam is mainly determined by the precision of equipment such as positioner, fixtures, and arc welding robot. The welding quality of the weld seam is determined by the pass rate of the sampling samples. This testing method cannot obtain the true product pass rate, nor can it timely remove unqualified products for necessary repairs. Based on this situation, we have designed a arc welding robot workstation with dual station detection based on vision in this paper, which solves the problems of weld seam tracking and post weld seam quality inspection, synchronization of welding robots and handling robots, and welding and inspection of all welds in the flat welding position, achieving the effect of improving quality and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Pedestrian Re-Identification Method Integrating ResNet and Residual Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Person Re-identification is an important task in the field of computer vision, which aims to identify the same person across cameras and scenes. However, due to the influence of perspective changes, illumination differences, occlusion and other factors, person re-identification still faces great challenges. In order to solve these problems, this paper proposes a deep learning method combining ResNet and residual self-attention mechanism to improve the robustness and feature expression ability of the model for complex scenes. In this method, the ResNet-18 network is used as the backbone, and a self-attention module is embedded in each residual block to enhance the network's ability to perceive global context information by learning the relationship between different positions in the feature map. At the same time, the output of the self-attention module is fused by residual connection, which can not only effectively avoid gradient disappearance, but also retain the original feature information and promote the training of the deep network. Experimental results on the public dataset Market-1501 demonstrate that the proposed method achieves mAP and accuracy scores of 95.21% and 93.01%, respectively, outperforming existing methods. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach in the person reidentification task.

articleTitle: Lightweight detection method of distracted driving based on YOLO-SSC
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the problems of high device requirements, low detection accuracy, and high miss detection rate of overlapping targets in traditional distracted driving target detection models, a vehicle target detection algorithm called YOLO-SSC, based on the improved YOLOv8, was proposed. First, the main body network was reconstructed by using multi-scale fusion. Then, the StarBlock module was used to improve the C2f module in the neck, achieving multi-scale feature fusion to improve the model's detection accuracy for different size and distance targets. Finally, a lightweight model with shared convolution was used to further reduce the model's parameter number and computational cost. The experimental results show that the mAP50 of the improved model is 96.3%, the number of model parameters and the amount of model calculation are 1.4M and 4.5G, respectively, which are reduced by 53.3%and 44.4%compared with YOLOv8n.

articleTitle: Fault Monitoring of Electric Vehicle Motor Drive Systems: Effective Application of PLC Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Due to the inability of existing methods to complete the transformation of nonlinear drive information, the fault detection rate of motor drive systems is relatively low. This paper proposes a method for fault detection of motor drive systems in new energy vehicles under PLC technology. Wavelet packet analysis is used to obtain the frequency band components of the drive motor, and fault characteristic parameters are extracted by analyzing the changes in each frequency band component. Based on the fault characteristics, under PLC technology, a fusion of kernel methods and principal component analysis is used to transform the nonlinear information of the motor drive fault characteristic parameters into linear information. Finally, the fuzzy kernel clustering method is applied to cluster the linearized information, completing the fault detection of the motor drive system in new energy vehicles. Experimental results show that the proposed method has a low rate of missed and false detections, enhances fault detection rates, and has strong practical application performance.

articleTitle: Mixed-Domain Feature Fusion Network for Few-Sample Automatic Modulation Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the explosion of modern wireless communication information and the need for high transmission rates, automatic modulation recognition (AMR) based on deep learning (DL) has become increasingly popular. However, DL-based AMR methods often require large training samples. In order to solve this problem, we propose a mixed-domain feature fusion network (MDFNet) for small sample modulation recognition. The network can efficiently fuse the time and frequency domain features of signals, have certain noise reduction effect on the feature transmission of signals, enhance the capture of effective information by the model, and greatly improve the identification accuracy. Experiments with on two existing well-known datasets RML2016.10a and RML2016.04c demonstrate that the model performs significantly in small sample modulation identification.

articleTitle: Autonomous Penetration Test Path Planning Based on OIPPO
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Intelligent penetration testing combines deep reinforcement learning to plan attack paths and simulate complex attack scenarios to identify system weaknesses. Compared with traditional penetration testing, it can learn and optimize strategies independently and simulate more complex attack paths and attacker behaviors.However, the existing methods have problems such as gradient explosion, gradient disappearance and suboptimal solution in the training process. In order to solve these problems, this paper introduces proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm, and proposes an improved PPO algorithm which combines orthogonal initialization and policy entropy control (OIPPO).The algorithm combines the advantages of orthogonal initialization and PPO algorithm, and improves the performance and efficiency of the algorithm through policy entropy control. The experimental results show that the convergence speed of OIPPO algorithm is better than that of traditional PPO and its improved algorithms in various network scenarios, and it shows better effectiveness, scalability and compatibility when the network scale is expanded.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control of Buck Converter Based on Disturbance Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of matched and unmatched disturbances in Buck converter systems, this paper proposes a full-order sliding mode control strategy based on a disturbance observer. Firstly, the mathematical model of the Buck converter with multiple disturbances is established. Secondly, two disturbance observers are designed to estimate the matched and unmatched disturbances, respectively, in order to track the disturbance signals and mitigate the effects of various uncertainties on the system. Next, a full-order sliding-mode control strategy based on the disturbance observers is proposed to enhance the dynamic performance of the controller and reduce steady-state error. Finally, the stability of the proposed controller is proved using Lyapunov theory. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses system disturbances, resulting in faster convergence and higher tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: IOT Attack Type Detection and Classification Based on Multi-strategy Hybrid and Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm to Optimize Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
