abstract: In this paper, the classical random forest model is used as the basis, and the sparrow search algorithm with multi-strategy hybrid is combined to optimize the attack detection and attack type prediction in the Internet of Things system. The aim of the experiment is to improve the performance of the random forest model by using various parameters of the Internet of Things system, so as to realize effective identification and classification of various attacks in the Internet of Things environment. During the experiment, the dataset contained three different types of IOT attacks. After 15 training iterations, the model's prediction results of attack types gradually approached the actual situation, and the initial loss value gradually decreased from 3.2 to 0 in the 14th iteration, which indicates that the model's prediction ability and classification effect have been significantly improved. By analyzing the confusion matrix of the training set, it can be seen that the model achieves 100% accurate prediction for all three types of IOT attacks. In the test set, a total of 270 attack types were predicted, of which 268 were correct and only two were wrong, resulting in a prediction accuracy of 99.26%. This result is similar to the performance of the training set, indicating that the model not only has a good prediction effect, but also shows a strong generalization ability. In summary, this study successfully applied the multi-strategy hybrid improved Sparrow search algorithm to the random forest model, effectively improving the performance of attack detection and classification in IOT systems. This achievement provides important support for ensuring the security of the Internet of Things environment, not only enhances the response ability to potential threats, but also provides new ideas and methods for future related research.

articleTitle: A Review of Key Technologies for Monocular 3D Face Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In recent years, 3D face reconstruction techniques have gradually become a research hotspot. As a key part of visual perception, the human face contains a wealth of individual features, so it occupies an important position in 3D reconstruction and has a wide range of application potential. Currently, most 3D face reconstruction research focuses on single image face processing, while monocular 3D face reconstruction has been widely used in various fields due to its convenience and efficiency. Therefore, this paper will focus on monocular 3D face reconstruction, first outlining the development history of the technique and its commonly used datasets, followed by an in-depth analysis of the challenges and the application scenarios in which it can be implemented.

articleTitle: An improved meta-heuristic optimization algorithm based on chaotic mapping inspired by the football team training
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of the football team training algorithm (FTTA) that the solution is unstable and easy to fall into local optimum, this paper proposes 15 kinds of chaotic mappings to initialize the player population to improve the football team training algorithm, starting from the collective training of FTTA. Finally, the performance of the 15 improved soccer team training algorithms is verified by CEC2020 test function F1 and compared with the initial soccer team training algorithm. In the test, Sinusoidal map improved FTTA showed better performance. It provides new ideas and directions for improving FTTA.

articleTitle: Deep neural networks based Gravitational Field for Asteroid Landing Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The irregular shape of the asteroid makes it challenging for precise gravitational field modeling, further impacting control precision and making onboard computational time intolerable for the control law. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of gravitational field calculations and control for asteroid landing, deep neural networks (DNN) are employed to approximate the asteroid’s gravitational field. To this end, the DNN is trained by utilizing samples generated from the polyhedral model. Then, the asteroid gravitational field DNN is applied to multiple sliding surfaces control for asteroid landing. Finally, numerical simulation results of landings on 433 Eros are presented, demonstrating that the DNN yields highly accurate approximations and significantly improves the efficiency of control law resolution.

articleTitle: Robust Control Methods for Vehicle Trajectory Tracking Amid Multi-Channel Network Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Network attacks present a critical threat to vehicle trajectory tracking systems, especially when multi-channel attacks can severely compromise system stability and tracking accuracy. Addressing these issues is challenging due to the complexity of vehicle dynamics, attack signal suppression, and reliable tracking on roads with varying curvature. This paper proposes an advanced control strategy based on a fuzzy extended observer to mitigate multi-channel network attacks. A hybrid model integrating fuzzy inference with Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) techniques is developed to capture trajectory tracking dynamics. A fuzzy extended observer estimates attack impacts on vehicle dynamics, and a fuzzy controller is designed to counteract these attacks while ensuring stable tracking. The stability analysis confirms the stability of the system. Finally, co-simulations in CarSim and Simulink demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Covert Spoofing Method for Integrated Navigation Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely employed in both military and civilian domains, making spoofing technology a key component for achieving various operational objectives. This paper presents a covert UAV spoofing technique that utilizes the model predictive control algorithm to accurately manipulate non-cooperative UAVs, enhance the covertness of spoofing signals, and reduce the accumulation of control errors. Simulation verification indicates that this method significantly improves spoofing accuracy, offering strategic and tactical advantages for the covert spoofing of non-cooperative UAVs.

articleTitle: Research on Short-term Power Load Forecasting Based on APSO-SVR
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Since its introduction, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model has been widely applied in various aspects of society. In the field of prediction, many scholars and experts have proposed the Support Vector Regression (SVR) model based on SVM specifically for regression problems, but the original SVR model has certain deficiencies. As a result, numerous experts and scholars have proposed various optimization methods to address the shortcomings of the original SVR model, achieving good applications. The SVR model often leads to overfitting or underfitting due to improper selection of penalty parameters and kernel parameters. Based on this, this paper optimizes the selection of penalty parameters and kernel parameters by using the Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (APSO) algorithm to obtain optimal parameters, thereby improving the SVR model. A new APSO-SVR model is proposed and applied to a case study of Romanian power output prediction. The results indicate that the combined optimized PSO-SVR has higher fitting accuracy and better prediction performance, validating the effectiveness and practicality of the PSO-SVR model and expanding the application scope of SVR.

articleTitle: Mechanism design and performance analysis of tracked pipe robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Pipeline robot is a kind of system that can automatically walk along the pipeline, with one or more sensors and operation machinery (such as manipulator, spray gun, etc.), under the remote control or automatic control of the operator, can carry out a series of pipeline operations machine-electric-instrument integrated system. It is often used in petroleum, chemical industry, nuclear industry, urban construction and other engineering pipeline quality inspection, welding, maintenance and so on. Pipeline robot is also a combination of multiple disciplines, involving mechanical engineering, automatic control, computers, sensors, artificial intelligence and electronic technology. At present, the development of pipeline robot mainly focuses on the innovation and development of mechanism, drive, sensors, intelligent control, miniaturization, power supply and communication. Based on the scientific research achievements at home and abroad, this paper systematically studied the driving principle and mode, movement principle and mechanical mechanism of the pipeline robot. Main work for the institutional research design of pipeline robots. Based on the comprehensive consideration of various factors, the pipeline robot mobile mechanism is determined, and points out the main problems that should be considered when designing the robot.

articleTitle: Multi-target point TSP and optimized path planning for AUV based on 3D underwater digital topography
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Based on the underwater digital topography, this paper investigates the multi-target point traveling salesman problem (TSP) and path planning smoothing optimization problem for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) in underwater environments, combining the influence of ocean currents and the requirements of safety and energy consumption when navigating, and improved an algorithm suitable for underwater path planning. Firstly, distinguished from the traditional methods, the Digital Elevation Model (DEM) is introduced to create a map of the underwater environment with known terrain in order to simulate the underwater environment better. By adding the current factor to the map and applying it to the underwater path planning, the AUV successfully completes the path planning under the influence of the currents. As obstacles appear during navigation, the AUV can replan in real time to avoid the obstacles and ensure the safety of navigation. In planning, it is necessary to consider the weights between the target points, reasonably plan the path order, and convert the problem of the visiting order of target points into a TSP issue to find the optimal visiting order. Considering the kinematic characteristics of AUV on this basis, the path smoothing is carried out by using B spline curve to satisfy the kinematic constraints of AUV. Simulation analysis verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Automatic Dexterous Functional Grasping Data Generation Based on Conditional Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper proposes an automatic dexterous functional grasping data generation framework for multi-finger robot hands. This work has important benefits for developing effective data driven dexterous grasping methods, because the data scarcity has delayed the relevant research progress currently. Taking the diffusion model as the main architecture, the proposed method leverages the advantages of high generation quality and diversity, designing a controlling condition by integrating the grasp pose and object category. After further candidates selection and point clouds refinement, the generated dataset have been validated through experiments to fulfill the requirements of functionality, diversity, scalability.

articleTitle: Vehicle Recognition Method Based on Multi-sensor Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: A multi-sensor fusion algorithm for vehicle recognition and detection is proposed to solve the problem that a single sensor is prone to false detection or missing detection in a complex driving environment. The Ghost Conv module is used to improve the traditional Conv and C3 module to achieve lightweight. An improved PointNet++ algorithm based on ResMLP is proposed to increase network depth to solve the problem of low obstacle detection accuracy caused by too small obstacle detection model. Millimeter wave radar and camera features are associated based on the matching method between image detection frame and radar projection point. The radar point cloud is projected onto the pixel coordinate system to realize the fusion of multi-sensor information. The simulation results show that the detection accuracy of the multi-sensor fusion vehicle identification algorithm is 9.8% higher than that of PointPillars and 11.7% higher than that of CenterFusion, which can effectively obtain vehicle information.

articleTitle: The Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images Based on Improved YOLO11 with LDConv
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The YOLO series of object detection algorithms have been constantly updated in recent years, the latest YOLO algorithm has been updated to YOLO11, which can not only detect objects more accurately, but also detect sloping objects. Based on the newly released YOLO11-OBB algorithm, this paper improved the YOLO11-OBB algorithm on the remote sensing image dataset of Tianzhi Cup Competition held in this year, combined with a newly released LDConv algorithm, and finally trained the improved algorithm, which can improve the mAP of the YOLO11-OBB-N algorithm by 3.7% and the number of parameters is reduced by 4.5%, enabling more accurate and less computationally intensive object detection.

articleTitle: Research on Writing Robots Based on the XY Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence, writing robots have broad application potential in various fields. This study designs and implements a writing robot based on the XY platform, first addressing the mechanical design of the XY platform to enhance structural rigidity and optimize the drive system to reduce vibration and noise, integrating related components to ensure precise movement along the X and Y axes; on the software side, it processes vector text to extract and store character contour lines. The results of the study lay the foundation for the design and development of writing robots and further research in automated writing technology.

articleTitle: Design and experimental study of a bionic stingray robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Inspired by the pectoral fin fluctuation swimming of the biological stingray, a bionic stingray robot prototype was designed with reference to the morphological proportions of the stingray, which is capable of performing a more supple pectoral fin fluctuation motion. With the research objective of exploring the effects of fin oscillation frequency, maximum oscillation angle, and fin surface offset angle on the propulsive force of the bionic stingray robot, the relevant experimental programme was designed and tested according to the control variable method. Within the range of experimental data, it was concluded that the propulsive force was increasing with increasing swing frequency and increasing with increasing maximum swing angle.

articleTitle: Obstacles Avoidance Path Planning for Mobile Robot Based on Cellular Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to quickly plan the shortest path for mobile robot in two-dimensional space, a two-stage obstacles avoidance path planning algorithm based on cellular automata was presented in this paper. For the first stage, the distance between each free cell to the ending cell was gradually generated by the evolution of cellular automata, and the algorithm’s cellular space, cellular states, Moore type neighbors and evolutionary rules were described, respectively. For the second stage, by using the idea of the negative gradient, a method of generating the shortest path based on the cells’ state values was proposed. Accordingly, the corresponding flow chart and Matlab programme of the algorithm were designed. The effectiveness of the algorithm was verified by the simulation and the physical experiment. The results showed that the shortest path in complex environment can be efficiently planned by using our cellular automata algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Knowledge Creation of Large Language Models Based on the SECI Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rise of large language models, researchers have extensively explored their characteristics. This paper aims to integrate Large Language Models with the SECI (Socialization, Externalization, Combination, Internalization) knowledge creation theory. Based on the SECI theoretical framework, a comprehensive analysis is conducted on the knowledge creation and transformation process of Large Language Models across various stages, from pre-training to knowledge generation. By leveraging the language generation capabilities of Large Language Models, this study seeks to facilitate the flow, transformation, and innovation of knowledge both within and outside organizations, thereby advancing the field of knowledge management.

articleTitle: Research on Substation Equipment Defect Detection Technology Based on an Improved RT-DETR Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the challenges in intelligent inspection of substation equipment, including difficulties in acquiring defect image data, the high complexity of equipment, and the low efficiency of defect detection technologies, this paper conducts research on defect detection techniques for substation equipment based on an improved RT-DETR model. Additionally, a specialized dataset for substation equipment defect detection is constructed. First, the backbone of RT-DETR is replaced with the lightweight FasterNet, and deformable convolution (DCNv4) and channel attention (ECA) are introduced to achieve efficient feature extraction for multi-scale targets, improving detection accuracy while reducing the number of parameters. Moreover, an improved cascaded attention encoder is used to replace the original encoder, enabling the network to focus more on the target regions, further reducing computational redundancy and enhancing model efficiency. Finally, extensive comparative experiments are conducted on the self-constructed substation equipment defect dataset. The results show that the improved model achieved a 2.5% increase in average detection accuracy mAP@0.5 and a 2.2% increase in mAP@0.5:0.95 compared to the baseline model. Furthermore, the model’s parameters are reduced by 13.9%, GFLOPs decreased by 5.1%, and the frames processed per second (FPS) increased by 35%. Overall, the model outperforms other advanced defect detection models and is better suited to meet the demands of defect detection for multi-class and multi-scale targets in complex environments.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Knowledge Distillation-Based Network for Efficient Remote Sensing Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The rapid development of remote sensing technologies has driven demand for lightweight networks capable of efficient change detection on resource-constrained devices. This paper proposes a novel architecture combining knowledge distillation and an improved EfficientNet structure. Key innovations include the Feature Mask Distillation (FMD) and Multi-Kernel Fusion (MKF) modules to enhance feature extraction and multi-scale representation. Experiments on LEVIR-CD and DSIFN datasets demonstrate superior performance with F1-scores of 82.97% and 66.18%, respectively, offering an efficient solution for change detection in resource-limited scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Transformer-LSTM Daily Sales Forecasting Model Based on Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Accurate sales forecasting remains a key challenge for retailers. Existing methods often struggle to integrate local and global contextual dependencies, limiting their predictive accuracy in complex scenarios. In response to these challenges in sales forecasting, we propose an attention-enhanced Transformer-LSTM model. Firstly, we combine the LSTM’s capability to capture time-related sequential data with the Transformer’s global context awareness; secondly, we prioritize the most influential features dynamically through an enhanced attention mechanism for prediction; thirdly, by adopting a hybrid architecture, we effectively address both short-term and long-term dependencies within sales data. Experimental results show that our model not only significantly outperforms traditional forecasting methods but also improves upon recent deep learning approaches in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared (R2) metrics.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Platform AMR Loading Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In modern warehouse automation, the platform environment to the automatic loading of goods in the container is basically through manual or large conveyor belt machinery to complete, the container is dark and narrow, easy to due to the goods scuffing or the target point is not clear resulting in reduced efficiency. The automatic loading of mobile robots can solve these problems, but at present there are fewer autonomous mobile robot solutions applied to the platform container environment. In this paper, A path planning algorithm is proposed for platform loading tasks, in which LiDAR scans the container to calculate the coordinates of the loading positions and obtains the best third-order Bezier curve based on particle swarm optimization. The experiment proves that the algorithm can effectively get the loading points in the container and fit an excellent smooth route to improve the efficiency of navigation.

articleTitle: Locomotion of Microrobots Driven by Different Surface Velocities in Complex Fluids
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Over the past few decades, microrobots have rapidly evolved. Given their tiny size, microrobots can access all body regions to facilitate targeted therapies and diagnostics, having great potential in biomedical engineering and biomedicine. While most previous demonstrations of microrobots typically considered a homogeneous Newtonian fluid as the medium, the reality of the biological environment is much more complex, with many biological fluids displaying complex non-Newtonian properties including viscoelasticity and shear-thinning viscosity. The squirmer model is a popular and generalized swimmer model for motions in non-Newtonian fluid, where the swimming velocity is generally given by the surface average of the prescribed velocity. To further explore the effects of neglected surface velocity details and shear-thinning properties on the motions of microrobots in non-Newtonian fluids, a simulation framework was proposed for studying the kinematic performance of robots in complex fluids. The effects of shearthinning properties on the kinematic performance of microrobots with different surface velocity distributions were also investigated. Furthermore, the threshold value of the magnetic moment applied to the robot when it is not deflected was also discussed. The design of different types of surface velocities for microrobots involved in this paper can better guide more efficient propulsion of microrobots in complex biofluids.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Distillation of SAM for Lightweight Insulator Defect Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The real-time detection of insulator failures is particularly critical for the safety of power transmission networks. Traditional drone inspections are often constrained by limited computational resources and network bandwidth, making the real-time detection of defects an increasingly pressing requirement. This paper introduces a novel approach for insulator defect segmentation by hierarchically distilling a Segment Anything Model (SAM) to develop a lightweight UNet model. We propose utilizing defect detection boxes as segmentation prompts, thereby equipping SAM with the capability for defect segmentation. Through a phased distillation process, we refine a lightweight UNet model that maintains high accuracy while significantly reducing computational load. Specifically, we introduce a hierarchical distillation strategy that encompasses feature embedding distillation and segmentation mask distillation. Extensive experiments validate the efficiency and applicability of the proposed model for high-voltage insulator defect segmentation.

articleTitle: Study on Accuracy Degradation Experimental of RV Reducer*
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As the performance demands for precision reducers continue to increase, accuracy retention has become a critical evaluation criterion. This study examines the degradation of the RV reducer accuracy by analyzing real-time monitoring data, transmission performance test results, and cycloid gear surface wear measurements. The analysis identifies key characteristic variations throughout the accuracy degradation process and confirms that the degradation follows the typical wear pattern, often referred to as the "bathtub curve." Furthermore, the study reveals that the wear on the RV reducer cycloid gears is uneven along the circumferential direction, with notable differences in the wear and load bearing conditions between the two cycloid gears.

articleTitle: Data-efficient Iterative Learning Longitudinal Velocity Planning for Autonomous Logistics Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid growth of the logistics industry has brought rising fuel costs and increasing greenhouse gas emissions into sharper focus. With the development in autonomous driving technology, the problem of longitudinal velocity planning for logistics vehicles has attracted wide attention. To improve the fuel economy of autonomous logistics vehicles traveling on known routes, this paper proposes a data-efficient iterative learning optimization (DILO) method. The proposed method integrates the advantages of optimization-based and learning-based methods, using an iterative process to learn continuously from historical data and ultimately converge to the optimal longitudinal velocity solution. Simulation experiments conducted in Simulink and TruckSim using real-world road data demonstrate that the proposed method can generate optimized longitudinal velocity trajectories in both modes and significantly reduce vehicle fuel consumption.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of CNC machine tool spindle based on SSA-CNN-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the fault diagnosis of CNC machine tool spindle bearing, a fault diagnosis method of CNC machine tool spindle bearing based on SSA-CNN-Transformer is proposed. First, the vibration signal is converted into time-frequency image through continuous wavelet transform, and then the local features of the time-frequency graph of the vibration signal are extracted by using CNN. The attention mechanism of Transformer is used to capture the global dependence of the time-frequency graph of the vibration data. The SSA algorithm is used to optimize the hyperparameters of the model, which improves the generalization ability and precision of fault diagnosis. The results show that this method performs well in the fault diagnosis of spindle bearing of CNC machine tool, with an average diagnosis accuracy of 94.6%.

articleTitle: Investigating SLAM Algorithms for Robustness in Illumination-Varying Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Indirect methods for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) are susceptible to illumination variations, which can compromise the algorithm's robustness. To enhance the performance of SLAM algorithms in low-light or illumination-varying environments, we propose an improved ORB-SLAM method tailored for such challenging conditions. The method employs a joint histogram that integrates pixel intensity values with the mean intensity of their neighborhoods, using a twodimensional cumulative distribution function (CDF) to map intensity values and effectively expand the dynamic range. Additionally, a dynamic gamma correction technique is introduced to further enhance image brightness and optimize detail representation. Experimental evaluations on public datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the robustness of ORB-SLAM in low-light and illumination-varying scenarios.

articleTitle: Neural Inertial Navigation Method for Wheeled Robots Based on Semi-supervised Co-training
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Traditional supervised neural inertial navigation methods for wheeled robots rely much on training data. The lack of labeled data is usually caused by factors such as cost, which affects the normal training process This paper presents a semi-supervised one. It denoises IMU gyro data for attitude and faster iteration, estimates speed via co-training, and calculates the robot's position. Verified on a public dataset, without enough labeled data, compared to supervised methods, it reduces vehicle's absolute and relative trajectory errors by 83.27% and 84.14% respectively, proving its efficacy.

articleTitle: Smart Home Control and Implementation for Elderly People Living Alone Based on STM32 Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the acceleration of the aging process in my country, the number of elderly people living alone is increasing year by year, and the issue of home safety has gradually attracted widespread attention from the society. This paper designs a smart home system based on the STM32 microcontroller to improve the home safety and living convenience of elderly people living alone. The system integrates temperature and humidity, light, air quality and combustible gas sensors to collect real-time environmental data in the house and automatically control home appliances such as lights, air conditioners, humidifiers, etc. to maintain indoor comfort. When an abnormal situation (such as combustible gas leakage or high temperature) is detected, the system will automatically alarm and send an alarm SMS to the guardian through the GSM module. The hardware is based on STM32F103C8T6, and the software is developed based on Keil5 and STM32CubeMX, realizing the functions of environmental monitoring, equipment control and network communication. After simulation and debugging, the system shows that the design has good stability and reliability, can accurately collect environmental parameters and control equipment response, and provides effective assistance to the daily life of elderly people living alone.

articleTitle: A VMamba Attention Network for Efficient Deformable Image Registration in Lung 4DCT
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Image registration is a foundational technique in medical image analysis; however, it is often hindered by issues such as slow processing speed and limited accuracy. In this work, we propose the Visual Mamba Attention Network (VMANet) for lung image registration. VMANet incorporates a dual-stream Mamba Attention module, enabling the effective capture of global spatial and channel information. This enhances its ability to perform precise feature extraction and deformation field prediction, making it well-suited for image registration tasks. Finally, a spatial transformation layer leverages the deformation field to warp the moving image to the fixed image. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing convolutional neural network-based registration methods in terms of both registration accuracy and real-time performance. The proposed VMANet model thus shows significant promise for applications in pulmonary studies.

articleTitle: GABP-TroNet: Enhance Air-Ground Channel Modeling by Improving GZTDS Model for GNSS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Tropospheric delay is an error factor in high-precision positioning of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS).The simplified GNSS tropospheric delay model (GZTDS) predicts zenith tropospheric delay (ZTD) around the world and shows good global performance with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 3.46 cm. However, in some regions, the GZTDS model performs poorly. This paper intends to improve performance of the GZTDS model in the coastal regions of China by combining the GZTDS model with back propagation (BP) neural network based on genetic algorithm (GABP-TroNet). With the validation of data from the Vienna Mapping Function 1 (VMF1), the mean bias (MB) of the GABP-TroNet model is 0.08 cm and the RMSE is 3.11 cm, which improves the accuracy of predicting ZTD in the coastal regions of China compared to GZTDS.

Author Keywords: back propagation neural network based on genetic algorithm

articleTitle: A Triangular Descriptor with Distance Information for Loop Closure Detection in LiDAR SLAM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the field of mobile robotics, loop closure detection serves as an essential component of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM). Compared with vision-based approaches, LiDAR-based loop closure detection offers more stable geometric features. This paper proposes a novel triangular descriptor with distance information. The proposed method extracts keypoints through adaptive Euclidean clustering, constructs distance vectors based on keypoint relationships, and generates the descriptor by integrating triangular geometric features. Experiments on the KITTI dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches with superior maximum F1 scores across multiple sequences. Integration of the algorithm into the LeGO-LOAM system reduces cumulative drift error by 31.16%, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: An End-to-end Campus Fire Detection Algorithm Incorporating Priori Features
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the imbalance in detection speed and accuracy caused by smoke, flame, and background confusion in campus video surveillance scenarios, an end-to-end campus fire detection algorithm incorporating priori features is proposed. First, a feature pyramid fusion module guided by priori features is constructed to cascade the multi-scale feature fusion module. The priori features are individually pre-trained by Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) classification network. The feature complementarity between the two is utilized to improve the feature representation of the detection network. Second, a lightweight set prediction detection head is designed. The head does not require manually designed anchors and post-processing strategies, enabling end-to-end detection while balancing speed and accuracy. Finally, a joint loss function that integrates the losses of categorical and bipartite matching is proposed. Focus on the drawbacks of the slow convergence associated with bipartite matching, both classification information and bipartite bit matching are considered in the detection results. Experimental results on the fire detection dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm improved average accuracy by 7.8% while maintaining detection speed, effectively balancing speed and accuracy in fire detection.

articleTitle: Fully End-to-End Chinese-Tibetan Bilingual Speech Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of insufficient amount of Tibetan speech data for bilingual speech synthesis. Based on the commonality of Chinese and Tibetan languages, we investigate a hybrid Chinese-Tibetan phoneme conversion table to share model training primitives. And then an end-to-end Chinese-Tibetan bilingual speech synthesis model is trained using the vits model. The model is capable of achieving cross-language speech synthesis for speakers utilizing merely two monolingual corpora; however, the Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) indicate a slight deterioration in the naturalness of the synthesized speech. In addition, this paper investigates the effects of whether Tibetan phonemes are labeled with tones or not, whether the bilingual speech synthesis model uses a hybrid phoneme list or not, and the training set size on the quality of speech synthesis. The experimental results show that for bilingual speech synthesis training, although adding tones to Tibetan can improve the performance of speech synthesis for a specific monolingual, it is difficult to fully utilize its performance because of dataset size; after that, this paper finds that mixed tones outperform other representations, and different language complexities lead to different amounts of data required for training.

articleTitle: A New Smart Flying-Car Based on Intelligent Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this paper, a new intelligent flying-car was designed and discussed. In order to solve surface traffic congestion, flying-car was designed based on flight control technology and automatic driving algorithm. It was a vertical takeoff and landing aircraft. When there were some different barriers, it could hover for a long time automatically. Its power source was composed of ternary lithium battery. By flying-car, choices of travel would become simple and convenient. Besides overcoming road congestion, energy conservation and environment protection will help flying-car become more and more popular.

articleTitle: Research on Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Few-shot Adversarial Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In cross-domain fault diagnosis tasks of bearings, the data distributions between the source domain (SD) and target domain (TD) often exhibit differences. Directly applying models trained on the SD to the TD typically fails to achieve satisfactory diagnostic results. Existing cross-domain diagnostic methods often require a large number of fault samples, which increases data collection costs and does not meet the practical needs of industry. Therefore, this paper proposes a few-shot adversarial domain adaptation method based on lightweight convolutional networks. By utilizing a lightweight feature extractor and adversarial mechanism to align features between the source and target domains, the classification accuracy of the TD is enhanced. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly improves the accuracy of the TD in multiple cross-domain classification tasks.

articleTitle: Development of a massage robot based on visiontactile fusion and adaptive force control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of robotics, robotic massage systems have shown great potential in ensuring consistent massage effectiveness and providing personalized treatments. However, accurately controlling the force applied during the massage, especially given the variation in muscle stiffness and tissue properties across different body regions, remains a significant challenge. Traditional force control methods typically rely on predefined trajectories or basic feedback systems, which are insufficient in adapting to these variations, often resulting in discomfort or suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. To address this, this paper proposes a robotic massage system with adaptive force control, integrating both vision and tactile sensing. The system combines computer vision-based skeletal recognition with real-time feedback from a six-dimensional force sensor to dynamically adjust the applied force based on variations in tissue stiffness across different body areas. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach optimizes force application, significantly enhancing both the effectiveness and comfort of the massage. This study introduces a vision-tactile fusion approach, offering new insights into overcoming the challenges of diversity and adaptability in current robotic massage systems.

articleTitle: Design of maize disease monitoring system based on Beidou satellite positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As times change, increasing crop output and quality is a must for contemporary agricultural development. Under the background of global warming and variety changing, maize pests have been multiplying and evolving, and the occurrence rule of insect pests has been changing. The only method to guarantee a high production and quality of maize is to avoid and control insect pests, as their presence has a significant negative impact on these factors. Based on Beidou satellite positioning technology and several sensors, this research realized real-time monitoring and early warning of corn field environment, and marked the location of disease and analyzed the data, integrating the Beidou data with the agricultural management system, generating disease and pest distribution maps and optimizing spraying and treatment plans, thereby reducing the impact on the environment.

articleTitle: Object Detection on SAR Images Via YOLOv10 and Integrated ACmix Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep learning techniques, object detection on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images has shown increasing potential in recent years. However, due to the unique microwave imaging mechanism of SAR, targets can easily be confused with background structures like harbors and aircraft aprons, leading to poor recognition accuracy. In this paper, we propose YOLOv10n-ACmix, an enhanced object detection model that integrates the ACmix attention mechanism into the YOLOv10 framework to improve feature extraction and detection precision. Through experiments conducted on the SARaircraft and MSAR datasets, YOLOv10n-ACmix consistently outperformed YOLOv5, YOLOv8 and YOLOv10 in precision, recall, and mean Average Precision (mAP). The inclusion of the ACmix mechanism enables the model to focus more effectively on critical features, resulting in more accurate detections. Despite a slight increase in computational complexity, the significant improvements in detection performance make YOLOv10n-ACmix a robust choice for high-precision object detection in SAR images. This work highlights the potential of attention mechanisms to enhance object detection in complex, large-scale SAR image datasets.

articleTitle: Research on Fast Identification and Location of Disordered Objects Based on Binocular Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor real-time performance of robot arm in identifying, positioning and grasping chaotic targets. A fast recognition and location algorithm of disordered targets based on binocular vision is designed. In this algorithm, an improved semi-global block matching algorithm is used to calculate the stereo matching of the target image, and the parallax map is output quickly by stereo matching of the image. Then combined with PCL library, the disordered target image is transformed into a point cloud image; Then point cloud processing and other operations are carried out; Finally, the point cloud image is segmented to screen out the first captured target, and the target point cloud is transferred from the camera coordinate system to the base coordinate system, and then the plane normal vector and plane center point coordinates of the target are obtained by plane fitting. So as to complete the rapid identification and location of disorderly targets. Experiments show that the improved algorithm can obviously reduce the time spent in stereo matching of disordered targets, and the calculation speed is increased by 30.7% compared with the traditional stereo matching.

articleTitle: Sliding mode control for uncertain robot manipulators based on reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper investigates a new method that combines sliding mode control with reinforcement learning to improve the robustness and adaptability of robot manipulators. Sliding mode control is renowned for its effectiveness in managing disturbances and ensuring stability; However, it typically requires a precise understanding of system dynamics, which may not always be available. By combining forward learning and a super-twisting algorithm observer to estimate the state and uncertainty of the system, our framework enables the robot system to learn the optimal control strategy through interaction with the environment, thereby reducing dependence on precise model parameters. Through theoretical analysis and simulation experiments, we have demonstrated that the proposed hybrid control method not only maintains robust performance in the face of uncertainty, but also can dynamically adapt to constantly changing conditions. Extensive simulations were conducted on a two degree of freedom robot system to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: M-LIME: a marginalized local interpretable model-agnostic explanations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To mitigate the inherent black-box nature of deep models, explainable artificial intelligence has gradually received widespread attention. Local Interpre table Model-agnostic Explanations is a popular interpretable algorithm, but its random deletion of perturbed samples generation leads to the problems of unstable interpretation results and out-of-distribution of the perturbed samples, resulting in a significant reduction in the credibility of the interpretation results. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes an explainable algorithm for text classification models based on input marginalization, alleviating its many problems through external component enhancement. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper has improved stability and effectiveness with low time cost. In addition, an evaluation metric is proposed that can more comprehensively and accurately measure the interpretable algorithm.

articleTitle: Perception and Autonomous Navigation Framework for an Underwater Micro-Bionic Snail Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The exploration of the underwater environment has driven research into bionic robotic systems, particularly the development of efficient and compact underwater robots capable of performing complex tasks. This study proposes an advanced framework for the perception and autonomous navigation of underwater micro-bionic water snail robots in accordance with the current bio-mechanistic motion model. The proposed model combines a hybrid neural control system with reinforcement learning, with the objective of enhancing the adaptive navigation of the robot in a dynamic underwater environment. In particular, the robot perception system employs a multi-modal sensor fusion methodology to integrate visual, fluid dynamics, and acoustic signals, thereby ensuring the robust perception of the surrounding environment. Additionally, an innovative approach to path planning has been developed, utilizing a deep neural network as its foundation, aimed to enhance obstacle avoidance and trajectory optimization. Furthermore, the locomotion system mimics the peristaltic motion of a water snail, thereby enhancing energy efficiency and mobility in confined environments. This study presents two novel concepts: real-time feedback mechanisms for adaptive behavior and a hierarchical decision-making framework balancing immediate actions with long-term objectives. The experimental results indicate that the proposed model showcases considerable strengths in navigation precision, adaptability, and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Spoofing Effectiveness Evaluation System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To quantify the effects of spoofing, this paper designs an evaluation system for assessing the efficacy of UAV spoofing, which integrates software-defined radio and data fusion technologies The system includes modules for spoofing effectiveness evaluation management, signal monitoring, UAV motion status monitoring, and communication. Details of the system's software and hardware implementation are provided, as well as how to evaluate metrics such as response time, signal effective range, accuracy, and minimum power. Experimental results validate the system's capability to assess UAV spoofing effectiveness. The system's modular design, compatibility and data recording capabilities render it a robust platform for UAV spoofing research and verification.

articleTitle: A Source Code Vulnerability Detection Method Based on Positive-Unlabeled Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As the scale of modern software continues to expand, the risk of software being attacked also increases. Software vulnerabilities are the primary cause of these risks. Traditional detection methods rely on expert knowledge and are difficult to meet the complex needs of today. In recent years, with the development of pre-trained models, some researchers have applied these models to the field of code vulnerability detection. However, pre-trained models require large amounts of labeled data, which is often difficult to obtain and ensure its quality. Therefore, how to effectively detect code vulnerabilities in a weakly supervised setting remains an important challenge. This paper presents PU-CBVD, a source code vulnerability detection model built on the pre-trained CodeBERT model. PU-CBVD utilizes abundant unlabeled data alongside a limited set of labeled samples, generating pseudo-labels for the unlabeled data. The combined dataset is then input into a pre-trained model, enhanced with a Gated Graph Neural Network (GGNN) for feature extraction and training, resulting in an effective source code vulnerability detection model. To evaluate its performance, we compared our model with existing weakly supervised learning methods and popular supervised vulnerability detection approaches. Experimental results show that our model significantly outperforms existing models.

articleTitle: National Cryptographic Algorithms based Personalized Federated Learning with Flight Data
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper designed FedPDA (Federated Learning Personalized Data Authentication) a new architecture that combines personalized federated learning and domestic encryption algorithms. The FedPDA enhanced the adaptability and prediction accuracy of specific flight data, -divided the model parameters into global general parameters and personalized specific parameters. In addition, FedPDA uses domestic encryption standards SM2 and SM3 to ensure the security and integrity of flight data. The experimental results show that FedPDA can not only effectively protect user privacy and data security, but also significantly improve the stability and efficiency of the heterogeneous flight data.

articleTitle: LCLB: Low Cross-Chain Transaction Ratio and Load Balancing for Blockchain Sharding
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As blockchain technology becomes widely applied, handling high volumes of transactions has become a critical challenge. Sharding has emerged as an effective solution to enhance the throughput of blockchain systems. Yet, this approach introduces challenges related to the frequency of cross-shard transactions and workload balancing. High rates of cross-shard transactions can slow overall processing speed and reduce throughput, while uneven load distribution can overburden some shards and underutilize others, impacting overall efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a sharding method named LCLB. This method employs the concept of label propagation to pre-shard accounts with frequent transactions into a designated shard, ensuring a lower ratio of cross-shard transactions. It also uses an elastic load balancing algorithm to dynamically adjust the distribution of accounts, ensuring a relatively balanced processing load across all shards. Our results indicate that LCLB significantly enhances blockchain sharding performance,not only enhancing transaction throughput but also significantly reducing transaction confirmation latency, while ensuring a balanced load across various shards.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interactive Elderly Care System: Enhancing Emotional and Physical Well-being through the Pepper robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study addresses the growing challenges of traditional elderly care models in meeting the diverse needs of the aging population by presenting a human-computer interactive elderly care system based on the Pepper robot. The system integrates advanced technologies, including voice recognition, emotion analysis, and intelligent life assistance, to provide key functionalities such as daily companionship through voice communication and emotion recognition, real-time weather and solar term updates for personalized clothing and dietary recommendations, and health-promoting activities like Baduanjin and Tai Chi exercises. These modules work together to enhance emotional well-being and daily comfort for elderly individuals, offering a comprehensive and efficient solution to modern elderly care. The results demonstrate the system's potential to significantly improve the quality of life for seniors, providing an innovative approach to address the evolving needs of elderly care in an aging society.

articleTitle: Galaxy Morphology Semantic Segmentation Based on K-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: At present, modern large-scale astronomical observation equipment can collect a large number of high-resolution images. Astronomy has entered the era of big data. Deep learning has shown great potential in astronomical image analysis due to its powerful feature extraction and segmentation capabilities. In the study of galaxy evolution, image segmentation can separate different parts of galaxies, help identify the types of galaxies and analyze structural details, which is crucial to understanding the formation and evolution of galaxies. Therefore, this paper proposes a galaxy morphology segmentation method based on K-Net. The experimental data comes from the Galaxy Zoo project, and the model is trained using strategies such as transfer learning. The trained model can be used to segment four common galaxy images. The experimental results show that the overall accuracy reaches 97.11%, and the mean intersection over union is also 80.87%, indicating that the model performs well in the segmentation of astronomical images. The mean accuracy and the mean dice coefficient are both higher than 87%, indicating that the model is stable in distinguishing different categories. Therefore, K-Net has great application potential in astronomical image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: A new perspective on face detection utilizing language modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Most traditional face detection models rely heavily on manually designed prior knowledge. Moreover, for other related facial visual tasks (such as facial attribute analysis, facial pose estimation, etc.) may require additional models or complex integrations. Based on the generalized features of Pix2Seq for visual tasks, this paper studies its application in face detection, thus providing a universal language interface for facial visual tasks. We define face detection as a language modeling task based on pixel input. In order to speed up the training data, we used DETR model code to implement the Pix2Seq model algorithm for transforming from image to sequence, and add data augmentations. To further compress the model and reduce the computational load, we choose to delete the FFN. By training Pix2Seq on the large-scale WIDER Face dataset, we report the latest results on the WIDER Face validation set.

articleTitle: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks with Coordinate Attention for Human Activity Recognition in Manufacturing Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In today's rapidly advancing manufacturing industrial landscape, the application of wearable sensor-based human activity recognition (HAR) technology has become essential for enhancing productivity, ensuring safety, and optimizing human-machine collaboration. However, extracting robust feature from wearable sensing data that is multi-positional presents significant challenges, due to the implicit and disordered correlations among data from different locations. Considering graph neural networks (GNNs) could represent data in structured graph format and uncover complex relationships with message passing between graph nodes, a novel human activity recognition strategy based on dynamic graph neural networks and coordinate attention mechanism is proposed, which uses a dynamic graph mechanism to capture the associations between different time slots and extracts spatial-temporal features from multi-dimensional data, utilizing the coordinate attention mechanism. Experiments are conducted on the public OPPORTUNITY HAR dataset and a self-constructed worker activity dataset in manufacturing industry (WAMID), the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed dynamic graph neural network with coordinate attention (CA-DGNN) achieves a more competitive classification accuracy than other existing HAR deep learning-based models.

articleTitle: Propagation trend deduction model of major health emergencies in megacities based on Attention-Bi-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the continuous outbreak of major health incidents in megacities, China 's epidemic prevention and control has entered a new stage, facing new situations and new tasks. In order to effectively grasp the trend of public health events in the new stage, this study introduces a deep learning model to build a public health event trend prediction model. Firstly, a multivariate data set that conforms to the trend of virus evolution in the new stage of epidemic prevention is established. Then, the data were preprocessed by principal component analysis, normalization and other methods. After that, a variety of prediction models are built based on deep learning frameworks such as long-term and shortterm memory neural networks to compare the prediction effects, and the attention mechanism is increased to improve the prediction effect of the model. Finally, MSE and R 2 score are used to evaluate the effect of the model. Studies have shown that conventional environmental factors such as temperature and weather cannot be the eigenvalues of the trend prediction model, and the number of infections at the previous time step can more effectively predict the trend of viral infection. The prediction effect of the 'Attention-Bi-LSTM' model is significantly better than other machine learning and deep learning algorithms. The MSE is 0.014, and the R2 score is 0.560. The predicted number of new infections basically fits the real value.

articleTitle: Prediction of Insider Trading Behaviours through Highly Interconnected Core People Network with Graph Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study investigates the potential of graph-based machine learning to enhance the detection and understanding of trading by insiders, encompassing both legal and potentially illicit activities. Given the complex and interconnected nature of financial markets, insider trading poses a significant challenge to market fairness and resource allocation efficiency. This research employs Graph Convolutional Networks to model insider trading within a network constructed from shared board memberships among S&P 500 companies. By integrating both historical stock prices and board interlocks, GCNs offer a comprehensive perspective to uncover subtle interactions leading to insider trading behaviours. The study aims to demonstrate the superiority of GCNs over traditional models on predicting the tendency of insider trading by conducting rigorous ablation studies and benchmark comparisons, which assess the impact of feature removal, edge deletion, and edge rewiring on model performance. These results demonstrate the potential benefits of graph-based methods for financial applications such as market regulation and monitoring.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Elderly-oriented Pharmaceutical APP Based on Artificial Intelligence Background
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Nowadays, all kinds of cell phone APPs are actively exploring the development of aging-adapted versions to meet the needs of elderly users. Based on understanding the behavioral characteristics and psychological features of elderly users, this paper explores the aging-adapted design of pharmaceutical APP through the analysis of actual cases, and optimizes the color scheme, fonts, interface layout, etc., so as to make it easy for elderly users to operate; And more aging-friendly functions are added in the APP to meet the deep needs of elderly users, so that the elderly can experience the convenience brought by artificial intelligence technology, and at the same time, it provides certain reference and help for the aging-friendly design of medicine APP in the context of the artificial intelligence era.

articleTitle: Real-time Frequency Offset Estimation and Demodulation Method of DroneID Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The DroneID signal transmitted by drones carries important information, including real-time coordinate position and ID serial number of the drone and controller. In recent years, adequate reception and demodulation of these signals have become focal points in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) monitor research. The actual DroneID signals exhibit low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and substantial frequency offsets, leading conventional demodulation techniques to suffer from low estimation accuracy of frequency offset and operational failure under significant frequency offset. This results in prolonged demodulation delays, high frame loss rates and high bit error rates (BER). This paper analyzes the time-frequency characteristics of DroneID signals, and proposes a novel frequency offset estimation and demodulation approach based on parallel streaming processing. By employing high-processing gain symbol for frequency offset measurement and executing frequency offset calculation and demodulation in parallel, real-time streaming processing is achieved, enhancing the accuracy of frequency offset estimation and the responsiveness of demodulation across frames. Simulation results demonstrate that under conditions of SNR at -14dB and frequency offset of 8kHz, the proposed method achieves frequency offset estimation accuracy of 1kHz, satisfying real-time demodulation needs for low SNR and large frequency offset signals.

articleTitle: Prior Enhanced Diffusion Model for Low Light Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Low-light image enhancement is a critical challenge in computer vision, particularly in applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and photography. Traditional enhancement techniques often fail to preserve details and colors in poorly illuminated images. In this paper, we propose a novel diffusion models based method enhanced with effective prior for low light image enhancement. Specifically, observing the underlying structures instead of pure noise in low-light images, we first remove the strong Gaussian noise limits in each diffusion step to reserve the details. Second, to ensure the overall color consistence,a 3-channel Color Map is involved to provide essential intensity information. Our experiments reveal that removing Gaussian noise limits from model output during training significantly enhances the model’s ability to restore low-light images, demonstrating that excluding noise allows for sharper and more accurate restorations. Our findings indicate that such prior can boost the diffusion model and yield superior performance across multiple evaluation metrics. This work offers valuable insights for optimizing preprocessing techniques in diffusion-based models for low-light image enhancement, paving the way for improved real-world applications.

Author Keywords: removing Gaussian noise limits from model

articleTitle: An Automatic Control Method for the Number of Simulation Experiments based on Multi-variable Steady-state Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Different experiment times for the same simulation experiment affect the validity of the experimental results. In this paper, the basic principle of Monte Carlo method for determining simulation times is introduced, and its limitations in large-scale combat scenarios are analyzed. Then, a steady-state analysis method of variables is proposed, which takes the core index concerned by experiment-personnel as the investigation variable and passes normality test and significance analysis. In addition, the overall structure of automatic control of simulation experiment times is designed and the effectiveness of this method is verified. For the application scenarios where a large number of simulation experiment schemes need to be deduced, this method can realize unattended, and can greatly improve the experimental efficiency while ensuring the effectiveness of experimental results.

articleTitle: Boosting Adversarial Robustness through Channel Adversarial Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Adversarial attacks have become a significant challenge for deep learning models, especially in resource-constrained environments. While adversarial training (AT) has proven effective for improving robustness, it often suffers from limited applicability to smaller models due to their computational constraints. Recently, adversarial distillation has emerged as a promising approach to transfer robustness from large teacher models to smaller student models. However, existing adversarial distillation methods often focus on logits-level distillation and overlook the importance of intermediate layer features. In this paper, we propose a novel method called Channel Adversarial Robustness Distillation (CARD) which attempts to identify the vital knowledge against adversarial threats through channel distillation. CARD leverages feature alignment at the channel level between the teacher and student models, utilizing 1x1 convolutions to ensure compatibility in feature map dimensions. We introduce Channel Distillation Loss (CD), which computes the divergence between aligned feature maps, and incorporate adaptive KL divergence for the upper bound of prediction discrepancy. The experimental results demonstrate that CARD effectively enhances adversarial robustness while maintaining high accuracy, offering a balanced approach to model distillation. Our method provides a promising direction for improving the robustness of student models in adversarial settings.

articleTitle: Text Classification of Sudden Public Health Events Based on Abstracts of Scientific Papers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this study, text analysis techniques are used to explore the abstracts of papers in the field of public health emergencies, with the aim of accurately capturing the research dynamics and directions in this field and providing rich references for researchers. In this paper, we first use Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) to explore the 10 topics corresponding to the relevant literature, and classify the literature based on the topics. At the same time, considering the randomness of the LDA model parameters, this study incorporates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to obtain a new hybrid model to improve the accuracy and stability of text classification, and finally the model obtains 15 topics and discusses the evolution of the research topics of the literature in this field in the past 20 years, which still has great prospects for development in the future.

articleTitle: Automatic Decision-Making for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Operation Based on CNN-RF Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Automatic decision-making is crucial for the autonomous operation of unmanned surface vehicles, especially in effectively utilizing multi-source information for dynamic strategy selection. In this paper, we propose a CNN-RF hybrid model for unmanned surface vehicle operations. This model integrates CNN’s feature learning with RF’s nonlinear classification for comprehensive multi-source data modeling. Our approach includes meteorological data alongside state and obstacle information, enhancing decision-making reliability. Comparative simulations with traditional methods demonstrate that our model accurately predicts collision risks and performs effective avoidance, ensuring efficient navigation in complex environments.

articleTitle: Long short-term memory assisted FIR filter for tracking human upper limb motion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To better correct the spatial trajectory of human motion, this paper proposes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-assisted correction algorithm for the Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter, aimed at improving the accuracy of human joint motion capture based on inertial sensors. In the proposed algorithm, the forward data is obtained from the backward-updated data smoothed by the Rauch-Tung-Striebel (RTS) smoother and compared with the forward-predicted data from the FIR. The resulting error is input into the pre-trained LSTM model to predict the error data, and the backward data at that moment is updated, making the positional information more accurate. This calculation shows significant effectiveness when estimating the elbow data. In the experiment, the data obtained using the LSTM-assisted FIR filter showed a 35.83% improvement compared to the data obtained with the LSTM-assisted Kalman Filter.

articleTitle: A Robust Specific Emitter Identification Method Based on Frequency-Domain Amplitude Mixing for Enhanced Domain Generalization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Specific emitter identification (SEI) leverages the inherent features of radio frequency signals to identify individual emitters.Recent progress in deep learning (DL) based SEI has significantly improved wireless device identification. However, real-world electromagnetic signals fluctuate due to varying channel conditions and time, resulting in poor performance for conventional models in unseen channels. To address this domain generalization challenge, we propose a robust SEI method based on frequency-domain augmentation, termed frequency-domain amplitude mixing (FAM). FAM applies a Fourier transform to the signal, interpolates and mixes the amplitude in the frequency domain, introduces phase perturbations, and then reconstructs the signal using an inverse Fourier transform. This augmentation generates diverse training samples, enabling the model to capture a broader range of features and improve generalization. We validate the effectiveness of FAM on a multi-domain dataset covering different time periods and receivers. Experimental results demonstrate that FAM achieves an average recognition accuracy of 80.67% on unseen domains, significantly outperforming existing domain generalization methods and highlighting its robustness in SEI tasks.

articleTitle: A New Path Planning Algorithm for Marine Engine Room Inspection Based on RA*-ADWA*
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Path planning plays a key role in robotic inspection, especially on ships. Previous research does not consider the unique terrain condition of the engine room, such as ladder steps and narrow areas, which greatly influence the walking efficiency of robots. In addition, how to realize path correction when the direction is deviated due to bumps caused by waves remains to be explored. Therefore, the RA*-ADWA algorithm combined by global and local planning is proposed in this paper, which provides a new idea for inspection in multi-terrain environment of the marine engine room. The globally optimal path(GOP) is obtained by adding terrain factors and using the rectangular safety frame filtering (RSF) method proposed in this paper. And local path planning realizes adaptive path correction by calculating the data from environmental information and introducing the distance loss function on the basis of the GOP. The method demonstrates superior performance compared to other traditional methods in terms of path length, path angle, efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: Named Entity Recognition of E-commerce Texts Fusing Large Language Models and Lexical Knowledge
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that Chinese e-commerce text data set covers many fields and various kinds, this paper constructs a synonym table combined with the powerful information search and learning ability of large language model, and carries out data enhancement by randomly replacing the synonym text in the text of the data set, which makes the data set more rich. In addition, a LE-Roberta-wwm-BiLSTM-CRF model integrating vocabulary information is proposed. First, word information related to each word vector is fused into the pretraining model Roberta-wwm-ext-large, so that full and effective learning and training can be carried out in the pre-training stage. The feature is extracted by BiLSTM, and the conditional random field model (CRF) is usedto calculate the conditional probability and optimize the output, so as to improve the accuracy of e- commerce text named entity recognition. The experimental results show that the comprehensive accuracy, recall rate and F1 of the proposed method are 90.64%, 92.11% and 91.36%, respectively, which proves that the proposed method can better improve the named entity recognition accuracy of Chinese e-commerce texts.

articleTitle: Accurate Parameter Estimation Based on the Two-Sided KZ Filter in Low Signal-to-Noise Ratio Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: System identification is the process of developing models based on data collected from dynamic systems. A significant challenge in this field is accurately estimating model parameters using input-output data. This data, typically gathered through sensors, often contains noise due to inaccuracies in the sensors and errors during communication.
