The presence of such noise can lead to biased estimates of parameters, which undermines the model’s effectiveness. While traditional methods strive to minimize this bias during parameter estimation, they frequently encounter difficulties when dealing with high levels of noise. An alternative strategy involves employing filtering techniques to clean the data before estimation takes place. Low-pass (LP) filters are designed to reduce frequencies above a specific threshold and are widely used for mitigating noise issues. Among these filters, the Kolmogorov–Zurbenko (KZ) filter operates as multiple iterations of a moving average (MA) filter and has shown strong capabilities in reducing noise; it is commonly applied in high-resolution signal analysis and image processing tasks. In this study, we introduce two KZ filtering approaches aimed at denoising data prior to parameter estimation. Theoretical evaluations and experimental findings indicate that the proposed KZ filtering method surpasses LP filters and wavelet denoising techniques, particularly in environments characterized by low Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR).

articleTitle: Path planning of inventory UAV based on adaptive fireworks algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This article focuses on the problem of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning in inventory counting. Considering the flying environment area, the UAV trajectory planning model under multiple constraint conditions is established with the goal of minimizing the total cost of trajectory length, yaw angle cost, and obstacle threat cost. An adaptive fireworks algorithm (AFWA) has been proposed. An adaptive explosion radius transformation strategy is proposed for fireworks with different adaptations. An elite Gaussian substitution selection method is designed to avoid the algorithm falling into local optimality. In the trajectory planning problem of UAVs in smart inventory, by simulating the explosion process of fireworks, the algorithm can continuously generate new solutions and quickly approximate the global optimal solution. The comparison results show that the adaptive fireworks algorithm has great advantages in convergence speed, solution efficiency and robustness, and can optimize the UAV inventory path, improve inventory efficiency and accuracy, and reduce flight time and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Research on multiple loading method for cigarette boxes loading machine
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In tobacco industry, using robots to replace manual loading operations has become a focused issue. Varieties of loading machines in research can only implement simple loading methods, which are difficult to meet the actual needs in tobacco industry. In response to the above problems, a cigarette boxes loading machine using two articulated robots as robotic arms was developed. Through the design, development, experimental research and loading tests, the loading machine, can realize multiple loading method and mixed loading method of cigarette boxes of various specifications. This research has significantly improved the dexterity and flexibility of the cigarette boxes loading machine, which can meet the technical requirements for loading machine in tobacco industry.

articleTitle: Research on tree species identification method based on YOLOv8 and visible light images
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the field of forest resource management and biodiversity surveys, traditional manual survey methods are gradually being replaced by efficient automated technologies. This study utilizes UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) visible light imagery to investigate the effectiveness of the YOLOv8 model in classifying tree species in natural forests. The research focuses on the natural secondary forest in Mao'ershan Forest Farm, constructing a dataset of seven tree species. Subsequently, a tree species instance segmentation model was established based on the YOLOv8 algorithm to segment tree crowns and predict tree species. By optimizing strategies and analyzing convergence, Radam was identified as the optimal optimizer, with the model converging after 200 training epochs and achieving an mAP50 of 89.6%. In summary, this study proposes a novel method for tree species recognition based on UAV visible light imagery combined with the YOLOv8 network. Using the tree species identification in the natural secondary forest of Mao'ershan Forest Farm as an example, the validity of the instance segmentation model was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Emotion-Aware Systems for Hazardous Operations: Integrating Mobile Sensors with LLM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study proposes a mobile device sensor-based emotion sensing system for hazard-involved operational action environments. In this study, the system utilizes accelerometers and gyroscopes on mobile devices for actor gait data acquisition. The obtained gait data is classified using an artificial intelligence algorith to classify the emotional state of the operator. At the same time, the system combines the gestures recognized by the sensors to identify critical operations, and combines the generative large language model (LLM) to provide personalized reminders and safety recommendations in high-risk operations. Through data analysis, the prediction accuracy of the regression model reaches 68% in anxiety, anger or relaxation, real-time safety reminders based on emotional state. Edge computing-based processing analyzes sensor data in real-time and combines emotions and actions to generate adaptive reminder content. This approach demonstrates the potential to develop low-cost, real-time methods for monitoring an individual’s mental health using LLMs.

articleTitle: Research on the Dynamic Modeling and Fuzzy Control Strategy of cable-Driven Parallel Cleaning Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The surface of a ship's hull is prone to the attachment of marine organisms and other contaminants. If not cleaned regularly, this can lead to increased sailing resistance and fuel consumption, thereby reducing the ship's energy efficiency. Manual cleaning faces issues such as long cleaning times and operational hazards, resulting in significant time and labor costs. To tackle this issue, The present study presents a cable-driven cleaning robot, which incorporates a cable-driven parallel robot as its fundamental framework, along with a high-pressure water jet serving as the actuator, thereby creating a hybrid robotic system. First, the dynamic model of this system is established using the Lagrangian method. Building on this model, a Fuzzy-PID control strategy is proposed, enabling accurate trajectory tracking. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, numerical simulations are performed as a final step. The outcomes of the simulation indicate that, when contrasted with the conventional PID control approach, the proposed Fuzzy-PID control strategy significantly improves control accuracy and exhibits superior performance in terms of stability. The cable-driven cleaning robot and its control strategy presented in this paper offer a theoretical basis and practical support for applications in the domain of ship cleaning. Since the system uses only four cables to actuate the robot in the plane, we establish a planar coordinate system (xoy), where the y-axis represents the error and the x-axis represents time.

articleTitle: Automated Adaptive Navigation Leveraging Natural Language Models in Aerospace Robotics System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Vision-based obstacle detection in the space environment is a fundamental task for aerospace devices to differentiate between semantically altered and unaltered regions. Large language models (LLMs) have been utilized in various domains for their exceptional feature extraction capabilities and have shown promise in numerous downstream applications. In this study, we harness the power of a pre-trained LLM, extracting feature maps from extensive datasets and employing an auxiliary network to detect changes for aerospace device. Unlike existing LLM-based change detection methods that solely focus on deriving high-quality feature maps, our approach emphasizes the manipulation of these feature maps to enhance semantic relevance.

articleTitle: An anti-swing control method for crane robot with liquid container lifting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The sloshing of liquid in containers being lifted by crane robots presents a serious safety hazard. To effectively suppress liquid sloshing during the lifting process, a sliding mode control method is proposed in this paper. An equivalent dynamic model of the crane robot lifting liquid containers is developed based on a mass-spring system. A sliding mode surface is constructed that incorporates the coupling of trolley displacement, payload swing angle, and liquid sloshing displacement. The sliding mode control law is derived, and the stability of the closed-loop system is analyzed. The simulation results have demonstrated the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Design of guidance law for hypersonic drone based on trajectory profile
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this paper, longitudinal and transverse lateral guidance methods are proposed to solve the trajectory tracking problem of hypersonic drone during the return of the energy management segment. A three-degree-of-freedom particle model of a hypersonic drone was established, and the longitudinal and transverse lateral guidance laws were designed to guide the drone to track the longitudinal and transverse trajectory profiles, so that it could reach the landing window with the desired energy state. Finally, the three-degree-of-freedom model is used to simulate and analyze the guidance law.

articleTitle: MATeacher: Multi-scale Views Learning and Adaptive Unsupervised Weight for Semi-supervised Pest Region Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Agricultural production is extremely important, yet it also faces the challenges posed by pests. Object detection techniques based on deep learning have shown promise, but the lack of annotated data has limited their performance. And the general semi-supervised object detection framework cannot achieve good performance in pest detection scenarios due to the small, complex, and dense nature of pests. To solve these problems, MATeacher is put forward in this paper. Based on the characteristics of pest regions, Multi-scale Views Learning (MSVL) is introduced for joint consistency training from features of high and low resolution views. We also consider the information of different datasets and different stages of the model from an overall perspective. Through the Adaptive Unsupervised Weighting (AUW), we generate the unsupervised loss coefficient, avoiding inefficient and cumbersome manual design. The experiment on the corn borer dataset shows that our method can get an mAP of 68.2 using just 20% supervised data, 6.7 higher than the supervised baseline. Compared with all the state-of-theart (SOTA) models in comparison, MATeacher performs better. Also, compared to the fully supervised baseline, our method achieves around 93% of its performance with only 20% supervised data, almost matching full supervision. MATeacher provides an effective solution to the lack of annotated data in the task of pest region detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical Image Super-Resolution with GANs and Residual Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Medical image super-resolution is crucial for improving the quality of MRI scans, aiding better diagnosis and analysis. In this paper, we propose an enhanced super-resolution approach based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) that incorporates residual attention mechanisms and perceptual loss functions to achieve high-quality image reconstruction. Specifically, we employ Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks within the generator network to improve feature learning and integrate perceptual and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) losses to enhance perceptual and structural quality. Experiments on the IXI MRI dataset demonstrate significant improvements over the baseline SRGAN, achieving a PSNR gain of 2.17 dB and an SSIM improvement of 0.062. Our approach effectively enhances visual fidelity and diagnostic relevance in reconstructed MRI images.

articleTitle: Ice cover thickness detection based on CEEMDAN-WOA-BILSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a transmission line ice cover thickness prediction model based on CEEMDAN-WOA-BILSTM.the bidirectional long and short-term memory network (BILSTM) is used to establish a prediction model to make use of the information provided by the past and future at each point in time in the process, and the WOA algorithm is added to carry out optimisation, avoiding falling into the local optimal solution as well as reducing the errors caused by human intervention, and improving the accuracy of the ice cover thickness detection. The accuracy of ice cover thickness detection is improved and the model is finally validated by experimental results.

Author Keywords: bi-directional long and short-term memory network

articleTitle: Synchronous Control of Bilateral Teleoperation under Hybrid Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The wide prospect of bilateral teleoperation system in various practical applications has attracted many researchers to study its control methods. This scholarly work addresses the control challenges inherent to bilateral teleoperation systems subjected to hybrid cyber-attacks. A model is developed to describe the working state of a bilateral remote operating system, taking into account the impact of denial of service (DoS) attacks and false data injection (FDI) attacks that exist with probability. An adaptive controller is designed to mitigate issues arising from data loss due to DoS attacks and packet tampering resulting from FDI attacks. When an adversary launches an attack, there will be DoS or FDI attacks in the channel of a communication network Therefore, this paper uses Bernoulli component to model the attack situation of the system. By utilizing the Lyapunov functional methodology, a criterion for global asymptotic stability is established, thereby substantiating that the master-slave system is capable of attaining global asymptotic synchronization. Finally, by selecting a manipulator system for numerical simulation, the effectiveness of the control strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Research on multi-node gait information acquisition system and time synchronization based on BLE
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Gait information is critical in various domains. However, achieving accurate time synchronization across multiple sensor nodes in wireless systems remains a challenge, particularly in gait information acquisition, where precise data alignment is essential. Current solutions are limited by high power consumption, system complexity, and transmission instability. This study proposes a multi-node gait information acquisition system incorporating a six-axis inertial sensor and a plantar pressure sensor, with the ESP32 serving as the core processing unit. The system utilizes the low-power Bluetooth protocol for real-time data transmission. To address the issue of time desynchronization, we introduce an average error-based time synchronization algorithm. The algorithm was tested in an experimental setup using a signal generator, two gait systems, and a mobile device. The results demonstrate that the average error method effectively estimates and corrects frequency drift, significantly reducing time synchronization errors. The system offers a low-power, high-precision solution for multi-node gait information acquisition, advancing the accuracy of gait data fusion and analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Gesture Recognition Algorithms Based on Electromyographic Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the advancement of myoelectric control technology, surface electromyography (sEMG) signals have been widely applied in prosthesis control. However, effectively decoding movement intentions remains a challenge, making the construction of intention recognition models a critical issue. This study proposes combining the transient trigonometric Harris Hawks optimizer (TTHHO) with a radial basis function (RBF) network to build a gesture recognition model. Five hand gestures were collected from ten volunteers using a self-developed acquisition board, and the performance of the proposed model was compared with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), support vector machine (SVM), and K-nearest neighbor (KNN) models. The results show that the proposed model achieved an average recognition accuracy of 87.54%, which is 14% to 16% higher than the other three models, with a maximum accuracy of 92.47%.

articleTitle: Semantic-Guided Pruning Approach for Large Language Model-based Class-Level Code Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Recent advancements in code generation from natural language have been driven by large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 and WizardCoder, but current methods often underutilize their capabilities, especially for class-level code generation. The ClassEval benchmark addresses this by focusing on longer, more complex code snippets, but LLMs face challenges with input length constraints. Traditional approaches like zero-shot and few-shot learning struggle with the complexity and length of class-level code, limiting their effectiveness. To overcome this, we propose a semantic-guided pruning method, which optimizes input length through coarse- and fine-grained pruning, retaining only the most semantically relevant tokens. Our method improves LLM performance, increasing pass@1 accuracy by over 4% on the ClassEval benchmark.

articleTitle: Research on Multi object Occlusion Tracking and Trajectory Prediction Method Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of multi-target occlusion tracking and trajectory prediction in complex scenes, an ensemble method based on deep reinforcement learning is designed. By constructing three core modules of occlusion detection, deep reinforcement learning tracking, and trajectory prediction, and utilizing spatiotemporal feature fusion and attention mechanisms to achieve multi module collaboration. The experiment was conducted on datasets such as MOT17 and MOT20, and the results showed that the proposed method had significantly better target recovery ability and trajectory prediction accuracy in occluded states than traditional methods. The accuracy of multi-target tracking was improved by 12.3%, and the overlap of long-term trajectory prediction was increased to 0.72, verifying the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method in complex dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Temporal Alignment of Multi-Dimensional Asynchronous Data for Digital Twin Evolutionary Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Digital twin technology is widely used in smart industries and other fields. However, analyzing its evolution in complex scenarios faces challenges in collecting and merging data, particularly in achieving precise data time alignment. Existing methods often struggle with diverse data types and frequencies. This paper introduces a new method for aligning multi-dimensional asynchronous data in digital twin evolution analysis. This approach ensures time alignment and frequency consistency through techniques such as filling null values, intelligent interpolation, and resampling. Key contributions include BiLSTM-based interpolation and flexible adjustment of data granularity. These advancements effectively address the challenge of data time alignment in digital twin evolution analysis, thereby improving data quality and alignment accuracy. The proposed method supports reliable data processing for tasks such as anomaly detection, accelerated evolution, and decision-making. Experimental results demonstrate its capability to recover data with severely damaged features, thereby advancing digital twin evolution analysis in complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Power line detection method based on hybrid attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) play an important role in modern technology, especially in inspecting power lines and acquiring aerial imagery. Their flexibility and high adaptability make them ideal for these tasks. Although drones can capture large amounts of aerial image data, accurately detecting power lines within them is not easy. To solve the problem of power line detection, a novel solution is proposed: using a multi-scale U-shaped network model that incorporates a dual attention mechanism. Our design fully takes into account the complexity of the power line detection task and adopts a multi-level processing method to improve the accuracy of identification. The designed model includes an encoder and two decoders. The use of this structure helps to make fuller use of feature information. The encoder is responsible for converting the input image into a high-level abstract feature representation, while the decoder is responsible for mapping these features back to the original image space to achieve accurate localization and identification of power lines. In order to solve the problem of feature space information loss that may be caused by continuous downsampling, this model introduces two independent attention mechanisms, channel and space. This design can effectively compensate for the detailed information lost due to downsampling, thereby improving the ability to accurately extract power line boundaries. After a series of experiments, it has been proved that this method can achieve certain advantages.

articleTitle: Research on Visual Localization of the Pallet Relative to the AGV Based on Image Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In factory environments, although laser radar is widely used for AGV navigation, when pallets are being forked, due to the position error of the pallets, visual localization of the pallets relative to the AGV is still required when the AGV navigates to the vicinity of the pallets. In this paper, the visual localization of the pallet relative to the AGV is carried out based on the extraction and matching of ORB feature points and the pose optimization based on the Gauss-Newton method. The main research includes the following aspects: first, the AGV and the pallet are adjusted to the standard position in advance, the standard RGB image and depth image are taken, and the realtime acquired image in operation and standard RGB image are used for ORB feature points extraction. Next, brute-force matching was used to establish the initial matching among the extracted feature points, and the coarse and fine matching of feature points was carried out according to the Grid-based Motion Statistics (GMS) algorithm and the RANSAC algorithm to remove the mismatched points. Finally, the 3D positions of feature points in the standard RGB image and the feature points in the real-time image are paired to form 3D-2D point pairs. The current precise pose of the pallet relative to the AGV is determined by the Gauss-Newton method based on the reprojection error minimization. Experimental results suggest that the method proposed in this paper attains good localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Slave-Core Parallel Implementation of Two-Dimensional Coupled Markov Chains on Shenwei Processors
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The SW26010 pro processor on the new-generation Shenwei supercomputer is fundamentally different from ordinary commercial processors in that it adopts a master-slave heterogeneous multi-core hardware architecture, and almost all of the processor's computational performance comes from the slave core arrays. Therefore, if we use only MPI for parallelization at the task level and a simple compile-and-run porting approach, where only the master cores in each core group are involved in the task and the slave cores are left idle, this makes the Shenwei processor indistinguishable from the average commercial processor. In this paper, we first further understand the tasks to be processed, then partition them, and finally optimize the parallelization strategy according to the task characteristics to further partition the tasks that are computed on the master cores, so that each slave core is involved in the task and the full computational performance of the processor is exploited.

articleTitle: Intelligent tracking system based on composite algorithm fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In today's social rapid development of science and technology environment, for autonomy and efficiency of artificial intelligence has become very important, in order to promote the future more people for the convenience of artificial intelligence on the tracking, and with the complexity of the application scenario and variability, especially in the dynamic obstacle and unknown environment path tracking, in the autonomous tracking algorithm needs a highly flexible, fast general algorithm. At this time, the memory enhancement path optimization algorithm (memory enhancement path finding algorithm, MEPA) can provide a convenient process and idea. Compared with the traditional tracking algorithm, this algorithm is more adaptable to the environment, and the simulation experiment shows that the algorithm can reach a reuse rate of more than 70% after increasing the complexity of the environment. This greatly reduces the time consumption of repeated pathway calculations.

articleTitle: Observability of Two-Time-Scale Multi-Agent Systems with Antagonistic Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the observability of two-time-scale multi-agent systems (MASs), with particular attention to antagonistic interactions among agents. The study begins by modeling the systems, followed by defining observability and establishing its conditions using singular perturbation theory. Numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed conditions.

articleTitle: Task-Oriented Language Grounding for Robot via Learning Object Mask
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: For robots to follow human instructions, it is essential to associate the rich semantic information in human vocabulary, e.g. "pick up the red block" to their sensory observations and actions. This brings up a notably difficult challenge for robots: while current robot learning approaches allow robots to learn different behaviours from observational learning, it is impractical for robots to have experiences that cover all semantic information when faced with variable language instructions. We would enable the robot to perceive and manipulate task objectives and language instructions, even if it has never seen them before. In this paper, we propose a modular system and a FiLM-based language-visual object mask model (LOVM) to extract target masks of task objects from language instructions and images, and execute robotic manipulation strategies from the current image, the instructions and the extracted object information. we evaluate the generalization ability of LOVM for unknown language instructions and task goals using three test sets. Results demonstrate that our approach is effective for a wide range of language instructions, and achieves an average success rate of 92%.

articleTitle: Compressed Image Artifacts Removal with U-Net and Attention Mechanism Net
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Traditional block-based image compression introduces block artifacts. The evolution of deep learning has simplified the process of image artifact removal. However, the diverse quality of compressed images post-compression means that a universal model cannot uniformly enhance image quality. Furthermore, the lack of attention mechanisms in the estimation of image quality leads to inaccuracies. To overcome these challenges, we introduce the U-Net and Attention Mechanism Network (UAMN) for Compressed Image Artifacts Removal. By training a single U-net, we enable blind artifact removal from images. We also incorporate attention mechanisms into our Quantization Parameter (QP) estimation to enhance image quality. Our testing shows a 11.17% performance improvement over traditional JPEG images, effectively upgrading the quality of compressed images.

articleTitle: A Robust and Low-Complexity RF Fingerprinting Method Using Gated Multilayer Perceptron for Cross-Receiver Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) has emerged as a critical technology for the identification and authentication of wireless devices by exploiting the unique hardware-induced characteristics of transmitted signals. In recent years, Deep Learning (DL) has notably enhanced the performance of RFF, but the previously proposed DL-based RFF methods generally suffer from high computational complexity and lack robustness across diverse environments, particularly in cross-receiver scenarios. These limitations hinder their applicability in real-time and resource-constrained systems. To address these challenges, a novel RFF method utilizing a Gated Multilayer Perceptron (gMLP) is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the gMLP integrates gated linear units into the traditional multilayer perceptron. This can enhance information flow management and complex pattern capture at low computational costs, improving performance in cross-receiver scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 91.8% in cross-receiver scenarios, utilizing only 12,000 parameters and an inference time of 5.5 ms. This performance significantly outperforms several baseline models, including convoultion neural network and ResNet.

articleTitle: Optimizing the mathematical model of IoT data processing in smart cities using artificial intelligence algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This article explores how to use artificial intelligence algorithms to optimize the processing of IoT data in smart cities. Firstly, the concepts of artificial intelligence, smart cities, and IoT data processing were introduced; Secondly, the BP algorithm and ant colony algorithm were introduced; Subsequently, taking the optimization of dangerous goods transportation management in smart cities as an example, the most optimized path was explained. The ant colony algorithm simulates the foraging behavior of ants to optimize the search for the optimal path and solution. Therefore, this article proposes a mathematical model that combines BP algorithm and ant colony algorithm for data processing in smart city IoT. By dividing the data into different processing levels, the BP algorithm is used to preprocess and classify the raw data, while the ant colony algorithm is used to find the optimal path and solution during data transmission and storage. This model can improve the speed and accuracy of data processing, providing strong technical support for the construction of smart cities. This study is of great significance for promoting the development of IoT technology in smart cities, providing new ideas and methods for data processing in future smart cities.

articleTitle: Human robot collaborative control of live working robotic arm in substations based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The conventional human-computer cooperative control model of manipulator for live working in substations is often set as basic cooperation, and the control areas often overlap, resulting in a large standard deviation of the final cooperative control. Therefore, the design and practical analysis of human robot collaborative control of live working robotic arm in substations based on deep learning is proposed. According to the current control demand, first calibrate the contact point of the manipulator and calculate the compensation value, set the space trajectory planning, combine the deep learning technology, eliminate the overlapping area at the control point, and build the deep learning substation live working manipulator human-machine cooperative control model, using the admittance collaborative processing to achieve control. The test results show that the standard deviation of collaborative control finally obtained from the in-depth learning of live working robot arm human-machine coordinated control method in this design is relatively small, which indicates that the effect of this design of substation live working robot arm human-machine coordinated control has been significantly improved, the control coverage is large, and has practical application value.

articleTitle: Distributed mccKF based INS/UWB Integrated navigation for quadruped robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to better realize the quadruped robots localization, this paper proposes a combined positioning algorithm based on distributed maximum correntropy Kalman filter(mccKF) and ultra-wideband (UWB) technology for inertial navigation system (INS). The aim is to improve the navigation and positioning accuracy of quadruped robot based on inertial sensors. In this algorithm, the distributed maximum correntropy Kalman filter is used to estimate the position error of INS and UWB. The system parameters are used as the state vector, and the data output of the local mccKF filter is input into the main filter for fusion, and the optimal estimate is given. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme effectively reduces the positioning error.

articleTitle: Design of a Rigid-flexible and Multi-legged Robot Based on a Scorpion Tail Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the past few decades, multi-legged robots have been widely used in agriculture, construction, rescue and other fields for their excellent flexibility and good adaptability. However, for most multi-legged robots, due to the limitation of their materials and layout, they can only complete some simple tasks. According to the physical characteristics of scorpions, this paper studies a rigid-flexible hexapod soft robot, which uses traditional rigid materials as the main trunk and six walking feet. The scorpion tail bionic structure is also used as the end pneumatic soft actuator to adapt to different situations and realize the overall rigid-flexible combination. The robot uses a triangular gait algorithm combined with fuzzy PID for motion control. The Lora module aims to upload the information in the camera module, barometer module and self-developed circuit module to the cloud platform. Meanwhile, issue commands through the cloud platform. Such a structural design innovation enables the robot to have stronger adaptability and flexibility in grasping operation, which provides new insights for their subsequent development.

articleTitle: A Novel Lightweight Hybrid Model for Drone Identification Leveraging RF Fingerprints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As drones become more widely used, effectively identifying and managing various types of drones has become an urgent issue that needs to be addressed. Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) recognition technology can provide a reliable method for identifying drones, helping to prevent the intrusion of unauthorized drones and enhancing the security of airspace management. However, these methods often involve complex models that are difficult to deploy locally. To address this, this paper proposes a lightweight and efficient hybrid model that combines the effective local inductive biases of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with the global modeling capabilities of transformers, achieving a fusion of local and global features. Additionally, we introduced a spectral attention mechanism to enhance useful information in the signal while suppressing noise. Simulation results indicate that our model consistently achieves high recognition accuracy across various distances, with a peak accuracy of 99.11%. Under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions, our model significantly outperforms other models. For instance, at -5dB, our model achieves an impressive recognition accuracy of 81.25%, compared to MobileNetV2’s 57.14%, a difference of nearly 24 percentage points.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Sliding Mode Control for Coal Silo Cleaning Robots Simulation, and Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: During coal mining and storage, significant accumulation of coal dust and chunks often occurs in coal silos, reducing storage capacity and posing safety hazards. The coal silo environment is characterized by confined spaces, complex obstacles, high dust concentration, and significant variations in temperature and humidity, making the cleaning task highly challenging. This necessitates the development of control strategies that are precise, robust, and capable of adapting to complex environments. This paper presents an Adaptive Fuzzy Sliding Mode Controller (AFSMC) that integrates the robustness of sliding mode control with the smoothness of fuzzy control and employs an adaptive mechanism to adjust control parameters in real time. Specifically, AFSMC increases the control gain when encountering significant resistance from coal chunks to ensure sufficient torque for cleaning, and decreases the gain under lighter loads to minimize energy consumption and reduce mechanical fatigue. Simulation results demonstrate that AFSMC achieves high-precision and energy-efficient trajectory tracking, effectively reduces chattering, and significantly enhances overall system performance. This research provides an efficient and robust control solution for coal silo cleaning robots, meeting the demands of dynamic and complex mining environments and advancing intelligent cleaning technology in the coal industry.

articleTitle: Multimodal Fake News Detection Based on TinyBert Pre-Training and BiLSTM-GATV2 Models
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the current situation of large amount of news detection data and complex and variable news features, a multimodal false news detection method based on a lightweight version of pre-trained language model is proposed. Firstly, TinyBERT pretrained model is used to extract news text features; meanwhile, the propagation graph adjacency matrix is constructed to extract user propagation behavior features. Then, BiLSTM captures the forward and backward relationships of the news long text and encodes the news sequences by bi-directional information. Finally, Graph Attention Network v2 is introduced to dynamically adjust the attention weights among users and combine the textual and graph structural information for fake news prediction. The model achieves high accuracy on multiple datasets.

Author Keywords: bi-directional long and short-term memory networks

articleTitle: Research on Commercial Cryptography Large Language Model Based on Retrieval Augmented Generation and Low-Rank Adaptation Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As large language model technology improves by leaps and bounds, artificial intelligence has been initially applied in the field of the law and medical education. However, commercial passwords have not been widely used, resulting in the failure of information security of citizens and enterprises. This paper proposes a large language model of commercial cryptography based on search retrieval augmented generation and low-rank adaptation technology, aiming to improve the application of commercial passwords. The results show that the model is more effective than GPT4 in answering questions in the field of commercial cryptography.

articleTitle: Adaptive Estimation of Observation Noise Covariance using Neural Network in Maximum Correntropy Criterion Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In traditional maximum correntropy criterion extended Kalman filter (mccEKF) algorithms, the observation noise covariance matrix, is usually set as a fixed value. However, in complex environments with non-Gaussian noise, a staticobservation noise covariance matrix may not accurately reflect the dynamic changes in noise characteristics. To address this, neural network can be employed to adaptively estimate observation noise covariance matrix for each point in real-time. By training the neural network to adjust observation noise covariance matrix based on incoming data, the filter’s robustness and accuracy in noisy and uncertain systems can be significantly improved.The findings demonstrate that the suggested approach has significantly better localization accuracy when compared with mccEKF filter.

articleTitle: Improved Trajectory-based LiDAR-INS Hand-Eye Calibration Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Calibration between different sensors is crucial for improving mapping accuracy. Some sensors, such as inertial navigation systems (INS), cannot extract features and rely on motion-based hand-eye calibration to determine their transformation with other sensors. However, existing methods neglect cumulative errors in light detection and ranging (LiDAR) or camera-based mapping and inertial measurement unit (IMU) drift in rotation, degrading calibration accuracy. In this paper, an improved trajectory-based LiDAR-INS hand-eye calibration method is proposed. Firstly, a novel residual that accounts for IMU rotational error is designed, distributing the error across each trajectory vertex. Then, a weight matrix related to the distances between vertices in the trajectory graph is introduced, assigning higher weights to vertices with loop closure relationships. Finally, the proposed calibration method is validated on our self-collected data sequences. Experiments show that the proposed method outperforms the baseline, with an average loss of 0.0112 per vertex across four sequences. In addition, the method converges in an average of 22 iterations across these sequences, enabling real-time computation.

articleTitle: Med-Chat: Tuning ChatGLM3-6B with Chinese Medical Dialogue
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant success across a range of natural language processing tasks in general-purpose domains. However, due to limited specialized knowledge, LLMs sometimes generate responses that inaccurately represent medical facts, commonly referred to as hallucinations. Hallucinations provide possible hazards while using LLM in a medical context, including the possibility of misdiagnosis. To address this issue, we utilize the publicly available medical dialogue dataset DISC-Med-SFT, fine-tune the general model ChatGLM3-6B employing the LoRA method, and construct a dedicated medical knowledge base to provide a reliable source of information. Additionally, cascade deduplication is applied to the model’s generated responses to further enhance accuracy and consistency. Experimental results indicate that, compared to the baseline model ChatGLM3-6B, Med-Chat shows notable improvements in both BLEU and F1 score metrics. The resulting Chinese medical LLM, Med-Chat, demonstrates the capability to produce accurate, coherent responses and possesses fundamental medical question-answering skills.

articleTitle: Lightweight Two-Stream Convolution-Augmented Transformer for Multi-Task Human Activity Recognition Using Wi-Fi Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid growth of smart cities and smart homes, indoor human activity recognition (HAR) has become a critical technology for applications in security, health monitoring, and smart home automation. This paper introduces a lightweight and efficient HAR method based on Channel State Information (CSI) from Wi-Fi signals, utilizing the LTHAT network, a simplified yet powerful model optimized for resource-constrained environments. The proposed approach employs a modified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture with reduced computational complexity, featuring an adaptive attention mechanism and Gaussian encoding module for multi-label activity recognition. By leveraging the reduced attention heads and simplified encoder layers of LTHAT, we enhance the model’s performance in multi-user settings while maintaining accuracy and efficiency. Extensive experiments on the WiMANS dataset show that the LTHAT network outperforms conventional models, offering superior accuracy and real-time performance suitable for deployment on edge devices and IoT sensors. This work presents a scalable, practical solution for real-time HAR applications in smart environments.

articleTitle: Design and Traversability Analysis of A Tracked Pipeline Cleaning Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To ensure the drainage efficiency of urban sewer systems, a tracked pipeline cleaning robot is designed. The required driving force for the robot is calculated, and its traversability in pipelines is studied, focusing mainly on its performance in curved pipes and those with obstacles. The analysis includes the geometric constraints and motion characteristics of the robot in bends. The structural design is focused on the required functions of the robot, analyzing the characteristics of its walking diameter-changing mechanism and cleaning device. Finally, ADAMS virtual software and a physical prototype are used to simulate and test the robot’s traversability in pipelines, followed by comparative data analysis to draw conclusions. The results indicate that the robot can successfully turn by utilizing the speed difference between the inner and outer tracks and overcome obstacles with a maximum height of 9mm. During this process, the springs deform according to specific conditions, ensuring the robot can smoothly navigate obstacles and turns.

articleTitle: Mechanical arm assembly based on OpenMV visual perception and the 51 SCM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With OpenMV as the core component and 51 single-chip microcomputer as the control core, we carried out a deep research on autonomous grasping technology of robot arm. In this research project, we mainly use OpenMV camera to visually identify the weight of the object. In this way, the robot arm can accurately identify the weight of the object. At the same time, we use 51 single-chip microcomputer as the control core, responsible for the robot arm for precise operation control, so as to achieve accurate grasp of the object and precise positioning.In the course of research, we firstly expatiate on the working mechanism of robot arm, including the motion principle of each joint and how to realize accurate grasping through control algorithm. Then, we design the OpenMV visual control module to ensure that it can efficiently process image data and accurately identify the object weight information. In addition, we design the hardware circuit of the 51 MCU and write the corresponding control program to ensure that it can accurately control the joints of the robot arm according to the data provided by OpenMV.Through the combination of OpenMV vision module and 51 single-chip microcomputer control core, we successfully implemented a robot arm system which can grasp and locate objects autonomously. The system not only improves the accuracy and efficiency of the grasping task, but also has a good expansibility and application prospects.

articleTitle: Multi-target trapping method of swarm robots based on mean-shift
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The collective behavior of many creatures in nature serves as an inspiration for swarm robots. Therefore, this article proposes a mean-shift-based multi-target trapping method, which can enable swarm robots of different scales to accomplish the trapping task of targets in different distribution situations when facing multiple moving targets. And by combining the grouping mechanism proposed in this article, uniform allocation of swarm robots can be realized, which can effectively reduce the escape rate of targets. The effectiveness and feasibility of the method are validated through simulations experiments.

articleTitle: Vehicle Trajectory Prediction Model under Attention Network Based on Goal Areas Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In this study, we explore the utilization of video signals, which encompass both the historical movement paths and the surrounding context of vehicles within a defined setting. The trajectories of vehicles are conceptualized as sequential data points, which can be analyzed to anticipate their subsequent movements. We introduce a novel graph attention network that leverages goal-directed and interactive perceptions to deduce the collective probability distribution of forthcoming trajectories for multiple vehicles. This model presents several significant advantagesFirstly, it efficiently incorporates geographical mapping and real-time traffic data, and it harnesses the power of a Transformer architecture to capture extended temporal sequences. Secondly, leveraging these interdependencies, the model is capable of producing a variety of potential destinations and focal points, enabling the formulation of control trajectories for multiple vehicles. Lastly, by integrating a multimodal forecasting technique grounded in probabilistic distributions, the model also meticulously assesses the likelihood of each trajectory based on a comprehensive consideration of the various potential future paths linked to tshese focal points.

articleTitle: Multi-condition Temperature Detection of UAV Batteries Based on Least Squares Fitting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Conventional multi-operating condition temperature detection methods for UAV batteries are mainly based on temperature characterization, which do not take into account the relationship between temperature and operating conditions, thus affecting the accuracy of temperature detection. Therefore, a multi-condition temperature detection method for UAV batteries based on the least squares fitting algorithm is designed. Multi-point temperature sensors are arranged on the surface and inside of the battery to collect the temperature distribution data on the surface and inside of the UAV battery to ensure the accuracy of the subsequent temperature detection. Based on the least squares fitting algorithm, a battery condition-temperature detection model is constructed, and the temperature change pattern of the battery under each condition is analyzed to obtain the optimal detection results. The temperature detection error of UAV battery under multiple conditions is step-corrected, and the relationship between the temperature transient and the pulse function under any condition is obtained according to the Duhamel integral, so as to avoid the problem of temperature detection error. Comparison experiments are used to verify that the method is more accurate in temperature detection and can be applied in real life.

articleTitle: Precise motion control of omnidirectional mobile robots for nuclear power inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To increase the motion stability and accuracy of omnidirectional mobile robots for nuclear power inspection, an improved PID controller based on a fuzzy immune algorithm is proposed. Firstly, a kinematic model with velocity coupling constraints was developed according to structural analysis of the inspection robot. Secondly, fuzzy logic was used to adjust the three parameters of the PID controller adaptively, and an artificial immune algorithm was integrated to perform secondary optimization of the proportional gain in the design of a fuzzy immune PID controller. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed controller reduces velocity overshoot and enhances the motion control precision and stability of the robot.

articleTitle: Attitude Balance Control of a Wheeled Quadruped Robot for Unilateral Obstacle Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study explores an attitude balance control method for a Wheeled Quadruped Robot (WQR) traversing unilateral obstacle scenarios with varying slopes. By incorporating a force feedback mechanism, this method enables real-time adjustment of the WQR's hip and knee joint angles based on the kinematics model, facilitating effective navigation across different inclines of unilateral obstacles. The research begins with an analysis of potential attitude imbalance issues that the WQR may encounter when facing unilateral obstacles, highlighting the essential role of force sensors in detecting ground reaction forces and providing feedback. Subsequently, an attitude balance control algorithm is designed, based on feedback from in-wheel force sensors, which adjusts the WQR's motion posture in real-time to ensure stability in such scenarios. Simulation results have validated the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, demonstrating that by utilizing feedback information from in-wheel force sensors, the WQR can accurately perceive obstacles and make corresponding adjustments, thereby effectively preventing attitude imbalances. This research not only supports the stable movement of WQRs in complex environments but also provides valuable insights for future research in the field of robot attitude control.

articleTitle: NWD-YOLOv5: A YOLOv5 Model for Small Target Detection Based on NWD Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Target detection technology is vital in modern social management and urban security, with small target detection— accurately identifying tiny objects in large scenes—posing a key challenge for improving surveillance system accuracy and real-time performance. The YOLO series is still the mainstream target detection model, for the YOLOv5 model, as the IoU metric it adopts still uses the geometrical overlap of the detection frame as the basis of the loss calculation, while the experiments have proved that this metric is unable to effectively utilize the small-scale characteristics of small targets. Therefore, improving the loss metric in the existing framework can help the model to pay more attention to the spatial semantic features of small targets in the image in the training phase of the network, respectively, and thus improve the detection effect. In this paper, we propose the NWD-YOLOv5 model, i.e., we introduce the NWD loss that measures the difference in the distribution of the detection frames for the existing target detection framework YOLOv5, which ensures that the loss of the small targets is not neglected in the calculation of the forward propagation loss of the model, and we purposefully modify the structure of the feature extraction network in the original framework by adding a feature extraction layer for the detection of the small targets, which enhances the ability of the model to capture the subtle features thus improving the accuracy of small target detection. Through comparative experiments, we evaluated the detection performance of the original YOLOv5 model, the YOLOv5 model using only the NWD loss, the YOLOv5 model with only the additional small-target detection layer, and the full NWD-YOLOv5 model for small-targeted human bodies on the screened COCO2017 public dataset, respectively. The experimental results show that compared to the original YOLOv5 model, the model with only the NWD loss improves the mAP@.5 metrics on small-target detection by 16.5%, while the model with only the additional small-target detection layer improves it by 19.9%. Finally, the complete NWD-YOLOv5 model achieves the optimal small target detection effect, and its mAP@.5 index improves by 23.4% compared to the original model, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: Fast Penetration Decision-making Technology for UAV based on Improved Case-based Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In a threatening environment, this paper proposes a comprehensive strategy combining database matching method and traditional artificial potential field method for UAV penetration missions, and presents a fast penetration decision-making method for UAV based on improved case-based reasoning. In response to the characteristics of multiple threat factors and wide attributes, a database-based reasoning method is applied to improve the real-time decision-making by solving feasible solutions rather than optimal solutions. In response to the volatile threat environment and limited existing databases, the artificial potential field method is applied to obtain penetration routes and automatically expand the database. The simulation results show that the new method combines the correctness of decision-making with real-time performance.

articleTitle: Flight Control of Aerial Robots for Wire-Hanging Under Wind Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To enhance the efficiency of power transmission line inspections, this paper designs a novel aerial robot capable of hanging line operations and proposes an automatic hanging line flight control method. The robot's structure is designed, and its mathematical model is established using the Newton-Euler method, along with a wind field model for accurate wind disturbance simulation. To address nonlinear coupling and wind disturbances, a position controller based on Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) is developed, and system stability is proven. Simulation results demonstrate that the LADRC controller ensures stable and robust position control, enabling the aerial robot to perform hanging line tasks effectively under wind disturbances.

articleTitle: Defect detection of transmission lines based on SH-YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Power transmission lines are an extremely important component of the power system. With the rapid development of China's power industry, the inspection tasks of power transmission lines face significant challenges, among which the detection of insulator defects, faulty cables, and tower corrosion is a crucial part of the inspection process. In response to the issue of power transmission line defect detection, an improved YOLOv8 algorithm is proposed. The SH-YOLOv8 model, based on the structure of the YOLOv8 algorithm, integrates a Cross-Scale Feature Aggregation Module (CAFM) to further enhance the capability of detecting defects in power transmission lines, especially in complex backgrounds and multi-scale object detection. The introduction of the CAFM module allows SH-YOLOv8 to more efficiently integrate features of different scales, achieving stronger cross-level information sharing. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved SH-YOLOv8 performs exceptionally well in the task of power transmission line defect detection, particularly in the recognition of small-scale targets such as missing insulators and faulty cables, significantly reducing the incidence of missed and false detections. This provides an efficient and accurate technical solution for the intelligent development of power grid inspection.

articleTitle: Research on intelligent lane-changing model based on multi-intelligent reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Most of the traditional automatic driving behaviours are based on mathematical formulae or vehicle dynamics and kinematics models, which ignore the driver's perception and decision-making ability in the actual driving process, and the generated trajectories are very different from the actual lane-changing trajectories. In this paper, we adopt an automatic driving system based on multi-intelligence reinforcement learning to optimise the lane-changing decision of the vehicle by combining multi-intelligence reinforcement learning algorithms and avoiding the interference of inter-vehicle information interaction. In this way, the self-driving vehicle can have the functions of complex environmental perception, path planning and behavioural decision making. Combined with the highway mixed-flow environment scenario, the vehicle lane-changing behaviour model based on the HMM model is carried out for comparative experiments, and the results show that the lane-changing intention model based on multi-intelligence body reinforcement learning performs better in lane-changing detection accuracy and can be adapted to traffic scenarios with different traffic flow densities.

articleTitle: A Bearing Fault Diagnosis Model Based on SCSA-CNN-LSTM with Linear Deformable Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To overcome the constraints of conventional rolling bearing fault diagnosis approaches, which often extract insufficient features and struggle to deeply mine fault characteristics under complex operating conditions, this paper proposes a CNN-LSTM model based on linear deformable convolution (LDConv) and spatial and channel synergistic attention (SCSA) mechanism. The proposed model uses CNN as the backbone network, efficiently extracting features by incorporating LDConv and combining the SCSA module to uncover hidden channel and spatial information. Then, LSTM is utilized to leverage its sequence learning capability to extract the temporal features of the signal, ultimately achieving the identification and classification of bearing fault states. Experiments conducted on the Case Western Reserve University dataset under various noise conditions demonstrate that the proposed model effectively extracts fault features from the raw signals and exhibits strong robustness. The model achieves an accuracy of 95.86% in noisy environments, significantly outperforming other advanced fault diagnosis models. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the proposed modules.

articleTitle: A Calibration Method based on Heteroscedastic Evolutionary Bayesian Optimization for Simulation System of HVAC
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In recent years, increasing the energy efficiency of buildings has become one of the objectives of facility managers. Advanced control methods can be used to improve the efficiency of Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC). However, advanced control methods cannot be effectively applied due to inconvenient commissioning. Therefore, simulating and modeling the HVAC system becomes particularly important for verifying various control algorithms. Modeling and calibrating the HVAC simulation system becomes crucial for the application of various control strategies based on actual operational data, while current calibration methods are usually based on experience. In this research, a method for the calibration of an HVAC model based on Heteroscedastic Evolutionary Bayesian Optimization (HEBO) is presented. Firstly, the HVAC model is built using the Modelica language in the Dymola environment. Secondly, real operation and weather data are fed to the HVAC model to predict the energy consumption of various equipment. Thirdly, the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) between predicted and real values is minimized by HEBO so that the optimal parameters of the equipment can be obtained. Finally, a case study is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the CV(RMSE) of calibrated models meets the guideline requirements of ASHRAE, IPMVP, and FEMP.

articleTitle: Modeling the dynamics of Multi-agent systems in one-dimensional space and their stability analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Based on the Lennard-Jones potential function of long-range attraction and short-range repulsion between agents, this paper constructs a dynamical model of multi-agent clustering in one-dimensional space. The model takes into account the interactions between agents and the rules of motion to simulate and describe the motion of clusters of intelligent bodies in one-dimensional space. It also combines a graph-theoretic approach to global Lyapunov functions for heterogeneous multi-agent networks to construct global Lyapunov functions for the system, and uses a stability theorem to prove that the multi-agents eventually reach the stability of the cluster motion. Finally, to verify the theoretical results, simulations are carried out in both homogeneous multi-agent systems and heterogeneous multi-agent systems.

articleTitle: Innovative Research on IoT Architecture and Robotic Operating Platforms: Applications of Large Language Models and Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative design for robotic operating platforms, underpinned by a transformative Internet of Things (IoT) architecture, seamlessly integrating cutting-edge technologies such as large language models (LLMs), generative AI, edge computing, and 5G networks. The proposed platform aims to elevate the intelligence and autonomy of IoT systems and robotics, enabling them to make real-time decisions and adapt dynamically to changing environments. Through a series of compelling case studies across industries including smart manufacturing, healthcare, and service sectors, this paper demonstrates the substantial potential of IoT-enabled robotics to optimize operational workflows, enhance productivity, and deliver innovative, scalable solutions. By emphasizing the roles of LLMs and generative AI, the research highlights how these technologies drive the evolution of intelligent robotics and IoT, shaping the future of industry-specific advancements. The findings not only showcase the transformative power of these technologies but also offer a forward-looking perspective on their broader societal and industrial implications, positioning them as catalysts for next-generation automation and technological convergence.

articleTitle: Research on ship path planning in ice area based on improved ant colony algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In order to meet the practical needs of safe navigation in the ice area of ships, a path planning method with improved ant colony algorithm was proposed. The traditional ant colony algorithm has the characteristics of strong path search ability and high real-time performance in the path planning of ships in ice areas, but it still has the shortcomings of long search path and slow convergence speed. By introducing the Tent chaotic map, the initial value of the ant pack was optimized, which enhanced the diversity of the wolf pack and improved the global search ability. The Levy flight and random walk strategies were used to enhance the global and local optimization capabilities, respectively. Add the greedy mechanic to retain the more adaptable path solution. Experimental results show that, compared with the traditional algorithm, the proposed improved algorithm has a great improvement in the planning path length and smoothness, which can better meet the path planning needs of ships in the complex navigation environment of ice areas.

articleTitle: An Improved Bidirectional RRT* Algorithm for UAV Path Planning Based on Energy Consumption Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of ignoring turning cost and slow convergence in traditional path planning, a potential function sampling heuristic optimal path planning (AGB-RRT*) algorithm based on Gaussian distribution is proposed. In this paper, a path energy consumption estimation model combining distance and Angle is proposed. Secondly, on the traditional RRT, this paper adopts Gaussian sampling to achieve the heuristic sampling target, introduces the gravitational potential function of the artificial potential field method, and determines the growth direction of the random number according to the size of the configured gravitational factor, thus speeding up the convergence speed. Finally, integrated with the dynamic step size optimization strategy, it guides the growth of new nodes and the update of parent nodes, removes high-cost nodes and sampling points, and uses segmentation cutting and path interpolation to make the UAV plan a shorter path to shoot the target object. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can significantly reduce flight energy consumption and turn times, and accelerate initial path acquisition and convergence speed, which is suitable for UAV path planning.

articleTitle: Genetic algorithm optimization of terminal sliding mode multi-agent braking slip rate control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Braking stability is an important part of the safe driving process of the car, and the slip rate control directly affects the braking safety of the vehicle. In the braking process, the slip rate control is a nonlinear, time-varying complex system. In this paper, the vehicle braking process is modeled by considering the load transfer phenomenon. The non-singular terminal sliding mode control strategy based on multi-agent is designed and the algorithm is analyzed for Lyapunov stability. In order to improve the fastness and weakening chattering of non-singular terminal sliding mode control algorithm based on multi-agent, a genetic algorithm is introduced to optimize the design parameters of non-singular terminal sliding mode and improve the performance of the control system. Finally, the joint simulation was carried out by Carsim-Simulink, and the vehicle was selected for experimental simulation on a standard uniform road surface and a dry cement road surface. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has good control effect and meets the stability requirements of vehicle braking.

articleTitle: Research on the collaborative control process of unmanned aerial vehicles in disaster rescue process
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: During the disaster rescue process, unmanned aerial vehicles played an important role in all aspects. With the continuous progress of control technology, the collaborative work of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles has gradually become the norm. This article studies the task allocation problem through task sets and constraints, and defines the constraints of drones themselves. Based on the constraints of unmanned aerial vehicles, a simulation process for unmanned aerial vehicle collaborative tasks in disaster rescue situations is proposed, which theoretically improves efficiency.

articleTitle: Reducing False alarm rate of Sonar image Detection via Self-training
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Sonar image target detection is a key technology for underwater unmanned systems, but it faces the challenge of high false alarm rates, which limits the effectiveness and efficiency of underwater unmanned systems in performing tasks. Therefore, this paper proposes a method to improve the false alarm rate by self-training a deep learning detector on sonar images. This method automatically generates proxy classification tasks based on the sonar image target detection dataset. Through pre-training with these proxy classification tasks, the deep learning detector's ability to learn target and background features is enhanced, thereby improving its ability to distinguish between targets and backgrounds and reducing the false alarm rate. Experimental results show that, at the same or even higher recall rates, this method can reduce the false alarm rate by 3.91% compared to traditional transfer learning methods. This method achieves improved generalization performance of the deep learning detector without using external datasets, providing an efficient self-training approach for underwater target detection scenarios with small sample sizes.

articleTitle: A simple data augmentation method for automatic modulation recognition via mixing signals
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Automatic Modulation Recognition(AMR) is crucial in cognitive radio, transitioning from traditional methods to deep learning-based classification. However, deep learning requires large datasets for effective training, making data augmentation vital for enhancing model generalization and accuracy. It helps to expand the dataset, thereby improving the models’ generalization ability and accuracy. We proposes a novel data augmentation approach for AMR task based on signal mixing, with four specific methods designed to improve the performance of Mixed Signals. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods lead to a notable improvement in the classification accuracy of deep learning-based AMR models in diverse scenarios. Notably, experiments conducted with datasets at a single signal-to-noise ratio show a significant increase in classification accuracy, confirming the effectiveness of the signal mixing method.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Malicious Code Detection Using CNN-BiLSTM and Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of Internet technology, the threat of malware to computer systems and network security has intensified. Malware affects individual privacy and security and poses risks to critical infrastructures of enterprises and nations. The increasing quantity and complexity of malware, along with its concealment and diversity, challenge traditional detection techniques. Static detection methods struggle against variants and packed malware, while dynamic methods face high costs and risks that limit their application. Consequently, there is an urgent need for novel and efficient malware detection techniques to improve accuracy and robustness.This study first employs the minhash algorithm to convert binary files of malware into grayscale images, followed by the extraction of global and local texture features using GIST and LBP algorithms. Additionally, the study utilizes IDA Pro to decompile and extract opcode sequences, applying N-gram and tf-idf algorithms for feature vectorization. The fusion of these features enables the model to comprehensively capture the behavioral characteristics of malware.In terms of model construction, a CNN-BiLSTM fusion model is designed to simultaneously process image features and opcode sequences, enhancing classification performance.
