Experimental validation on multiple public datasets demonstrates that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional detection techniques in terms of accuracy, recall, and F1 score, particularly in detecting variants and obfuscated malware with greater stability.The research presented in this paper offers new insights into the development of malware detection technologies, validating the effectiveness of feature and model fusion, and holds promising application prospects.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of the Airport Stop Bar Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Since 2013, the International Civil Aviation Organization has recommended the use of stop bars at operational or newly-built airports to reduce the probability of runway incursions during airport operations. With the implementation and deployment of domestic industry standards, regulations, and related application cases, the importance and significance of the stop bar system in airport surface operations have been verified, laying a solid foundation for its comprehensive promotion. Starting from the installation methods, working principles, and control logic of stop bars, this article studies the composition and implementation methods of the system. By combining radar-vision fusion technology for accurate monitoring of airport runway entrances, and utilizing 5G wireless communication technology to achieve accurate and reliable monitoring of the status of stop bars and remote control of their lighting and extinguishing, it provides additional warnings to pilots and vehicle drivers, enhances ground situation awareness, effectively prevents runway incursion incidents, and simultaneously improves airport operational capabilities. This article also provides technical references for the design of runway incursion warning systems.

articleTitle: A Text Augmentation Method Based on Dual Diversity Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In text augmentation in the field of natural language processing, it has been observed that most of the traditional methods often result in only minimal changes to the original text, which consequently limits the diversity of the augmented samples. In this paper, a novel text augmentation method based on Dual Diversity Generation is proposed, which effectively addresses the aforementioned limitation through two key components: keyword diversity and sample diversity. Initially, a sketch is constructed through keyphrase extraction, which is subsequently input into the text augmentation model for the generation of new samples. To mitigate the semantic overlap among the extracted keyphrases, keyphrase diversity is incorporated into the extraction process. Furthermore, sample diversity is emphasized during the generation phase to enhance the overall quality of the text augmentation. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated by text classification effect, and the experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves significant improvements compared to other methods.

articleTitle: A Channel Pruning Method Using Subtraction-Average-Based Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs) require huge resources, which hindered the implement on light devices. However, existing pruning techniques primarily concentrate on choosing channels based on their importance or on regularization strategies that are crafted through empirical knowledge, the compressed networks obtained through these methods have unstable performance and require unnecessary human intervention. This paper proposes a new channel pruning method based on the Subtraction-Average-Based Optimizer, dubbed as SABOPruner. To facilitate deployment on FGPA, we constrain the pruning step size of each layer to be a multiple of 8. Finally, the search was transformed into an optimization problem and we solve it by integrating the SABO algorithm, reducing the need for manual intervention. We introduced Adaptive Batch Normalization to improve the efficiency of fine-tuning, this strategy also accelerates the search efficiency of the SABO algorithm. SABOPruner has been demonstrated to be effective, we conducted efficacy tests on four leading CNN models using two image classification datasets. On the ILSVRC-2012 dataset, the pruned ResNet-50 model reduced 55.15% in FLOPs and make only a 0.9% decrease in accuracy compared to the baseline. With MobileNetV2, we achieve a 51%-FLOPs reduction with a 3.05% performance higher on ImageNet-1K.

articleTitle: Combining Textual and Behavioral Features to Improve Method-Level Bug Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The information retrieval-based bug localization approach exploits semantic similarity to locate source code errors through bug reports. The main difficulty lies in distinguishing the semantics of candidate codes. The candidate code semantic information directly impacts the localization accuracy through semantic mapping. Most existing approaches increase the distinguishability by mining the semantic features of candidate codes to improve feature quantity. However, on the basis of extracting text keywords as features in the traditional bug localization approach, simply superimposing the feature quantities and calculating the suspiciousness of candidate codes based on experience is very limited in improving the accuracy of bug localization. In this paper, we distinguish the types of features that can be attached. Then, we determine the range of candidate codes according to the program execution behavior information. Mining similar codes from historical requirements, we expand the semantics of candidate codes based on the attention mechanism. Finally, we combine the code execution behavior features and text features with different weights to calculate the suspicious degree of candidate codes. The optimization method maximizes the location accuracy of bugs. We implemented MethodLocator, a method-level bug localization method that combines textual and behavioral features, and we conducted bug localization experiments on seven open-source projects. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, MethodLocator improves MRR by 3.4%-47.2% and MAP by 2.0%-38.4%. Our statistical tests show that our improvement is significant.

articleTitle: BiGRU-Attention-Based Specific Emitter Identification Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Specific emitter identification plays a pivotal role in electronic countermeasures within the realm of complex electromagnetic environments. This study introduces a novel method for specific emitter identification, leveraging the capabilities of BiGRU-Attention (BiGRU-Att). The process begins with the segmentation of steady-state signal slices from the targeted emitter. Subsequently, six distinct features, including wavelet entropy and amplitude skewness within the timefrequency domain, are meticulously extracted. These extracted sequence feature data are then employed to train the model, culminating in the acquisition of the identification outcome. The methodology was rigorously tested using TETRA communication signals from nine distinct emitters. Experimental findings affirm that the model proficiently harnesses the timing information inherent in the specific emitter's signal, substantially enhancing the identification accuracy. This approach not only underscores the effectiveness of integrating BiGRU and attention mechanisms for signal classification but also sets a precedent for future research in specific emitter identification under intricate electromagnetic conditions.

articleTitle: Time Series Fusion Model for Predicting Electric power tools and equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To effectively address the issue of inadequate accuracy and timeliness in industrial data classification, this paper proposes a fusion classification model based on time series (DT-RF-MLP) for loss prediction of electrical work equipment. Firstly, data information is extracted from the dataset and features are constructed based on the data information to enhance the diversity of data features. Secondly, redundant and highly correlated features are removed by quantifying the correlation degree between the features to simplify the model inputs. On this basis, a fusion classification model is constructed and comparative experiments are conducted with a single model to validate the advantages of the fusion model in terms of prediction performance. The experimental results demonstrate that the model markedly enhances prediction accuracy while concurrently reducing the duration of the model run.

articleTitle: Research on Graphene Thermoacoustic Speakers Based on a Sparse Autoencoder-Back Propagation Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To mitigate the complexities of traditional theoretical models for graphene thermoacoustic speakers, which are hampered by multifarious influencing factors that are challenging to unify and constrained by discrete data, leading to imprecise characterizations, this study delves into a deep learning model for graphene thermoacoustic speakers. Initially, nine parameters pertinent to graphene thermoacoustic speakers are identified as initial input features: the density, thermal conductivity, and specific heat capacity of both the film and substrate, the root mean square (RMS) value of the input voltage, frequency, and the measured distance. A deep learning model is then established for predicting the sound pressure level (SPL), serving as the output feature. Subsequently, a sparse autoencoder-back propagation (SA-BP) neural network model is constructed by integrating the encoding network of a sparse autoencoder with a fully connected BP neural network. Optimization is achieved when the encoder network of the SA-BP model comprises three hidden layers with 11 neurons each, reducing the nonlinear feature dimensionality to five, and the BP neural network comprises seven hidden layers with 18 neurons. Finally, the predicted SPL is computed using the SA-BP neural network model on a test set. Comparison with a BP neural network reveals that while the latter exhibits a maximum relative error of 6.5%, the SA-BP model achieves a notably lower maximum relative error of 1.5%. The SA-BP model outperforms the BP neural network in both feature extraction capability and SPL prediction accuracy, particularly demonstrating enhanced adaptability at lower voltage levels. This research offers a highly accurate solution for precise feature extraction and output prediction in a wide range of sensor applications.

articleTitle: Compound AI System for Personalized Learning: Integrating LLM Agents with Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Personalized learning plays a critical role in enhancing educational outcomes by customizing experiences to meet individual learners' unique needs, preferences, and abilities. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities for personalization through natural language interactions, they face challenges related to maintaining long-term context and ensuring traceability of a learner's evolving knowledge. This paper introduces a composite AI framework that merges an LLM-powered conversational agent with Knowledge Graphs (KGs) structured according to Knowledge Space Theory (KST), enhanced by advanced retrieval tools and a robust long-term memory mechanism. This system autonomously orchestrates meaningful, context-aware dialogues while utilizing function calling to access various tools, effectively bridging the gap between dynamic interactions and structured knowledge representation. Our empirical evaluations indicate that the proposed system excels in maintaining coherent dialogues, accurately tracking learner progress, and providing reliable, personalized educational support. By addressing the limitations of standalone LLMs and traditional adaptive learning systems, this integrated approach signifies a notable advancement in intelligent educational technology.

articleTitle: Forecasting Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Using Random Forest and LSTM Networks: Enhanced Predictive Modeling with Climate-Based Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of machine learning approaches for predicting palm oil futures prices in Malaysia. The research employs Random Forest (RF) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to evaluate the impact of both conventional market indicators and climate factors on price prediction accuracy. Through rigorous analysis of 112 potential indicators across agricultural, commodity, Malaysia-specific, economic, and climate categories, 83 core indicators were identified for the predictive models. Results demonstrate that the RF model consistently outperformed LSTM, achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 7.45% compared to LSTM's 13.36% in multivariate analysis. The incorporation of climate factors significantly improved LSTM model performance, reducing its MAPE from 21.59% to 13.36%, while showing minimal impact on RF model accuracy. Notably, the RF model exhibited superior performance in long-term (100-day) forecasting compared to short-term (15-day) predictions, with MAPE values of 3.61% and 7.45% respectively. This research provides valuable insights into agricultural commodity trading and risk management, particularly highlighting the effectiveness of RF models for palm oil futures price prediction and the potential benefits of incorporating climate variables in forecasting models.

articleTitle: Design of an Adaptive Spiral-Loop Pipeline Robot Based on Laser SLAM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Urban development leads to a large and complex underground pipe network with pipe issues. Regular inspections of pipelines are necessary. Current pipeline robots have drawbacks like limited diameter adaptability, high traveling resistance and poor navigation. Manual inspection is inefficient. This paper presents an adaptive spiral-loop pipeline robot using Laser SLAM. Its mechanical structure has a spiral mode and loop design to reduce resistance. It employs a multi-stage screw-nut-spring support rod type diameter-changing mechanism to adapt to pipes of different diameters. For localization in GPS-ineffective underground, Laser SLAM is applied. After validating the solution's feasibility via structure and trajectory analysis, the ROS/Gazebo and evo tool are used for simulation. Quantitative analysis shows the robot's average absolute error in the pipeline is under 0.58m and stability standard deviation is less than 0.27m, proving Laser SLAM's applicability.

articleTitle: Research Progress and Knowledge Mapping Analysis of Smart Classrooms based on CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet technology, the design and application of smart classrooms has become one of the hot research topics in the field of educational technology. It is also a focus of many national governments, enterprises, scientific research institutes and educational researchers. In order to explore the research hot spots and development trends of smart classrooms, this article collects documents from the Web of Science database in this field from 2000 to 2024, and conducts visual analysis through knowledge and methods related to knowledge map combined with CiteSpace software. From the aspects of year distribution of paper, author and institutional cooperation, keyword co-occurrence analysis and cluster analysis, we sort out the research overview and research hotspots of smart classrooms. This paper summarizes existing research results, explores issues and directions worthy of attention by future researchers to provide reference for subsequent research and development in this field.

articleTitle: A universal adversarial perturbations generation method based on feature aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Universal Adversarial Perturbations (UAP) is a sample-independent adversarial attack that can be added to all natural samples to change most of their predictive labels. Aiming at the problems of the existing universal adversarial attack methods in the field of automatic modulation recognition, such as the large amount of training samples needed, the complexity of the method training process, and the low success rate of the universal adversarial attack, this paper proposes a universal adversarial perturbation generation method based on feature aggregation. In this paper, we first introduce the generic adversarial attack layer selection method based on the neural collapse phenomenon, and then propose the feature clustering loss for generic adversarial perturbation generation, and introduce the training process of the algorithm. This paper conducts a large number of experiments on several datasets and models, and proposes multi-dimensional metrics to measure the performance of the generalized adversarial attack, which finally proves the effectiveness of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: MiniSAM: A Lightweight Segmentation Model with Pruning and Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In practical applications, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) encounters difficulties in being effectively applied in scenarios with limited computing resources. In view of this, this paper, taking SAM-B as the base model, innovatively proposes MiniSAM, a lightweight variant of SAM. Specifically, firstly, model pruning and knowledge distillation strategies are employed to compress the large-scale image encoder module of SAM, optimizing its consumption of computing resources. Secondly, an object detection module is appended to the original basic structure of SAM, which is capable of automatically generating input box prompts, further enhancing the convenience and practicability of the model in relevant applications. Finally, the mask decoder of MiniSAM is meticulously fine-tuned to better adapt to the overall lightweight model architecture, enabling it to perform relatively well even in the context of limited computing resources. Experimental results demonstrate that in human segmentation tasks, despite having an image encoder with only 4.4% of the parameters of SAM Base (SAM-B) and 0.6% of SAM High-performance (SAM-H), MiniSAM achieves segmentation performance comparable to SAM-B.

articleTitle: Research on the Sharpness Evaluation Function Based on GrabCut for Autonomous Focusing in the Fluid Physics Experimental Cabinet of the Tiangong Space Station
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Autonomous focusing in aerospace systems often relies on image sharpness evaluation algorithms, which are primarily optimized for satellite cameras and thus unsuitable for experimental images from space stations. To address the lack of autonomous focusing capability in the fluid physics experimental cabinet aboard the China Space Station, this paper presents a novel image sharpness evaluation method based on an edge gradient function utilizing GrabCut. The proposed method is specifically tailored to the unique characteristics of images from the experimental cabinet, where color blocks are concentrated, the observation area is central, and boundaries are distinct in clear images. These distinct features enable the method to effectively leverage edge information for precise evaluation, making it particularly suited to the requirements of the Space Station’s experimental environment. We employ the GrabCut algorithm to segment the foreground from the background, using the boundary as the target area for gradient computation. A feature-based generic initial bounding box is adopted, ensuring broad applicability to all images from the fluid experimental cabinet without requiring user intervention. Subsequently, a convolution operator calculates the gradient along the target area, which serves as the sharpness evaluation function. Compared with two commonly used algorithms, experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves clear unimodality near the focal point and remains robust against blurring and noise in out-of-focus regions. Consequently, this algorithm has meaningful engineering potential, satisfying essential sharpness evaluation requirements and providing an effective solution for image sharpness assessment in the Fluid Physics Experimental Cabinet of the Tiangong Space Station.

articleTitle: Identification and Resolution Technology Based on Multi-Layer Knowledge Graph for Industrial Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the advancement of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technology, there is an increasing demand for efficient data storage solutions and robust data processing capabilities. The IIoT involves numerous devices and sensors that generate massive data streams, which require efficient storage and processing for real-time analysis and decision-making. This paper proposes an information management architecture based on multi-layer knowledge graphs combined with identification and resolution technology. The approach utilizes knowledge graph technology to structure multi-layer information within the IIoT and introduces identification and resolution technology, using Handle encoding to uniquely identify entities for cross-layer querying and data exchange. The BiLSTM-CRF (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory - Conditional Random Field) algorithm is employed for hierarchical entity classification, enhancing data consistency and accuracy. This study provides new insights and methods for data management in the IIoT, significantly improving the efficiency and quality of data management.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Diagnostic Techniques for Line Loss Based on Comprehensive Analysis Utilizing Machine Learning Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In the context of the expanding power grid infrastructure and escalating electricity demand, the issue of line loss has emerged as a significant concern within the power industry. This paper endeavors to investigate an intelligent diagnostic technique for line loss, leveraging comprehensive analysis through machine learning methodologies, with the objective of enhancing the precision, flexibility, and adaptability of line loss diagnosis. By developing models for the classification of non-conforming characteristics of transformer districts, the analysis of primary factors contributing to non-compliant line loss, the examination of correlated anomaly causes, and the assessment of quantifiable impacts of anomalies, and by incorporating sophisticated machine learning paradigms such as the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) algorithm, Bayesian networks, deep learning, and reinforcement learning, this paper presents a comprehensive framework for the quantitative evaluation and optimal mitigation of anomalies in line loss within transformer districts.

Author Keywords: Operation and Maintenance of Power Distribution Areas

articleTitle: Research on Motion Control Technology of Quadruped Robot Arm Based on Visual Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address the issues of limited working range, weak interactivity, and low safety in robotic arm, a collaborative quadruped robot with an attached robotic arm is designed and implemented. Using the door-opening task as an example, this system covers target recognition and measurement, kinematic modeling and path planning, collision detection, and collaborative control. The Mask-RCNN algorithm is employed for precise identification of the door handle, and a depth camera is used to measure the spatial distance to the door handle. A torque observer based on generalized momentum is designed for collision detection of the robotic arm. Based on the coordinates of the target object and the observed external torque, a motion control strategy for the robotic arm to open the door is planned. Finally, a collaborative control logic is established between the quadruped robot and the robotic arm, enabling them to work together to complete the door-opening task while ensuring safety.

articleTitle: Assembly space optimization for linear actuator assembly process based on PSO: two-robot case
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: A particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm-based analysis and optimization method for minimizing the assembly space of a workcell which is composed of 2 robot arms and 3 fixtures is proposed. By analysing the effect of population and acceleration coefficients on the fitness values in PSO, the most suitable set of algorithm parameters for optimising the size of the assembly space is identified. By applying the optimal parameters to PSO algorithm and adding a boundary check and a path accessibility check for shaped fixtures, the minimum fitness value, which is the ratio of the minimum assembly space to the total assembly workcell, and the polar position parameters of each layout object are derived. The feasibility of the layout is verified by simulation in RoboDK. A set of PSO parameters appropriate for solving the 2-robot arms assembly space minimization problem is determined, a path accessibility check for shaped fixtures is established, a layout for minimizing the assembly space of a workcell composed of 2 robot arms and 3 fixtures is derived, and the feasibility of the conclusions is verified through simulation. The analysis and optimization method of the multi-robot arm assembly space minimization problem based on the PSO algorithm is obtained. This research is an exploration of a new optimisation objective in the field of workcell layout, the minimisation of the assembly space of multiple robotic arms and has led to an analytical and optimisation method based on PSO algorithm for solving this type of problem.

articleTitle: Research on Driver Facial Expression Detection Algorithm Based on BBAN-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With a variety of uses in human-computer interaction, safe driving, and other domains, driver expression recognition is used to identify the type of expression from face photos. Various labels for expression data are frequently unsegregated in real-world applications. Expression recognition model performance is impacted when expression labels are not aggregated, as this lowers classification optimizer accuracy. Because of this, this study suggests a facial expression recognition technique called BBAN-Net for expression label non-aggregation. In the feature learning stage and the classifier optimization stage, respectively, this technique optimizes the model for category aggregation. BBAN-Net achieves distributed aggregation of labels for each category by combining the BBN and ANFL structures with a dual-branching architecture that uses regular learning and rebalancing. Before and after the addition of the expression label pre-training module BBN was verified on DISFA data, the experimental results showed that for expression label pre-processing, the F1-Score improved by 31.16%. Quantitative experiments conducted in four different networks show that BBAN-Net achieves 67.43% accuracy in detecting the average F1- Score on 8 AUs with 81.7% accuracy and 85.9% AUC. It also compares relatively well with a host of other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Dynamic Modeling and LQR Optimal Control of Wheel-Bipedal Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The wheel-bipedal robot integrates the advantages of both wheeled and legged systems, enabling efficient locomotion. However, many control approaches simplify this system to a wheeled linear inverted pendulum (WLIP), treating the legs and body as a unified entity and overlooking the distinct dynamics and effects of the legs. This paper derives a simplified model of the leg mechanism that captures the interactions between the robot’s leg and body dynamics. A linear quadratic regulator (LQR) controller is further designed to maintain overall balance, while a dedicated leg controller governs leg-specific movements, establishing a dynamic composite control framework. Additionally, this paper details the system architecture and development of controllers for various scenarios. Experimental results from prototype testing in real-world environments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control strategies.

articleTitle: CTF-LIOM: Coarse-to-Fine Loop Closure Detection in Lidar-Inertial Odometry and Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: We propose CTF-LIOM, a novel coarse-to-fine loop closure detection method for lidar-inertial odometry and mapping, which significantly enhances global pose estimation consistency and mapping quality. The approach integrates structured steps: data preprocessing, loop detection using the Stable Triangle Descriptor (STD), coarse matching based on plane overlap, and subgraph fine matching with Nano-VGICP. This framework effectively identifies accurate loop frame indices and corresponding pose constraints. Experiments on the M2DGR door_02 dataset demonstrate that CTF-LIOM achieves an average error of just 0.19 meters with an RMSE of 0.20 meters, delivering a 47.1% improvement over Faster-LIO. On the street_04 dataset, incorporating backend loop detection and global pose optimization yields a 58.62% improvement in accuracy over CTF-LIO. Overall, CTF-LIOM exhibits superior trajectory accuracy and robustness in complex environments and during prolonged SLAM tasks, effectively reducing ghosting and map overlap.

articleTitle: Research on the Planning Method of unmanned underwater vehicle Cluster Encirclement under Weak Connectivity Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In underwater environments, due to the limitation of exploration distance, UUV (unmanned underwater vehicle) clusters face challenges in coordination and efficiency when performing capture tasks. In order to effectively capture dynamic targets, this paper proposes a capture strategy for UUV clusters, aiming to achieve effective monitoring and capture of dynamic targets. Firstly, establish a mathematical model for dynamic target UUV cluster capture decision-making and the collaborative action mechanism of UUV clusters during the capture process. Ensure efficient collaboration of UUV clusters in capturing dynamic targets and improve the success rate of capture. Secondly, a target motion trajectory prediction method based on timestamps and dynamic models is proposed, which aims to reduce the adverse effects of communication delays. By predicting the target’s motion trajectory, more accurate target position information is provided for UUV clusters, thereby optimizing the capture strategy. In addition, this article designs a target tracking method based on angle measurement information. After the calculation is completed, the artificial potential field method is used to plan the trajectory of the UUV, in order to achieve effective encirclement of the target.

articleTitle: Adaptive Zoom Active Object Tracking Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Active Object Tracking (AOT) involves the tracker using visual observations from the camera to keep the object centered in the frame by controlling the motor system. In contrast to extensively researched passive tracking, which primarily focuses on perception, AOT integrates both perception and control tasks, making it more suitable for real-world tracking applications. AOT has the capability to interact with the environment, where perception determines the control actions, and the outcomes of these actions, in turn, shape future inputs and influence perception. We employed a pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) camera as the active tracker for highly maneuverable targets. By intelligently adjusting the zoom level based on the target's movement, our tracker optimizes the size of the target in the visual input, thereby enhancing the tracking success rate. Recognizing the complex interaction between perception and control, we applied deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to jointly train the tracker's perception and control modules in a virtual environment. The experimental results in the virtual environment demonstrate that our proposed method achieves a higher tracking success rate and speed compared to traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Classical Mechanics-based Kinematic Analysis of a Specific Microrobot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Detailed kinematic analysis is a necessary part of microrobot research, which is an important reference for the selection and determination of robot structural parameters, the optimisation analysis of motion performance, and the selection of robot control strategies. In this paper, we derive detailed equations of motion for a microrobot with bionic inchworm motion based on the theory of classical mechanics, thus obtaining a theoretical design method for a microrobot based on low-frequency motion performance. Comparison of the predicted kinematic data of the microrobot with the experimental data using the theoretical formulas revealed an error of less than 6.1%. This results in a theoretical kinematic predictive design method for microbots, which can provide a reference for the design of such inchworm-type microbots.

articleTitle: Electronic Nose Coupled with Deep Learning Techniques for Tea Quality Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Currently, the evaluation of tea quality primarily relies on sensory methods such as the observation of tea appearance, smelling the aroma of the tea liquor, and tasting it. Alternatively, instrumental quantitative methods like chromatography and spectroscopy are also employed. However, these methods tend to be highly subjective, prone to fatigue in the evaluator’s sensory organs, lack real-time capabilities, and are susceptible to measurement errors. Given the crucial role of the aroma emitted by the tea liquor in assessing its quality, this study employs a gas sensor arrays, commonly known as electronic noses, with deep learning techniques to assess tea quality. Specifically, a stacked sparse autoencoder was utilized to build the neural network. The entire network was trained using (Multi-Layer Perceptron) MLP with labeled data. Additionally, a Softmax regression function was integrated into the output layer of the MLP. The proposed method achieved a classification accuracy of approximately 90%, outperforming the average accuracy of the SVM method for each tea type.

articleTitle: Research on Unmanned Vehicle Material Security Path Planning Model in Plateau Area
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In a specific operational area, we aim to establish a comprehensive logistics support and transportation system linking "rear area - transit warehouse - forward area" utilizing unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) of various models. Initially, following reconnaissance, candidate locations for the rear area, forward area, and transit warehouse were identified, along with three-dimensional terrain data of the operational zone, technical specifications of UGVs, and operational protocols. Subsequently, an indicator system for UGV logistics support path planning was constructed, primarily defining metrics for path safety, stability, and time efficiency. Combined with constraints such as power consumption, maximum traversable slope limitations, and movement regulations of UGVs, a multi-objective path planning evaluation model was established. Finally, an improved A* algorithm was employed to determine the optimal route. This model provides scientific reference for UGV support missions in plateau regions.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-direction N-RGVs (N-Rail Guided Vehicles) Scheduling System Based on Bubble Sort Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: To address issues related to queuing of four-way vehicles and potential collisions, a novel bubble sort scheduling algorithm was designed with the aim of enhancing the operational efficiency of four-way vehicles. Based on the bubble sort algorithm, with the objective of minimizing the total time for goods to be shipped out of the warehouse, and with the constraint of multiple four-way vehicles (N-RGVs) operating together, a multi-closed loop system model for inbound and outbound warehouse operations was constructed. In this scheduling system, a novel bubble sort scheduling algorithm was introduced to perform a new sorting and path planning for multiple four-way vehicles. In comparison with the A* scheduling algorithm and the closed-loop scheduling algorithm, extensive tests were conducted on an experimental platform to gather relevant data for the three algorithms. The experimental results indicate that the novel bubble sort scheduling algorithm effectively resolves issues of queuing and vehicle conflicts, reduces computational costs, and thus significantly enhances overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: An improved air situation assessment method based on intuitive fuzzy reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Accurately and reliably identifying and predicting the air situation under the conditions of refusal environment and strong confrontation is the prerequisite and foundation for the command and control system to make reasonable task decisions and achieve predetermined goals. In response to this situation assessment issue, this article proposes an improved air situation assessment method based on intuitive fuzzy reasoning, using basic theoretical methods such as fuzzy theory and threat assessment. Firstly, describe the problem of air situation assessment, analyze the characteristics of typical situation assessment methods, and focus on summarizing the shortcomings of current research. Furthermore, utilizing the expressive power of generative adversarial networks and fuzzy reasoning, the situation in the denied air environment is modeled, and an improved air situation evaluation method based on intuitionistic fuzzy reasoning is designed by integrating intuitionistic fuzzy set theory, three-way decision strategy, and cumulative prospect theory. The simulation results show that the proposed Generative Adversarial Intuitive Situation Assessment method can effectively evaluate the current air situation.

articleTitle: Intelligent Sorting Solution Design Based on Engine Cylinder Cover Casting Line
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Based on the demand for engine cylinder cover Mixed production of multiple products renovation of an automotive engine manufacturer, this study identifies key technology points to be broken through beat analysis, integrates and improves traditional mechanized sorting and transfer methods, robot sorting and palletizing methods, and AGV transfer methods, and plans a solution based on accumulation and sorting in a narrow space and long-distance transfer. The establishment of the stacking area provides the opportunity for time-sharing between the front and rear sections, realizing energy savings and reduced labor intensity. The implementation process of the solution also utilized the machine vision system required for workpiece recognition to achieve gripping guidance and improve the classic program structure of robot depalletizing work, enhancing the stability of gripping and depalletizing; Finally, based on the network equipments of small production line achieves the collection of key operating data of key equipment, providing a low-cost equipment data collection solution and lays a solid foundation for predictive maintenance of equipment.

articleTitle: Exploration of the Relationship between the Six Methods of Forming Chinese Characters in Shuo Wen Jie Zi and AI Deep Learning of Chinese Characters
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Shuo Wen Jie Zi, authored by Xu Shen during the Eastern Han Dynasty in China, is the first linguistic dictionary in China to systematically analyze the forms and etymologies of Chinese characters. The book summarizes the formation and usage of Chinese characters into six types: pictographic, indicative, associative compound, phonetic-semantic compound, transformative annotation, and loan characters. It comprehensively sorts out the rules of Chinese character construction and holds immense value for studying the origin and evolution of Chinese characters, providing fundamental theories and methods for research on the knowledge graph of Chinese characters. Currently, many AI models are primarily trained on vast amounts of English data, with relatively limited coverage of Chinese data, leading to insufficient understanding and adaptability of these models to Chinese. Leveraging the rules of Chinese character construction in the Six Methods of Forming Chinese Characters theory from Shuo Wen Jie Zi to establish knowledge graphs and models enables AI to undergo deep self-learning training for Chinese characters. By analyzing the rules of Chinese character construction in the Six Methods theory and combining computational formulas, application strategies for the Six Methods theory in AI deep learning are formed, providing theoretical guidance for AI model computations. The aim is to train AI to deeply learn the rules of Chinese character construction and semantic explanations in Shuo Wen Jie Zi, thereby understanding the cultural concepts and ways of thinking in Chinese contexts. This enables AI software to better grasp the cultural connotations behind Chinese texts when engaging in cross-cultural communication, language translation, and graphical representation of Chinese content, thereby enhancing the accuracy and fluency of cross-cultural communication.

Author Keywords: the Six Methods of Forming Chinese Charactiers

articleTitle: A Continual learning approach based on Gaussian process model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In light of the limitations associated with traditional continual learning methods, such as catastrophic forgetting and inadequate generalization capabilities, we propose a new continual learning model guided by Gaussian Processes. This method constructs a relationship between batch data and the global distribution using a Gaussian model. By integrating Gaussian Processes into the empirical replay mechanism, we enhance the global awareness of batch data. The learning process involves modeling the mapping relationship between the feature and label spaces. We utilize Gaussian process regression to compute the contextual prediction probability for each sample within the current batch. By exploring the joint optimization of contextual prediction probabilities, original labels, and network prediction probabilities, we improve the representation learning capability of the neural network model, thereby enhancing the accuracy of target recognition over time. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly reduces training and validation losses across MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 datasets. The integration of Gaussian Processes markedly improves both the convergence speed and final accuracy of the model. These findings underscore the potential of Gaussian Processes in the training of complex neural networks and offer a new avenue for future continual learning research.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Multi-UAV Target Coverage via Improved GA-PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The study of path planning problems has wide-spread applications in the automation and intelligence of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Metaheuristic algorithms have shown promising results in optimizing path planning tasks. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is a frequently used metaheuristic algorithm, known for its fast convergence, strong search capabilities, and robustness. However, it also has the drawback of easily falling into local optima. We have implemented various optimizations to the PSO algorithm and proposed the comprehensively optimized grouping PSO (COGPSO) algorithm to better address path planning tasks. Multiple experiments were conducted to compare and analyze our algorithm with other PSO variants. Furthermore, we integrated Genetic Algorithm (GA) to tackle the multi-UAV target coverage problem.

articleTitle: PTrans: Transformer-Based HRRP Target Recognition Method with Patching
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Due to the characteristics of high-resolution range profiles (HRRP), which are easy to obtain, have low computational cost, and contain rich structural information about the target, HRRP-based target recognition has become a popular research direction in the field of radar automatic target recognition (RATR). To address the issues of traditional HRRP target recognition methods, which require time-consuming and labor-intensive, researchers, inspired by the powerful feature extraction capabilities of convolutional neural networks (CNN), have widely applied them to HRRP target recognition, significantly improving the accuracy and generalization of recognition methods. However, the inherent vulnerability of CNNs makes them susceptible to adversarial attacks, which significantly impact the recognition performance. Nevertheless, such adversarial attacks are typically constrained by real-world factors and can usually only generate adversarial samples by adding large, localized perturbations. Therefore, to defend against theses adversarial attacks, we propose a Transformer-based HRRP target recognition method, as Transformer enables target recognition through global feature. In order for the recognition model to simultaneously understand local feature, we propose a data patching strategy as a supplement. Experimental results show that our method has better recognition accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: State Estimation of the Self-Balancing Lower Limb Exoskeleton Using Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The safe operation of self-balancing lower limb exoskeletons heavily depends on real-time and precise monitoring of essential state variables, including position, velocity, and posture, necessitating the development of more refined and efficient measurement update techniques. This paper delves into the realm of state estimation strategies, leveraging the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm. By integrating diverse information sources like inertial measurement units (IMUs), joint encoders, and planned bipedal trajectory, it successfully accomplishes precise estimation of the exoskeleton’s torso and foot states within the global coordinate system.The EKF-based state estimation algorithm introduced in this paper notably enhances the overall state estimation’s accuracy and robustness by effectively mitigating the accumulation and propagation of IMU measurement errors at the exoskeleton’s torso. This advancement establishes a robust foundation for stable and precise control of self-balancing exoskeleton robots. Simulation experiments have further substantiated the high-precision capabilities of the proposed exoskeleton state estimation method.

articleTitle: Image super-resolution reconstruction method based on improved attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Image super-resolution enhancement technology occupies a central position in visual information processing in the digital era, and its core task is to reconstruct high-resolution images using low-resolution image data. With the development of computing technology, image super-resolution techniques are not only theoretically significant, but also become more and more critical in practical applications, and it has become a hot area of computer vision research. Nevertheless, there are still some challenges in current super-resolution solutions. Existing models are deficient in extracting the diversity of image features, which leads to the problems of detail loss and excessive smoothing of the reconstructed images, which seriously affects the visual quality of the images and makes the reconstructed images visually lacking in realism. In order to overcome these difficulties, this study focuses on the integration of image multi as features as well as exploring the attention mechanism of arbitrary scale images. Through these studies, we aim to improve the performance and efficiency of super-resolution reconstruction techniques. The main contributions of this thesis include:Aiming at the limitations of the multi-feature self-attention mechanism, this study proposes several innovative attention operators. These operators not only enhance the model’s feature extraction ability to capture image details and texture information more efficiently, but also improve the diversity of feature information. In addition, in order to overcome the limitations of existing attention mechanisms in feature extraction, this study introduces a novel, parameter-free attention module. This module effectively integrates information from both channel and spatial dimensions, significantly enhancing the feature representation. This design simplifies the model structure, avoids complex operations, and enhances model performance in image processing and computer vision tasks.

articleTitle: The dynamic malicious code identification model based on the lambda attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the development of the Internet, malicious code attacks have increased exponentially, with malicious code ranking as a key threat to Internet security. The ability to detect malicious code is critical for protection against security breaches, data theft, and other dangers. In the field of dynamic malicious code detection, existing vectorization methods and model construction techniques face challenges in capturing contextual information effectively and in having long convergence times.This paper proposes a method that utilizes BERT for vectorization combined with a transformer model based on the lambda attention mechanism. We use a cloud sandbox to obtain API sequences, effectively reducing the configuration complexity of the sandbox while enhancing efficiency. We then apply the concept of the longest common subsequence to deduplicate the API sequences. The BERT model is employed to perform vectorization on the API sequences. The classification model utilizes a transformer architecture based on the lambda attention mechanism, which effectively extracts contextual semantic information from the API call sequences, resulting in improved recognition and classification performance, as well as higher training efficiency. Experiments show that our model achieves higher classification accuracy than traditional models, with an accuracy increase of 2.0% to 5.6% compared to standalone CNN or LSTM models, and an improvement of 0.4% over conventional transformer models that utilize self-attention mechanisms. The use of the lambda attention mechanism results in approximately a 70% reduction in average training time for the transformer model on our dataset compared to traditional self-attention mechanisms, effectively addressing the issue of prolonged convergence times in traditional models. Additionally, comparisons with methods from other literature validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the approach presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Communication Adaptive Multi-Task Coupled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Despite the impressive success achieved in various domains, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is still faced with the problem of incomplete information and how to deal with complex decision-making tasks with multi-task coupled. The information fusion algorithm ensures the consistency of the global state information by integrating local information to cope with information loss and communication interruption. The majority of prior work only considers the fusion prediction of single state information, while the continuously changing state information in real scenarios is relatively unexplored. Furthermore, traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms can only handle a single task, leaving open the important question of how to adapt to complex scenarios with multiple subtasks coupled. This paper proposes a novel framework called CAMM (Communication Adaptive Multi-Task Coupled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework) to solve the above problems. CAMM provides a distributed fusion prediction method for continuously changing state information to obtain a unified global state for each agent, which leverages the continuity of state changes. CAMM designs a multi-task coupled multi-agent hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, which makes it feasible to decouple complex decision-making tasks into separate decision solutions for each task. As a result, CAMM can be easily combined with existing MARL algorithms and any feasible solution algorithm for each task. Experimental results show that CAMM significantly predicts and fuses state information, ensures the consistency of global state, and achieves comparable performance with the best solution in each subtask in multi-task decision-making environments.

articleTitle: Enhanced Grid Map Correction Using an Improved ORB Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of grid map accuracy errors in multi-map merging, focusing on developing a robust and consistent occupancy grid map. To enhance feature point detection, the oFAST algorithm usingadaptive thresholding is proposed, which amplifies edge responses and increases detection accuracy. Additionally, descriptors derived from local self-correlation matrices are integrated into the BRIEF algorithm to improve robustness in complex environments. Matched feature points are refined using a K-Nearest Neighbors strategy combined with distance threshold filtering, followed by RANSAC-based estimation of the homography matrix to further ensure matching precision. A correction algorithm is proposed, which adjusts the coordinates of the matched feature points and fits a correction curve, thereby refining the pixel structure of the entire grid map. The proposed algorithm is validated by experimental data.

articleTitle: A Digital and Intelligent Design Paradigm for Exhibition Space based on Knowledge Graph & Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper addresses the deficiencies in traditional design methods for exhibition spaces, particularly in terms of efficiency, customization, iterative speed, and design cycles. Specifically, it highlights the issues with the emerging digitalized design methods based on Generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI), such as non-standard and unstructured input expressions, high inconsistency in output results, and low repeatability. By utilizing the Knowledge Graph (KG) to achieve accurate semantic representation and orderly contextual association, as well as structured and standardized expression, this study explores and establishes a KG-genAI-based paradigm for the digital and intelligent design of exhibition spaces (KG-genAI-PDIDES). This paradigm drives Midjourney and Stable through unstructured natural language prompting methods for the digital design of UAV exhibition spaces. Comparative analysis of the results demonstrates that the proposed KG-genAI-PDIDES significantly enhances the standardization of input expression and consistency of output results, offering a new design paradigm for the digitization of exhibition spaces.

articleTitle: Energy-Aware Distributed Sliding Mode Control for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Vehicle platooning, powered by Connected and Automated Vehicle (CAV) technologies, offers significant potential for improving transportation efficiency, enhancing road safety, and reducing fuel consumption. This paper addresses the control challenges of heterogeneous vehicle platoons, with the objective of optimizing fuel efficiency while maintaining system stability and the desired inter-vehicle spacing. An enhanced Energy-Aware Distributed Sliding Mode Control (E-DSMC) framework is proposed, integrating the nonlinear dynamics of vehicles within the platoon and their communication topology. The E-DSMC framework introduces a fuel optimization strategy by developing sliding surfaces and reaching laws aimed at minimizing fuel consumption through the regulation of vehicle acceleration. This approach ensures system stability and robustness under various operating conditions—an aspect often overlooked in conventional control methods. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating that the improved E-DSMC framework outperforms traditional PID control in terms of fuel efficiency and platoon stability, reducing fuel consumption while ensuring the safety and operational efficiency of the platoon.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Hybrid Human-Computer Interaction Strategy Based on Online Classification of Motor Imagery and Eye Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: As China’s manned space programs develop, space tasks such as online maintenance, assembly, and adjustment have become increasingly complex and challenging. Astronauts need to interact with the operation interface via portable wearable devices and cooperate with space manipulators to complete the operation tasks. A hybrid human-computer interaction (HCI) system is therefore proposed here based on electroencephalogram (EEG) and eye movement signals, which resolves the "King Midas problem" in the single eye movement interaction mode and facilitate the space manipulator to fulfill tasks. The proposed strategy uses eye movement fixation and instance segmentation to recognize and select operation objects, and employs online decision-making based on motor imagery EEG signals to send interaction instructions, match with task library, and start execution as per the predefined trajectories and tasks. The user selects the region of interest and objects in the interface through eyeball fixation behavior, collects EEG signals synchronously, and makes online classification decision based on characteristic Gaussian enhancement and adaptive dynamic window length (CGDW). Compared with the previous front-end replication with dynamic time window (FRDW) method, our new method has an improved information transfer rate (ITR) and can enable better interaction. In the new method, visual feedback and manipulator state parameter is provided through real-time 3D simulation from the slave, thus avoiding simple feedback loops. Experiments show that the new strategy significantly has significantly reduced the overall interaction time, and surveys demonstrate that the new method achieves higher physical comfort, which verifies the high efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Open-set image segmentation based on an improved Segment Anything model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Image segmentation is crucial in computer vision, but traditional approaches are limited by dataset and label diversity. Segment Anything introduces open-set segmentation capabilities but struggles with clause-level prompts and precise mask edges. This paper presents SAM-TP, a new algorithm combining Grounding DINO for clause-level prompt handling and Segment Anything for segmentation. By integrating non-maximum suppression and connected component denoising, we refine segmentation accuracy. Additionally, incorporating ViT-Matte enhances edge precision through a trimap-based structure. Experiments on the COCO2017 dataset show that SAM-TP improves Mean Pixel Accuracy by 6.04%, achieving 24.74%, demonstrating its enhanced foreground-background segmentation ability.

articleTitle: Efficient Collaborative Perception with Adaptive Communication in Bandwidth-Constrained Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In autonomous driving, collaborative perception significantly improves safety by addressing occlusions and expanding the perceptual range of individual vehicles. Nevertheless, effectively exchanging data among vehicles under bandwidth constraints presents a major challenge, especially regarding adaptive communication strategies. To tackle this, we introduce Adacomm (Adaptive Communication for Collaborative Multi-agent Perception), a network-adaptive framework that enhances multi-agent collaborative perception by optimizing data exchange to improve perception accuracy and reduce communication costs. The Adacomm framework consists of modular operations such as blind spot identification, multi-scale feature generation, data scheduling optimization, shared message fusion, and detection decoding. Experimental results demonstrate that Adacomm enhances multi-vehicle perception by 16.8% in AP@IoU=0.5, compared to traditional single-vehicle perception, and lowers average communication costs by 29.5% relative to the existing Where2comm method, with a minimal performance decline of 5.6%. Our analysis across different feature layers indicates a trade-off between communication volume and perception accuracy, with medium-resolution features providing a balanced solution. Overall, Adacomm effectively addresses critical challenges in collaborative perception, showing substantial benefits and advancements in scenarios with limited communication resources.

articleTitle: Research on The Application of Object Detection and Tracking Technology in Abnormal Event Detection on Highways
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Real-time detection of abnormal events on highways, such as pedestrian intrusion, abnormal vehicle parking, and vehicle converse running, is one of the crucial measures for reducing traffic accidents on highways. However, the current method of detecting abnormal events on highways based on manual inspection of surveillance videos is beset with high costs and high rates of missed detections. With the advancement of deep learning and computer vision technology, abnormal events detection method for highways based on object detection and tracking technology has been proposed, but it still faces the challenge of low detection accuracy and poor application effects in real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a three-stage based pedestrian intrusion detection method for highways, which achieves a precision of 96.8% and a recall rate of 99.69% in highway scenes. In terms of abnormal vehicle behavior detection on highways, a vehicle tracking algorithm A-BoT-SORT is proposed by introducing the feature detection description algorithm AKAZE based on BoT-SORT algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed A-BoT-SORT algorithm has higher accuracy compared with BoT-SORT algorithm.

articleTitle: PRBJE: A Novel Pre-Relation Bidirectional Joint Extraction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Joint extraction of entities and their semantic relationships to form factual triples from unstructured text is a fundamental task in information extraction. However, existing methods either ignore the interactions between relationships and entities or extract the subjects and objects in a fixed sequential order, which makes these approaches too sensitive to the extraction results of subjects. To address the two issues, we propose a pre-relation bidirectional joint extraction model (PRBJE). Specifically, we first detect potential relationships from the sentence to assist in the subsequent extraction of head and tail entities. Then, we extract all possible entity pairs maintained in the text using two complementary directions: extracting the tail entity based on the head entity and vice versa. Finally, we assign relationships to all entity pairs by a biaffine model, thereby forming complete relational triples. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with improved F1 scores across four public datasets, particularly achieving gains of 0.9 and 0.7 on NYT and WebNLG, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of tourism interpretation system based on intelligent light control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The emergence of smart tourism, propelled by the advancement of new-generation information technologies such as 5G, cloud computing, big data, and artificial intelligence (AI), has instigated transformative shifts in the tourism industry. This evolution has disrupted conventional marketing paradigms and heralded a new era for tourism. Smart optical technology has injected fresh momentum into the progression of tourism and facilitated significant advancements in smart tourism. This study explores a tourism interpretation system based on visible light communication (VLC). By harnessing variations in LED light sources, this system achieves automatic interpretation functions to offer users services including text, audio guidance, and intelligent navigation. These features enrich immersive experiences and cater to tourists’ individual needs. The intelligent light control tour guide system enhances the intelligence and interactivity of the tour, effectively showcasing the characteristics and value of tourism resources, while also fulfilling its educational function of interpretation.

articleTitle: Research on Stereo Vision Localization Method Based on Prior Semantic Map
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: In fields such as intelligent robotics and autonomous driving, visual localization is a fundamental and crucial problem. During long-term operation, the absence of loop closure or prior constraints inevitably leads to accumulated errors. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel visual localization method that integrates prior semantic maps. The method obtains local depth maps using stereo disparity and performs semantic segmentation on RGB images. The segmented images are aligned with the depth maps, and semantic information is mapped onto the depth maps to generate 3D semantic point clouds. After visual odometry initialization, the method employs the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm to align visual point clouds with prior map point clouds using invariant semantic information, resulting in more accurate camera poses. This method has the following advantages: By selecting only fixed and invariant objects for registration, the system demonstrates strong robustness against environmental changes while relying solely on low-cost, lightweight camera sensors to complete the tracking task, significantly reducing the overall system cost. Experiments conducted in real-world scenarios validate that this method can estimate camera pose more accurately than visual odometry.

articleTitle: A transfer-based adversarial attack method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Deep convolutional neural network models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, which can lead to incorrect classification by the model. This adversarial attack has become one of the challenges facing the full-scale deployment of artificial intelligence. Examining adversarial attacks, especially in image recognition, is beneficial. It not only uncovers the weaknesses of deep convolutional neural networks but also enhances our understanding of the security threats associated with deep neural networks, thereby facilitating their enhancement. Through an indepth analysis of the principles behind adversarial attacks, this paper proposes an adversarial attack algorithm aimed at target recognition models.One of the key challenges with current adversarial attack methodologies is their limited ability to produce adversarial examples that can be consistently effective across different models. The generation of such universally effective adversarial samples is a significant hurdle. Nonetheless, achieving this transferability is essential for assessing and bolstering the resilience of AI models against potential security threats. Therefore,this paper introduces a novel adversarial attack algorithm called AdvGAN-G Attack, building on the research surrounding adversarial attack methods that utilize Adversarial Generative Networks (AdvGAN). By utilizing the AdvGAN adversarial training principle and combining the conversion of sample space domain and frequency domain, the gradient editing mechanism is used to optimize the generator gradient parameters in the AdvGAN model, thereby generating adversarial samples with high transferability. Finally, by comparing the performance of AdvGAN-G Attack with other adversarial attack algorithms with transferability, the advantages of AdvGAN-G Attack in terms of sample transferability and algorithm runtime cost were verified, providing an effective solution for improving model robustness and addressing adversarial attack challenges.

articleTitle: Superpixel Edge Refinement and Differential Feature Enhancement for Transformer-Based Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Change detection in remote sensing images is a challenging task, particularly when identifying small and complex objects such as buildings. The task is often hindered by issues such as high fragmentation rates, blurred edges, and elevated false and missed detection rates. These issues arise due to the inherent complexity of the scenes and the problem of class imbalance. To address these challenges, we propose a superpixel edge refinement and differential feature enhancement for Transformer-based change detection networks. First, a region-enhanced Transformer encoder is introduced, incorporating a superpixel edge refinement module. This module leverages pixel-level features extracted by the Transformer to generate superpixel feature embeddings, thereby enhancing local and edge information. Second, a differential feature enhancement module is designed to emphasize true change regions while suppressing pseudo-change areas. This is achieved through a dual-branch structure comprising feature enhancement and change extraction, further augmented by a saliency module. Finally, a Dice loss function is employed as an auxiliary loss term, complementing the cross-entropy loss in the construction of an edge-optimized loss function. The resulting loss function aims to balance overall detection accuracy with edge refinement. The proposed algorithm was evaluated on the widely used datasets LEVIR-CD and DSIFN-CD. Compared to existing algorithms, the proposed method effectively improved edge detail and overall consistency while maintaining detection accuracy. Additionally, false detections and missed detections were reduced.

articleTitle: Distributed Fusion Estimation for Nonlinear Systems under Denial-of-Service Attacks using the Try-Once-Discard Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of distributed state fusion estimation in nonlinear, time-varying systems subjected to external denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. Given the susceptibility of network channels to such attacks, a transmission strategy employing the try-once-discard (TOD) protocol was introduced to reduce their impact. In this approach, each sensor in the network is linked to local estimators through multiple channels, with the TOD protocol determining the transmission priority. Data transmitted via the highest priority channel is retained, while data from other channels are discarded. A local estimator was constructed using the cubature Kalman filter (CKF), and a consensus-based approach was utilized to merge the local estimates, forming a distributed fusion estimation algorithm. The algorithm’s convergence was analyzed, and sufficient conditions for maintaining bounded filter error covariance were established, accounting for network disruptions and random nonlinearity. The proposed algorithm’s performance was demonstrated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Error evaluation for RSINS errors based on covariance analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Rotational strapdown technology is an error self-compensation technique that utilizes the periodic rotation of an inertial measurement unit (IMU) to modulate the errors of inertial components and improve the long-term accuracy of an inertial navigation system (INS). A new method for evaluating the rotational modulation effect of the transposition scheme is proposed to address the problem of tedious analysis and calculation process. It combines the covariance analysis of Kalman filter time update and the error propagation characteristics of open-loop strapdown inertial navigation. Through numerical simulation calculation, all inertial device error factors, including zero bias error and installation error matrix of gyroscope and accelerometer, are accurately separated and given. The implementation process is simple and easy to promote. The new method can also be used to assist in optimizing the design of transposition schemes.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Quality Weight Adjustment-Based Multi-source Fusion Method for Precipitation Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: Accurate precipitation forecasting plays a pivotal role in weather forecasting and disaster management. This study introduces a novel approach, the Dynamic Quality Weighting Multi-source Fusion Method, designed for precipitation forecasting by leveraging a Transformer-based architecture. The proposed model integrates multi-source precipitation data, including radar echo and satellite infrared imagery, to effectively capture spatiotemporal dependencies and cross-modal interactions. In order to enhance the robustness to noise and missing data, a dynamic quality weighting mechanism is added to the fusion module part, which dynamically adjusts the contribution of data of each source according to the forecasting confidence of precipitation data from different sources. Experiments were conducted on the MeteoNet public dataset, focusing on forecasting radar echo maps for the subsequent six hours using observations from the preceding six hours. The results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses state-of-the-art models, including ConvLSTM, PredRNN, and SimVP, in terms of both forecasting accuracy and the structural consistency of precipitation patterns. This study underscores the potential of dynamic quality weighting and Transformer-based architectures to advance precipitation forecasting and multi-source data fusion methodologies.

articleTitle: Intelligent Recognition and Integrated Navigation Technology for Typical Spacecraft Components
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: The demand for on-orbit services—like autonomous spacecraft assembly, on-orbit maintenance, and logistical support—is growing as technology develops. Common spacecraft parts and navigation algorithms form the foundation for the previously described on-orbit services. Due to the influence of light intensity, imaging quality, and spatial interference, standard approaches and deep learning algorithms for spacecraft component identification and localization still require improvement in terms of accuracy and stability.
