To address these issues, two contributions are made: firstly, the information of three-dimensional point clouds is integrated, based on the application of deep learning algorithms to identify spacecraft targets in low light. Second, to guarantee that highprecision navigation information is supplied autonomously, in real-time, and constantly throughout spacecraft operation, a plug-and-play fusion navigation technique for vision/LIDAR heterogeneous sensitive devices is created based on the factor graph architecture. The work in this paper simplifies the computational resources compared to deep learning algorithms that directly use 3D point cloud recognition and enables the accuracy and stability of spacecraft component recognition and navigation under low light to be improved. In addition, it also improves the implementability of the algorithm in practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Privacy-Preserving Scheme to Support Dual-agent Selection in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of IoT technology, smart grid, as one of its core applications, is gradually realising the intelligent management of the power system. The popularity of smart meters and other devices enables the grid to monitor power consumption in real time, providing a large amount of data support for grid operations. However, the privacy sensitivity of these data is extremely high, and how to effectively protect user privacy has become an important challenge for the development of smart grid. To address this problem, this paper proposes a privacy-preserving data aggregation scheme based on proxy reencryption, which aims to ensure the privacy and security of user data without sacrificing data utility. The secure collection and processing of data is achieved by constructing a multi-layer system model containing a trusted centre, a control centre, a fog node and a smart meter. It enables the data to complete aggregation and conversion in an encrypted state, effectively preventing unauthorised access and data leakage. At the same time, the solution supports bidirectional selective aggregation, allowing the system to flexibly perform data aggregation operations according to demand, improving system applicability and efficiency. Security analysis and performance evaluation show that the scheme proposed in this paper is effective in protecting user privacy and system security.

articleTitle: Research on GNSS spoofing detection method based on tracking loop moving average processing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: A spoofing detection algorithm based on Tracking Loop Correlation Output (TLCO) is proposed to address the issues of limited applicability and significant fluctuations in detection performance of traditional detection algorithms. To suppress noise, the TLCO Moving Average (TLCO-MA) detection algorithm is further proposed. The construction of TCCO-MA uses the output of correlators to multiply and linearly weight the TLCO detection metric, and uses skewness and kurtosis to jointly verify its approximate normality. Then, the TLCO is subjected to MA filtering to obtain the TLCO-MA detection metric. Conduct spoofing detection experiments using DS2, DS3, and DS5 from the TEXBAT database of the University of Texas, and analyze the detection performance of the proposed algorithm and traditional SQM algorithms in multiple scenarios, including detection probability, sensitivity, immediacy, detection range, and robustness. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional SQM algorithm, TLCO-MA has better detection performance and a wider range of applicable scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction of Thick-Film Resistor Values Using Genetic Algorithm-Optimized Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a neural network model optimized using a genetic algorithm to predict the resistance of thick-film resistors. Thick-film resistors are essential electronic components with significant industrial applications. However, achieving the target resistance often requires multiple process adjustments during production, resulting in low efficiency. The manufacturing process involves numerous steps and parameters, with resistance being closely tied to these variables. To address this issue, the proposed model predicts resistance directly from production process parameters, effectively enhancing efficiency. By integrating production practices and constraints, the method achieves an average prediction deviation as low as 1.198%. Additionally, the neural network analysis identifies key process parameters influencing resistance, offering targeted guidance for process optimization.
